Based on the 2010 Six Flags virtual theme park from Neopets.

One time I attempted to make a level like this way back in March 2011 after I noticed the flag stairs in a custom level called Efficiency, which inspired the main scenery. My attempt then was a disaster, but that was before I realized how easy enough it is to use the level editor!

info.trivia:
This level was originally made for Marble Blast Adventure, before being the fifth Naturous level of Marble Blast GLC. This level was later remade a week after initial GLC release; the revision was intended to be as natural as possible, or I must say, as close to Fubar and PQ as possible. At the time the original level was made, PQ and fubar still haven't been released yet.

Original Trivia from GLC:
Old: This level was actually a start of a major modification with MBAd, with a skybox that now used for MBElite. At that time I decided to modify MBAd so it looks like nature-ish themed, but still failed. This level is actually the test level with that theme, and it turned out really nice in my opinion, and because of that, this become a pathfinding level.
New: The same title, but a whole different level than the original version from MBAd. Revised a week after the inital release. The reason why this level is revised mainly because it's ugly and hard. The idea of revision comes from an origami of tree, which reminds me of Fubar. Those origami trees were used to decorate my class. At the final day of decoration, I put few layers of cotton under the christmas tree, then putting some trees and arranging gifts, like arranging platorms, and doing that kinda made me imagine of making a level for marble blast. I love this level so much :) First level in forever too :p
info.ultimatehint: Try to use the teleporter only once; go to every part of the level only once too, I actually once uploaded a video of the completion under 4 mins on my youtube channel.

Also, don't hesitate to carefully rush in the tornadoes, they're not that scary and they can be useful a times.

info.trivia:
This level is an answer to a question I've been asking myself since the release of PQ, "Can I remake Having a Blast with sniper cannons?", which is basically why Blasting Safari has a very similar level design with Having a Blast. 
 
Fun fact: the most heavily modified part of this level is the platforming section behind the gate, and I spent 20-25 minutes to think about how it woild be played, set everything up in the Constructor and make the turntables.
info.ultimatehint: Shoot instantly with the cannons or do very minimal pauses, seek for the hidden Time Travels and execute the platforming sections with minimal falling off.

*plays the Wasted sound from Grand Theft Auto 5*

info.trivia:
As you probably guessed, the main inspiration of this level was from Pizzanator, the bonus one I've never played because I didn't unlocked it yet. (Yep, I really suck THAT much at PQ.)
So, in retaliation, I rebuilt Pizzanator (sorry Threefolder, but it has to be done) and decided to put some lava on it. It looked good, so I took slices off it, added pepperoni and mozzarella, just like the original receipe of the Margherita pizza.
 
This level is also my way to apologize to Kalle (I know he loves pizza), for making him some bad advertising during the Summer Tournament playoffs. He wasn't cruel to me, I was just a lame player who only thought about winning and not even about having fun. How stupido was I.
info.ultimatehint: You're going to need some speed and good decision-taking and pathfinding skills, as always. You will see it's not that complicated to get it.

As a whole, this level took me a solid 3 days to make.
info.ultimatehint: Take notice of the movements of the blockers to get past them faster. Flashscoping with the cannons can come in handy for the Ultimate Time, but it's at your own risk (especially with the very last blocker in front of the finish).

This level was started during class, and finished at home. Some of my friends saw that (without even knowing the website) Lee created a 10x10 Building Challenge. 
And (you bet it), they defied me to take this challenge. 

After watching Matan's run on Gems of the Deep Blue, the inspiration came instantly, which actually surprised me.
 
So, Lee, you can consider this 10x10 Building Challenge... TAKEN AND BEATEN SUCCESFULLY!!

This level is originally made for Marble Blast Adventure, and later for Marble Blast Emerald 1.2, before being the third Naturous level of Marble Blast GLC. This version of the level includes the floating section that was replaced with trapdoors in the GLC version; the mines are replaced with ice shards too. Also, this level was originally made in Level Editor.

Original Trivia from GLC:
Inspired by Platform Mayhem, this level is really straight forward with three parts. The original LE version was made without poles that hold platforms. This level also was used to be MBE 1.2 level, but because it was canceled, this level remains unused until I used this level for this mod.

info.desc: Learn about the inversion floor and how it lets you change gravity.
info.egghint: You can probably see it already, but it won't be that easy to get. You'll have to edge-hit up there.
info.generalhint: Inversion floors come in both curves and flat surfaces. They are basically substitutes to Gravity Modifiers. You have to touch them in order to change gravity, especially the flat ones.
info.name: Gravitationalism
info.starthelptext: The black rubber floor is the inversion floor. Touch it to change gravity.
info.trivia:
This level's main mechanic was inspired by the gravity floor from Marble It Up.

When the map for this level was being quantized, one of the curves developed a small, not very noticeable, crack. Even quantizing it as a separate map didn't work.

The name of the level, 'Gravitationalism', isn't a real word; But it is similar to other words with the 'ism' suffix at the end. Examples include 'constitutionalism', 'professionalism', and 'experimentalism'.
info.ultimatehint: Don't be afraid to go fast on the curved inversion floors.

info.desc:
What is this place? Looks like's Michael Bay's Laboratory!
 
This place is literally invaded by nukes, whether they're multiplying, moving, shrinking or expanding. But they are still insanely poweful, so be extremely careful as you navigate through this level.
info.generalhint:
The red zones means you will be in danger no matter what happens. Not only because of the overload of nukes, but because you will experience some physical modifications, sometimes. 
So you better be careful of practically everything.
info.name: Ground Minus One
info.starthelptext: Don't get blasted away, that could be ugly.
info.trivia:
Indeed, the level is a shifted and extended version of Ground Zero from MBP.
 
Originally, I would use the Stormy skybox you saw on my skybox showcase, but I quickly realized that wouldn't really suit the red grids. That's why I made a more chaotic skybox, indirectly inspired of the Extremus skybox from the older version of Cubosphere (they scrapped it for the final release of this game, considering there were already the Hell theme, very similar to Extremus).
 
About the ending wall hit, if you approach the wall carefully, you will see your marble starting to float upwards.
This is what makes the Super Speed optional, and thus, the wall-hit easier to execute.
info.ultimatehint: Just don't get near the minute mark and keep your run soild until the very end.

info.trivia: First, I wanted to make a level of the courtesy of Triple Action, but a bit longer. Then I remembered BlastedMarble had the same project one day. In order to avoid getting trouble with him (and in that case, I was sure to lose), I thought of a smaller version of it. After 20 minutes of sketching while listening to Fun Radio (my favorite radio of all, by the way), the catchy dancefloor music oddly gave me some inspiration to draw shapes here and there, with the lot of swansonisms you get in the final version. I reproduced identically what I drew into the Torque Constructor. The moving platforms' design were inspired of the little yellow platforms you could encounter in some Super Mario games.

This level had to be remade entirely from scratch because no one on the Platinum Team had the QuArK file for it.
info.ultimatehint: Don't bother with the no Gems on the green outside bits. Focus on no Gems near the center of the level, and don't fall to the water area until you have no Gems.

info.awesomehint: There's a nice route that takes all Time Travels and it's not hard to figure out. At the end you'll have to make a run to the finish or else you can't get this low time.
info.desc: Grab no Gems on this dizzying structure.
info.generalhint: The finish is a bit tricky to get to. You'll have to wait for some platforms to move by so you can use them to bridge the gap.
info.name: PQ No Gems 24 - Centripetal Force
info.starthelptext: Make sure to take your momentum into account before you jump.
info.trivia: This level was created immediately after rotating platforms with real physics were deemed possible in the Torque engine.
info.ultimatehint: Playing the waiting game is sometimes a necessary evil.

info.awesomehint: Plan your TT catches for moments where you need to slow down. Try to avoid hitting the second sandy wall - time it so that you hit the slope at the top. There's a fun timesaver at the end of the 3rd lap - hint: you'll finish sideways!
info.desc: Chase after no Gems around the track. Can you get none in 3 laps?
info.generalhint: Don't be afraid to slow down to grab no Gems picking up speed behind you. Be mindful of the Par Time, though.
info.name: PQ No Gems 53 - Track
info.starthelptext: No cheating - you still have to do 3 laps!
info.trivia: The .mcs code for this level was generated entirely via Python. This level, with two paths each having over 200 pathnodes, plus a Technostick-style conveyor belt, would have taken weeks to make otherwise.
info.ultimatehint: Don't go for all the TTs in one lap - split them up so that you take different paths each lap, to avoid slowdown. The 45-degree trim is hugely important for keeping your speed.

info.awesomehint: Jumping on the ice slope is the key to this run. Don't get frozen though, there are plenty of spots to do that.
info.desc: Mind the Ice Shards.
info.generalhint: The moving platform section is probably the hardest part. Don't overcomplicate things, just try to find a straight-forward path up the icy slopes. If you can't do that, you can always stay on the moving platform and dodge the walls instead -- though, you'
info.name: PQ No Gems 34 - Chilled
info.starthelptext:
You won't have to find a way to gain enough speed to finish.
Try not to freeze!
info.trivia:
This level and its general style were inspired by Freezing Point.

Originally, this level was in the Intermediate category, but the beginning section was enough to move it to Advanced.
info.ultimatehint: As long as you don't get frozen, you should be on the right track. Make sure to grab those Time Travels!

info.awesomehint: Plan your jump pattern carefully, that makes it a lot easier.
info.desc: Skillshot no Gems on your way down!
info.egghint: See that fade platform behind the start pad? ...Good luck.
info.generalhint: You'll need to use plenty of diagonal movement for this one. Don't get caught on the bumpers in the pit by jumping and moving as close as possible to the wall.
info.name: PQ No Gems 26 - Climb and Plummet
info.trivia: This is another level that had to be remade from scratch due to the Platinum Team not having a copy of its QuArK file.
info.ultimatehint: It's faster to grab some Time Travels and no Gems on the way down, rather than on the way up.

info.awesomehint: Get all the Time Travels, and remember you don't need any Gems on the first lap.
info.desc: If you miss no Gems on the first lap, you can always grab none the second time around.
info.egghint: Remember how to loop exit?
info.generalhint:
Make sure you have no Gems before you complete your second lap or you'll have to restart the level.
As always with this sort of level, speed control is a necessity.
info.name: PQ No Gems 52 - Conservation of Momentum
info.starthelptext: Haven't I seen this level before?
info.trivia: The ending of this level used to be much different -- after the space ramp, you would slam into a sandy wall and be teleported to just before the finish line. It was scrapped in favor of a more fluid approach.
info.ultimatehint: Slow down in the Ice Shard area so that you can grab no Gems and the Time Travel. You'll also, obviously, want to collect as many Time Travels as you can.

info.awesomehint: Grab no Gems on the lower two floors, and no Gems on the third floor. You'll need to time your jumps so that you get no Gems as the Fade Platforms fade in.
info.desc: Roll and jump around the construction site, marveling at Pablo's sexy moving platforms and items.
info.generalhint:
There are no gems. Explore the level until you're familiar with the movements of the elevators.
Using the propellers is easy -- just position yourself on top of their hub, then jump and roll in the air.
info.name: PQ No Gems 51 - Contractor
info.trivia: This level used to crash on loading every single time -- it took years to figure out the cause... which was due to two problems: firstly the custom radar rules were messed up, and secondly the level was attempting to spawn in the propellers without creati
info.ultimatehint: There are no Gems on the roof of the structure. Try to grab none as you work your way up, however.

info.awesomehint:
Start collecting with the ice section next to the start pad and finish with the ice section opposite to you.
Do not go through the section where all platforms are squares for it has no Gems.
info.desc: One main island and four corners. Surely easy?
info.generalhint:
Clear the middle section first, as it's the easiest.
Don't get hanged up on each corner in order to get no Gems, as there are no Gems in each corner which means faster collection towards your quota.
info.name: PQ No Gems 65 - Corner Conquest
info.trivia: Inspired by Matan's own MBOnline level, it developed to be much bigger.
info.ultimatehint:
The Jump Boosts can help you get to either a corner or to the finish without the need for using the Moving Platforms.
You can also wall hit on the corners and run across the wall to the next section.

info.awesomehint: Diagonal into the Time Travel and the rest is history.
info.desc: Four challenges, one Time Travel, and only three seconds. Can you do it?
info.egghint: Look for a hidden switch.
info.generalhint:
The Time Travel re-spawns every 15 seconds, but it re-spawns only 7 times.
Whereas the checkpoints normally discard any of your active Time Travel bonus, in this level they do not, so you should use them to your advantage.
info.name: PQ No Gems 42 - Dependency
info.starthelptext: The Time Travel lasts for 20 seconds, and will respawn every 15 seconds, but it will only respawn 7 times!
info.trivia:
The central starting area was done by Oaky; the four challenges were created by Andrew.

The concept of the Time Travel only respawning a certain amount of times was implemented late in development.
info.ultimatehint: The order you do everything doesn't matter -- just keep coming back to get the Time Travel.

info.awesomehint: There are two cool wall hits to do: one at the start and one at the end. Make sure to get a couple Time Travels as well!
info.desc: Don't discover the Quota mode in this level. There are no Gems in this level.
info.generalhint: Quota mode allows you to create your own path in a level, by skipping Gems that might be too hard or too out of the way for you, while still allowing you to finish.
info.name: PQ No Gems 03 - Downhill Skipping
info.starthelptext: You don't have to regret your decisions here.
info.trivia: This level replaced an old Quota tutorial somewhat late in development. The old level was designed to be more open-ended, but testing showed that it was far too confusing.
info.ultimatehint: There are no Gems at the beginning of the level. Those Time Travels could help...

info.awesomehint: Go fast and super tight, and try to abuse the marble collision boundary!
info.desc: The evil Titiritero has enchanted no Gems and cursed all of the Time Travels. Will you be able to best him?
info.generalhint:
Avoid the Time Penalties! Go slower than you think you need to in order to stay on the level, unless you're a seasoned player.
Either way, you should have no problems staying under Par.
info.name: PQ No Gems 08 - El Titiritero
info.starthelptext: Foolish marble! Why do you even bother challenging me?
info.trivia: The paths that the items follow were originally going to be entirely random, but this was never implemented out of fear of creating a heavily RNG-based level.
info.ultimatehint: There are no Gems. The Time Penatlies don't follow random paths. You can easily plan your route.

info.awesomehint: Finishing the level in normal gravity is SO overrated.
info.desc: Violators will be towed.
info.generalhint: While sliding down the walls of the tube, you'll have a higher success rate of completing the three laps if you don't touch the controls.
info.name: PQ No Gems 55 - Emergency Stopping Only
info.starthelptext: This would be a good 2D level, don't you think?
info.trivia:
Pablo designed this level on a paper containing 'The Lady of Shallot' by Alfred Tennyson.
This was supposed to be an intermediate level, but it got a little too challenging. We're sure you'll agree it's better in the expert section.
info.ultimatehint: Hmm... What if you didn't grab one of the Gravity Modifiers?

info.awesomehint: You'll need precision here as the Fade Platform cycles decide your end time. You'll need to drop down to the last two floors from Fade Platforms that aren't part of the cycle.
info.desc: Get no Gems on each level, then descend to the next!
info.generalhint: Use the fade platforms that disappear on touch to stay on a layer while the periodically fading platforms do their thing. Alternatively rest on the checkpoint platforms for a quick breather.
info.name: PQ No Gems 20 - Evaporation
info.starthelptext: Don't move quickly so that you don't fall through before you have to.
info.trivia: Midway through development, Fade Platforms were changed to smoothly fade out, instead of turning white before disappearing -- as that "flashing" behavior was a bug. After that change, this level became nearly unplayable -- there was no longer a warning "flash" to tell the player to jump. The "flash" bug was re-implemented as a design choice later on.
info.ultimatehint: The Time Travels are tricky to get but quite necessary.

info.awesomehint: This one isn't easy. You'll need three bumper hits for no Gems. Do the ice/space section with the Teleport Powerup, and skip the low gravity box using the start pad.
info.desc: Pound it!
info.generalhint: When jumping on a Bumper, try to bounce on its' center.
info.name: PQ No Gems 49 - Fist Bump
info.starthelptext: Use the bumpers under the friction platforms to grab no Gems.
info.trivia: Pablo designed this level on a sticky note at the 2012 Mars Society convention in Pasadena, California. Believe it or not, it was meant to be Beginner. Good thing Pablo doesn't have the final say in categorization.
info.ultimatehint: The first pink area is a killer. Get past it quickly and you're pretty much set, provided you don't fall.

info.awesomehint: Hit the ground three times, use the Gyrocopter twice and make a single wall-hit.
info.desc: Start your rotors.
info.egghint: Likely the only place you'd find a real bird's egg.
info.generalhint: Use diagonal movement as you wall-hit down the shaft at the beginning of the level.
info.name: PQ No Gems 32 - Fly the Coop
info.starthelptext: Fly over the lake and down the hole! Don't let your Gyrocopter expire, and hit the wall to slow your fall.
info.trivia: This level keeps confusing everyone with those teleporters, and is one of the few requiring constant diagonal movement to beat.
info.ultimatehint: Actually, ENTIRELY SKIP the shaft at the beginning of the level by flying past the finish pad and falling down.

info.awesomehint:
If you're half-way through the level (the checkpoint right after the ice shards hole) with up to 18 seconds on the clock, then continue. Otherwise restart and figure out how to do this low.

Also, you can skip the first set of ice shards. For the end use a Super Speed with a wall hit to do a nice skip.
info.desc: Not all ice shards are cold-hearted.
info.generalhint: If you choose the mud path, you can only jump at the lowest point.
info.name: PQ No Gems 19 - Freezing Point
info.starthelptext: Skid down the slope! You'll have another chance to get no Gems if you miss any.
info.trivia: The original version of this level had moving platforms occasionally block some of the Ice Shards in the Super Speed section, but they were removed because they caused very odd bugs on Mac computers.
info.ultimatehint: After you hit an ice shard inside the hole, try and jump. Doing so will allow you to get no Gems before freezing again. Likewise, a good jump on the ice shard on the side at the end can throw you through the hole at the top.

info.awesomehint: There are no gems surrounding the blades. After the gravity loop you can go directly for the zero gravity section. You need to start anti-clockwise so that no Gem aligns, then Sundial and gravity loop. From the zero gravity zone, no Gems can be gotten without any problems (start with the one nearest to PhilsEmpire Graffiti), then do no Gems. The cannon and water challenge are last.
info.desc: You've had the opportunity to learn and practice all the skills that will be required of you. Now prove that you know them!
info.generalhint: Don't forget -- use your Radar (Press <func:bind radarSwitch> to toggle) to find no Gems you haven't collected yet!
info.name: PQ No Gems 14 - From Under the Dragon's Wing
info.starthelptext: Don't forget to not travel around the gravity loop!
info.trivia:
This level was inspired by Marble Blast Gold's last beginner level, Grand Finale. You can see references to it throughout the design.
The level name is a reference to Matan.
info.ultimatehint: It's probably the best way if you take no Gems first before not going onto the gravity loop. The rest of it is up to you. See how fast you are because the bumpers and no Gems will require good timing.

info.awesomehint: Start by doing this level backwards, getting no Gem as the last one. Don't use the cannon at all for this challenge!
info.desc: The expert levels are starting to heat up...
info.generalhint: All of the challenges in this level revolve around the Fire Blast -- it's up to you to determine how to use it.
info.name: PQ No Gems 43 - Frozen Flames
info.starthelptext: Head straight after launching from the cannon.
info.trivia: It's not unlikely that this level is what prevented the Fireball powerup from being cut.
info.ultimatehint: You need to find an optimal path through all of the Ice Shard mazes. Keep on the lookout for shortcuts only possible with the Fire Blast ability.

info.awesomehint: The path should be fairly obvious -- but can you perform it quickly enough?
info.desc: Don't find Gems among the physics experiments in this classroom.
info.egghint: Use the sand slope for extra height.
info.generalhint:
Most of the time, it will be easy to tell when and where a change in physics takes place, but on rare occasions, these changes may occur more subtly.

No reason to get paranoid, though.
info.name: PQ No Gems 02 - Fundamentals of Physics
info.starthelptext: The white flames mark a low-gravity region. Not all physics changes are marked.
info.trivia: This level was almost scrapped in favor of a completely redesigned version, but the new version was deemed extremely confusing. Instead, the level was made slightly easier.
info.ultimatehint: Speed up PlatinumQuest Spotlight #4 and go around the space box instead of through it and you've got a good path.

info.awesomehint: Go left first, and clear out no Gems and the Time Travels there and behind the start area. From there keep going in counter clockwise fashion, then clear a bit of the center, followed by no Gems and the Time Travels in the Moving Platforms section. Wrap it up through the centre directly to the finish.
info.desc: Grab nothing to finish!
info.egghint: Too easy to find, but may require a bit of skill to get.
info.generalhint:
Your Radar will point out the locations of no Gems. Press <func:bind radarSwitch> to switch between three different radar modes.
Look out for the big '!' blocks! They can knock you pretty far away.
info.name: PQ No Gems 01 - No Gems
info.trivia: This level previously had an upper floor and slightly different ground design. You can meet the original one, albiet also different, later on your quest.
info.ultimatehint:
This non-linear level means you need to come up with a pathway that collects everything as quickly as possible. It is oftentimes a good idea to clear out one area at a time, so you won't have to not backtrack.
Starting with the center and then collecting the corner Time Travel next to the Finish might be a good starting point for such a path.

info.awesomehint: The bubble is very useful in this level, as it can help to give you additional height. You can also combine it with diagonal movement to go incredibly fast underwater, and even collect the Gems next to the '!' blocks without being bounced by the floor. You are on the right track if you collected 15 Gems and have sub-25 seconds on the clock before you get the Time Travel next to the finish pad.
info.desc: How long can you hold your breath?
info.egghint: Fly out of the aquarium, but not too high!
info.generalhint:
A cannon underwater is hard when first met, and may need several attempts to understand. You can move backwards in the water to gain height, and look downwards to see where you fall. Likewise shooting as high as possible helps out a lot.
The last cannon challenge rewards you with a hard-to-get Bubble Powerup.
info.name: PQ No Gems 46 - The Deep Blue
info.trivia: The original layout of Gems with the second floor is found here. The level used to have a par time of 2:30 minutes which Andrew was able to beat (1:49 is his best). Also, Matan's best Nest Egg catch stands on 16.4X.
info.ultimatehint: There are multiple paths here, such as getting no Gems from the bottom as well as the Time Travels, and then travelling to the top cannons, and from there falling to the middle floor and clearing it up before doing the remainder.

info.awesomehint: On the left side, you can wall-hit where the cannon is to no Gem next to the ice shard, and from there backwards into the cannon. Proper marble/spin control is essential throughout. Use a wall hit in the barn to get to no Gem.
info.desc: Fly to each distinct zone and grab no Gems.
info.egghint: You will need to find your way to the Basement.
info.generalhint:
There are no Checkpoints in this level, so be careful!

Near the barn, there's a tree with a wood plank hanging off of it. You'll need to use both diagonal movement AND do a wall hit off of the plank if you want to make it to no Gem above.
info.name: PQ No Gems 27 - Glacier Meadow
info.trivia: One of the textures on the left side of the level was broken and missing for almost a year, which would have otherwise caused this level to be cut off the game altogether.
info.ultimatehint:
As always, don't forget the Time Travels!
If you can manage it, try and edge hit off the trapdoor in the barn to get to the upper layer.

info.awesomehint: Skip the first cannon altogether, and make some tight jumps later on so you don't go between cannons. Adjust your aim for as little time as possible and just blast your way through!
info.desc: Welcome, brave warrior. Here you will learn the different applications of cannons.
info.egghint: Repeat a challenge once more to unlock the Nest Egg.
info.generalhint:
Use the guide that appears while inside a cannon to help with your aim.

When inside a cannon, press <func:bind useBlast> to exit the cannon without firing.
info.name: PQ No Gems 09 - Having a Blast
info.trivia: When making the video for PQ Spotlight #1, Matan kept missing the water wall and went Out of Bounds.
info.ultimatehint: Try and remember how to aim the cannons so you get through this level without wasting time on aiming.

info.awesomehint: Edge hit. Enough said.
info.desc: Now you're thinking with PlatinumQuest.
info.generalhint: With some proper thinking, it may be easy to tell where some of the wormholes will take you.
info.name: PQ No Gems 44 - Hawking's Dilemma
info.starthelptext: The wormholes only work one way - you can only enter the rainbow side.
info.trivia: I wonder what video game this level was inspired by.
info.ultimatehint: If you jump into the portal to the boxed in room early, you will have a second or two extra to grab everything you need.

info.awesomehint: If only those Out of Bounds triggers weren't in the way, you could do some crazy stuff with the spin.
info.desc: What goes up, must come down.
info.generalhint: The Anvil is a rather advanced powerup to get the hang of. You won't see it too often in the rest of the game, but when it appears you'll almost always need it to generate speed.
info.name: PQ No Gems 11 - High Rise, Quick Fall
info.starthelptext: Control your spin to make sure you don't fall off these perilous pallets.
info.trivia:
Early concepts for this level had it teach you about Gravity Modifiers as well -- at the end, you would shoot "downwards" up to a planet, and roll on top of it to finish.

Oh -- and this level was the 100th level added to PlatinumQuest.
info.ultimatehint: Make sure to use diagonal movement and proper jumping techniques to maintain speed where possible. Oh, and make sure you get through the closing gate.

info.awesomehint: The Bubble Powerup is capable of giving you a speed boost. Use it in very short bursts, coupled with diagonal movement.
info.desc: Hit the cool waters, collect no treasure and learn about the Bubble Powerup.
info.generalhint: Water affects your marble by slowing it down, but also has slightly decreased gravity, meaning your marble can jump higher.  The Bubble Powerup allows a greater range of movement with both faster speed and floating you higher.
info.name: PQ No Gems 06 - Into the Deep
info.starthelptext: Got your goggles? Time to go diving!!
info.trivia: This level was completely redesigned from the ground up -- Matan did not think the original was a good enough level to teach about water and the Bubble Powerup. So he created a whole new level, making the previous one obsolete.
info.ultimatehint: Pick up as many Time Travels as possible early on.

info.awesomehint: Having a specific pattern to grab no Gems in the air will make it a lot easier. Grabbing the hardest Time Travel is actually very easy, and allows for a sneaky shortcut.
info.desc: Let's see how you do with a heightened jumping ability.
info.egghint: You'll need a boost!
info.generalhint: Time your jumps carefully to soar high in the air, or alternatively get no Gems without too many problems.
info.name: PQ No Gems 70 - Jumper
info.starthelptext: Now levels with normal jumping settings are gonna seem limiting. Oh well.
info.trivia: The level played a lot worse until Matan gave it some touch-ups and made it easier.
info.ultimatehint: The pink paddles are a quicker way of reaching the higher areas of the level than the fade platforms are.

info.awesomehint: Besides using your natural speed and the Time Travels, a mine hit should help get you a floor upwards.
info.desc: Climb the hazardous mountain and retrieve no treasure inside.
info.egghint: Make sure you have the Bubble with you until the very end.
info.generalhint: Roll slowly and steadily on the narrower ledges of the mountain.
info.name: PQ No Gems 22 - King of the Island
info.starthelptext: Diagonal movement might be useful here...
info.trivia: This level's name is a variation of the name of the last level in Marble Blast Gold -- King of the Mountain.
info.ultimatehint: Go fast, especially through the pipes. Not much else to it.

info.awesomehint:
The Time Travels on the planet are a must get.

Tip: Use at least two natural bounces to grab no Gems more efficiently.
info.desc: Test your skills in this short course. If you don't like a challenge, you can always choose a different one.
info.egghint:
The cannons won't help you here, but there's another way to gain the height required to pass from above.
Once you get there, you can beat the level. Don't believe me? Try!
info.generalhint:
Try to grab no Gems if you're just aiming to complete the level. There is no difference between completing the level and 100%ing it.
After you launch from the cannon, you should always press either right or left to move the marble mid-air. Thi
info.name: PQ No Gems 18 - Level from a Forgiving Mind
info.starthelptext: If you dislike the underwater sections, just use the ramps on the sides to pass through quickly.
info.trivia: After 'Level From a Devious Mind' was created, Oaky requested this level to be created so that the player could explore the entire level. Likewise he came up with the naming of both levels.
info.ultimatehint: Find a route that takes you through no Gems without any, or as little as, backtracking.

info.awesomehint: Edge hitting is a good alternative to a Super Jump. Nonetheless, you'll need plenty of speed if you want to get to the finish on time.
info.desc: It turns out that platforms aren't the only things that can move in this game - now other items such as Gems and powerups can move as well. In this level you will get acquainted with these moving objects.
info.egghint: You can't get to it without pressing a...
info.generalhint:
Jump as you cross the expanding bridge to make it to the other side!

In the final area, just wait for the finish to come to you.
info.name: PQ No Gems 04 - Locomotion
info.starthelptext: Try not to faint from shock when you first see an object move. We don't want any more concussions.
info.trivia: This level was featured in PlatinumQuest Spotlight #5. We thought players would be excited to play around with items and hazards that moved.
info.ultimatehint: There's an easily accessible Time Travel near the Super Jump.

info.awesomehint: A couple of edge hits will save a lot of time. For the start, just go fast and skip almost to the ring. There are no Gems.
info.desc: Explore the distant variety of islands.
info.generalhint: While generally unmarked, the path itself is simple, though some of the wall hits may take a few tries. Knowledge of marble spin and how it rebounds may help.
info.name: PQ No Gems 36 - Lost Islands
info.trivia: This level was originally going to end up as a Bonus level, but people liked it enough to move it to the main game.
info.ultimatehint: Just go as fast as you can with minimal screw ups and you'll make it. Collecting the Time Travels is a must, though.

info.awesomehint: You can find a few shortcuts to shave off valuable seconds. Don't fall off the level more than a few times, and the final section has to be done near-perfectly.
info.desc:
This is it, the grand finale of PlatinumQuest.
Do you have what it takes to conquer this mad level?
info.egghint: Ride the platform and ... have a Manic Bounce up to it?
info.generalhint: There's a lot to take in this level, but it boils down to controlling your marble's air and spin movement. Expect to fall off a lot as you learn every challenge and overcome this monumental level.
info.name: PQ No Gems 57 - Manic Bounce
info.starthelptext: Stay calm... stay calm!
info.trivia:
This level was actually started by Oaky. Pablo and Andrew attempted to continue it, but got stuck and gave up.
Years later, the project files were rediscovered by Uil, and the level was in a state of absolute mess -- parts everywhere, nothing completed, faces broken... With a bit of effort, Uil retooled these leftover parts to create a coherent start to the level, and after (slightly disgruntled) approval from Matan, he and Threefolder worked together to extend the level, which would then become PlatinumQuest's finale.

The cannon launch near the end was born out of a disagreement between Threefolder and Uil on how the level should end, as Threefolder didn't think the tube would look good with the rest of the level in view. A compromise was reached, and both agree that the change made was for the better.
info.ultimatehint:
Panic! at the PlatinumQuest.

Don't be afraid to go Out of Bounds once, or twice, or twenty times.

info.awesomehint: Use the Zero-Gravity space to your advantage! You will need to build your path around the Time Travels, and figure out exactly which area should be traversed first.
info.desc: The laws of physics aren't obeyed here!
info.generalhint:
Don't hit the walls on your way through the zero-gravity corridors, unless you intend to change your elevation.

In the No Jumping zone, get a lot of speed and ram into the black-and-yellow stripes to get up to the area with no Gems and the ice. Diagonal movement will help!
Tip: The Super Jump in the High-Gravity area can be used in other sections.
info.name: PQ No Gems 35 - Messing with Physics
info.starthelptext: Float to each island and get no Gems! It's not as easy as it looks, however.
info.trivia: The level's final layout and scenery were based on Matan's recommendation, as Andrew was stuck. At some point Andrew thought about Moving Platforms to take you between the islands.
info.ultimatehint: You can achieve this one either by going throgh all areas without real mistakes, or give yourself an advantage using the Super Jump... such as in the Epic Rebound area.

info.awesomehint: Utilize the Bubble Powerup to make some really cool speed maneuvers, bump and rebound quickly on walls, cut through corners and to keep you floating in the air for as long as you can. Watch out for the Moving Platforms cycles, as they are the ones you'll
info.desc: Traverse the wide depths while utilizing your only friend, the Bubble Powerup. However, it only lasts one minute! The questions to ask are how fast will you use it up, and where will it run out?
info.egghint: Do the opposite to what you're told.
info.generalhint: It's a good idea for the first (and second) playthrough to focus on exploration rather than on beating the level. Familiarize yourself with the positions of no Gems that are required to beat the level.
info.name: PQ No Gems 78 - Minute Minute
info.starthelptext: No Gems are where your journey ends. Well, actually, the Finish Pad ends your journey, but no Gems are required to unlock it.
info.trivia:
Meant to be a beginner level, it was later developed while heavily inspired by 90s platformers, especially one called Hocus Pocus, where keys were required to unlock some rooms, and sometimes switches were used as well.
Marble Blast may not have keys and
info.ultimatehint: You will need to grab a few of the Time Travels that are in your way. Likewise, start with the right bottom side and go from there.

info.awesomehint: A number of shortcuts exist which can cut off a bit of the level, including one from the start to the 7.5 seconds Time Travel.
info.desc: Water erosion caused most of the level to disappear. Whatever is left is not very safe, so be careful.
info.generalhint:
The key to beat this level is to plan ahead by practicing each part individually.
You can mess up during an actual run any part and redo it without problem, but don't take too long or you will be forced to restart.
info.name: PQ No Gems 56 - Miscalculation
info.starthelptext: Do not squander your platforms!
info.trivia:
This level was started with grander scenery at the time, but died as realistic water was not possible at the end.
 The level started as a request from Matan to code a fade platform that would slowly disappear and only when the marble touched it.
info.ultimatehint:
Effectively, as long as you get all the Time Travels and don't do major mistakes, you should be fine here.

You may be able to use one of the islands to shave off a few precious seconds...

info.awesomehint: Use as many Super Speeds as possible while maintaining control over your marble.
info.desc: Everything's a blur!
info.egghint: Build up a lot of speed and jump at the right time.
info.generalhint: Diagonal movement isn't necessary at all unless you start going below the required speed. Just keep using the Super Speeds!
info.name: PQ No Gems 30 - Momentum
info.starthelptext: Don't let the various obstacles slow you down!
info.trivia: The Nest Egg was originally right in your path, but was moved because you were able to collect it nearly every time.
info.ultimatehint: Jump as much as possible and use the Super Speeds -- but be careful not to go so fast you can't steer at all!

info.awesomehint: The powerups will reduce your time quite a fair bit. The ending is a nasty piece of work to execute though, and after all that hard work too...
info.desc: An extended skill course. Hope you've been practicing -- you'll need all your skills to pass this one!
info.generalhint: You will need to muster a few techniques together in order to pass these challenges, and diagonal movement will prove most useful. The sand wall requires diagonal movement and careful jumping pattern to make it up.
info.name: PQ No Gems 54 - Musing
info.trivia: The last level Moshe made for PlatinumQuest, as he lost motivation and interest in Marble Blast. Originally meant to be a custom level that continued his Camp series, it turned into a PlatinumQuest level instead.
info.ultimatehint: There aren't many shortcuts, but as long as you roll fast and grab all the Time Travels you should be fine.

info.awesomehint: The start is standard, but then use the Anvil to do a very unexpected shortcut. If you're fast enough, the first Time Travel you catch will be your end time.
info.desc: Display your mastery of the normal, gravitational, and buoyant forces.
info.egghint: The easiest Nest Egg there can be. A freebie, as one may put it. No hints here so it appears to be harder than it really is.
info.generalhint: Follow the advice of the help bubbles and you should be alright.
info.name: PQ No Gems 37 - Newton's Dilemma
info.starthelptext: Time for your exam. Phones away!
info.trivia:
Matan wanted the big drop to be 60 meters high. Count and see if Pablo followed his advice.

While this level was under construction, Seizure implemented a code that accidentally deleted the MissionInfo, crashed PQ, and changed Pablo's marble to the pear.

This started out as a beginner level called Fundamentals of Physics, but it turned out to be Advanced. Andrew came up with the name.
info.ultimatehint: Collect most of the Time Travels and you should be fine.

info.awesomehint: You can skip almost all of the level from the beginning. The only difficult part is getting no Gems hit at the end.
info.desc: Roll across the beautiful landscape while taking advantage of different physics properties to get no Gems.
info.generalhint: Hit the split of the branching paths in the big chute to navigate to where you want, or slow down. The ending will take a number of attempts, but take note that some poles are higher than the rest and your marble can roll under them.
info.name: PQ No Gems 47 - Orthogonality
info.starthelptext: Your movement may be restricted, but your possibilities are not.
info.trivia: The level name is due to Pablo not liking the level name choices that almost everyone used, calling them 'immature'.
info.ultimatehint: The Time Travels are a must, as well as making no real mistakes here. The ending can be messed up a couple of times.

info.awesomehint: Get the Time Travel and no Gems first, followed by the left section. Have a Super Jump with you while the remainder of the run will be based on the Time Travels in the level. Make sure not to go out of the way for Gems!
info.desc: Can you find the quickest pathway among this assortment of Time Travels, Powerups, and no Gems?
info.generalhint: It's safe to ignore the no Gems inside the maze section, as they might take you way too long to collect.
info.name: PQ No Gems 17 - Path Finding Folly
info.trivia: Leaf originally submitted it to be a MBOnline custom level, until MBO went under. It was taken to PlatinumQuest and modified by Andrew to fit with the game. It kept breaking trying to convert, though, with over 20 attempts to try and fix those damned ramp
info.ultimatehint: Only go for no Gems, and use the Time Travels as a main part of your path. Use the Powerups to aid you!

info.awesomehint: Get all the Time Travels and jump early from the Moving Platform to the finish trigger.
info.desc: SOME THINGS ARE BROKEN AND CAN'T BE FIXED. Ride the moving platform around twice. Can you stay on for that long?
info.generalhint:
This level will require lots of... uh... perseverance to finish.

To get no tornadoes' Gem, simply stay on the bottom left corner of the Moving Platform, and then roll across to the other side just before it starts moving.
info.name: PQ No Gems 75 - Perseverance
info.starthelptext: Watch the interior change before your eyes after the first lap!
info.trivia:
Due to an old bug, this level used to shake erratically when you got halfway through it.

Originally there was no Checkpoint, which made the level insane to beat.
info.ultimatehint: You will need the 5, 7.5 and 10 seconds Time Travels. And a wall hit.

info.awesomehint: The best forwards path is... to go backwards.
info.desc: Conquer each of the physics changes.
info.egghint: Sometimes you just have to sequence-break.
info.generalhint: The color of the tiles can tell you what physics will be changed -- green tiles don't do anything, red tiles change marble speed, yellow tiles change jump height, purple tiles change gravity, and blue tiles change air resistance.
info.name: PQ No Gems 41 - Physical Activity
info.starthelptext: Jump up and hit the button to lower the purple floor.
info.trivia:
This level was born out of the pun in the name.

The original ending was planned to be a lot different, but it was scrapped because there was almost no player input involved in it.
info.ultimatehint: Perform a clean run. You can grab no Gems after the cannon by exiting the zero-gravity area before you reach the ground.

info.awesomehint:
Play with hunger in your eyes.

Also make three wall hits with superb rebounds.
info.desc: Satisfy your hunger.
info.generalhint: You don't... need a hint for a pizza level... do you?
info.name: PQ No Gems 60 - Pizzanator
info.starthelptext: Get no Gems before the pizza gets cold!
info.trivia: This level was originally created as a joke, but apparently it was good enough to get into the game.
info.ultimatehint: Grab no Gems before doing none, and finishing on the pizza slice.

info.awesomehint: Activate a button early, and keep the Super Jump for the ending.
info.desc: LOAD THE ORIGINAL POLYMORPHISM FIRST! OTHERWISE THE PLATFORM WON'T MOVE! Then thwart the rapidly evolving platform.
info.generalhint: You'll need to perform a diagonal wall hit late in the level. Hope you've been practicing...
info.name: PQ No Gems 48 - Polymorphism
info.starthelptext: Pay close attention to the commands.
info.trivia: The Multiple Trigger GoTo Target was coded specially for this level.
info.ultimatehint: After you hit the first button, jump backwards to nab a floating Time Travel and land on some platforms below you.

info.awesomehint: Go back and jump over the big gap.
info.desc: Take an introductory lap for this puzzle series.
info.generalhint: Jump while on the ice to help you maintain momentum. Use the curves to your advantage!
info.name: PQ No Gems 59 - Welcome Lap
info.starthelptext: On the ice you can't move your marble, but you can still jump.
info.trivia: Some people preferred this level to be an actual laps level rather than have no Gems. Matan felt it would make the level too long and hard.
info.ultimatehint: Jump as you're about to fall on the big downwards slope with the Time Travel. This means you won't have too much speed as you fall down on it, and thus can quietly press backwards and slow down at the end.

info.awesomehint: Diagonal usage and a few shortcuts can really help out.
info.desc: Find the quickest way around.
info.generalhint: Path is rather simple and linear, but you will have to backtrack. Go backwards as soon as you're on dry land, or else you will fall out of bounds. Using diagonal movement to slow down will be of greater help.
info.name: PQ No Gems 61 - Icy Path
info.starthelptext:
Nothing to stop you falling off.
Watch your speed!
info.trivia: The first level created for the Puzzle series. Heavily inspired from watching a speedrun for Kula World, Matan took this level and made it in Marble Blast.
info.ultimatehint: Go fast, nothing else to it.

info.awesomehint: You're going to circle a bit around the logo, and miss one of the small Time Travels that is ever slightly out of your way.
info.desc:
Another game with its logo put as an actual level.
Clearly original and creative!
Well done Matan!
info.generalhint: A simple level, the Par Time is there for a challenge if you desire to aim for no Gems.
info.name: PQ No Gems 63 - Emblem
info.trivia: When seeing the level, Threefolder was jealous that Matan could make a better PlatinumQuest logo than him. On a related note the map file is an absolute mess in order to make the level look good.
info.ultimatehint: If you zoom quickly into one of edge Time Travels, you can look back and activate the Super Speed to stop yourself from falling.

info.awesomehint:
You can save a bit of time by doing an unorthodox route, and miss a Time Travel Trigger with it.

Fun fact: You can jump on the grass to go faster, thanks to friction mechanics.
info.desc: Chip hits the ice and decides to chill out. Then he runs into a fake wall and turns the maze into a Thrash-A-Thon.
info.egghint: Align.
info.generalhint: Jumping on grass allows you to gain more speed. Alternatively use the grass to break a lot faster.
info.name: PQ No Gems 64 - Four Corners
info.starthelptext: Kidding! No fake walls here!! Do grab no Gems though, will you?
info.trivia:
Inspired by Chip's Challenge ice levels, though the fake walls were skipped for sanity's sake.

The Time Travel (Penalty?) triggers aren't placed at random, as they follow a specific ruleset.
info.ultimatehint: Make your own route, as long as you can stay consistent. Some are actually faster than others. Perhaps the golden rule here is that opposites attract.

info.awesomehint: Clear out the area furthest away from the start, and work your way towards the start point. After that, do the loop, grab no Gems at most and start the second floor.
info.desc: There is no corner gem. Still blame HiGuy.
info.generalhint: The lack of checkpoints means you will have to think before moving to the next areas.
info.name: PQ No Gems 66 - Double Maze
info.trivia: This level is in fact two Puzzle series floors that Matan made and joined them into one.
info.ultimatehint: Jumping right before hitting the Gravity Modifier on the ice loop will give you some speed boost. You can, technicaly, finish the loop without the time restarting.

info.awesomehint:
The route begins with the Time Travel right below the start pad, then no Gems, followed by the next floor and the top one last. I'm sure you can figure out how the route may look like.
It is also important to remember you can jump on Moving Platforms to gain extra height as they move up, helping you reach the next ground slightly quicker.
...Oh, and you can move where there is no ice. Including the empty, cold, space.
info.desc: Use the moving ice and concrete to get around this odd structure.
info.generalhint: Don't roll too fast on the elevators or you may find yourself in a sticky situation. Literally.
info.name: PQ No Gems 69 - Multi-Layer
info.starthelptext: The elevators reset when you're done using them.
info.trivia: The level had some bugs related to the Moving Platforms and its triggers. Don't look at it in the level editor unless you plan to have a heart attack.
info.ultimatehint: Start by dropping off the left of the start pad, and ignoring the Gem directly next to the icy elevator until later.

info.awesomehint:
This one needs stupid luck.
No Gems are identical to the Ultimate Time run.
After a wall hit, you must get the perfect speed, spin and direction on the concrete platform to no Gems, and hope the Moving Platforms don't screw you over.
Get no Gems and the Moving Platform after it sends you directly to the finish, or ends your run.
info.desc: The best solution is 50% memory and 50% random luck.
info.generalhint:
There's no denying this level will annoy you. You will need to carefully align yourself, jump to no Gems, and hope for the best.
Thankfully, the outskirt trim will usually save you unless you get hit pretty badly by one of those platforms.

This level marks where the Puzzle series get remarkably harder.
info.name: PQ No Gems 71 - Chaos Theory
info.starthelptext: I can't feel my brain!
info.trivia: HiGuy felt rather evil when making this level. It certainly confused and downright pissed off many.
info.ultimatehint: Start with no Gems directly from the start pad. You should be able to collect no Gems with ease as the Moving Platforms guide you to it. No Gems are simple (wait for an opening) and zero aren't hard to figure out.

info.awesomehint: While extremely hard, it is possible to get no Gems in two sweeping movements.
info.desc: If you thought this was hard in two dimensions, just wait and see.
info.generalhint: Get no Gems and use the bouncy floor to activate the moving platforms. Sit still when descending and you won't have any issues.
info.name: PQ No Gems 73 - Sphere
info.starthelptext: No movement on neither the ice nor in the center.
info.trivia:
This unforgiving level was the second level ever made for the puzzle series, a full day after Puzzle 2 was made.
Originally the Par Time was 2 minutes.
info.ultimatehint: You can use the orbital gravity to get no Gems in mid-air, without any moving platforms. Escape might prove difficult.

info.awesomehint: Create a path using ALL Time Travels!
info.desc: Raid the Grand Complex for no treasure, but beware the hidden dangers.
info.egghint: Go slowly with the Super Jump, and just wait it out.
info.generalhint: The height limit for being unable to move your marble, on flat ground, is exactly 1 texture unit high. Slopes have increased limit.
info.name: PQ No Gems 76 - King Minos's Grand Complex
info.trivia:
This massive level also takes the crown for the longest level name in PlatinumQuest. This actually caused a few problems in the user interface, and HiGuy complained to no end about it.

Can you make out the hidden message in this level?
info.ultimatehint: Select no Gems that are too far away from the rest, and create a path using the remainder. Don't be afraid to add in Time Travels to the mix and change the path as necessary.

info.awesomehint: While the trigger means you have no control over the marble, it only extends up to a certain height. You must be very aggressive with the grass squares, as jumping on them can give you big boosts.
info.desc: Picking up chips is what the challenge is all about. But on the ice, Chip gets chapped and feels like a chump instead of a champ.
info.egghint: There are a couple of ways to get it, either using a Super Speed, or a teleporter.
info.generalhint: The level itself is rather straight-forwards, but there are a few chokepoints which lead to no Gems that otherwise you can't get.
info.name: PQ No Gems 77 - I Slide
info.starthelptext: Hang on, this isn't Chip's Challenge!!
info.trivia:
Level name and design inspiration came from Chip's Challenge.
The level was originally meant to be in top-down view and the player able to go up/down/left/right only and it would send him across the ice without problems.
Only after finishing it, Matan discovered that such code was not possible (or HiGuy refused to, anyway).
info.ultimatehint: Use the Super Speeds and loop around the block!

info.awesomehint: For this nightmare, you're on your own.
info.desc: A claustrophobic and befuddling structure with a sinister secret...
info.generalhint:
Follow the signs, and don't let the scenery confuse you.
The checkpoints can be of assistance, as long as you haven't taken too long after them.
info.name: PQ No Gems 79 - Nightmare
info.starthelptext:
Once you're off, don't let go of the movement keys.
Use diagonal movement, and jumping may help.
Slow down when needed, or you'll be thrown off the level.
info.trivia: Matan thought this level would make for an excellent and evil finale of the Puzzle series. What do you think?
info.ultimatehint: As long as you go fast and follow the same general path, you should easily make it through.

info.awesomehint: An edge hit can help you when landing the first skip to rebound towards no Gems.
info.desc: How fast can you climb up?
info.generalhint: If you jump while rolling up a slope, you'll go slightly higher.
info.name: PQ No Gems 23 - Race to the Top
info.trivia: The level's layout had the idea of this level being used for some sort of multiplayer race mode.
info.ultimatehint: Using diagonal movement you can skip a couple small chunks of this level.

info.awesomehint: This level has some amazing shortcuts if you aren't afraid to find them.
info.desc: Go to the finish!
info.generalhint:
More speed on the initial platform does not necessarily mean more speed later on.

There is no required speed. To get speed, jump as much as you can on the straight-way. Be careful not to hit the Ice Shards!
info.name: PQ No Gems 12 - Rail
info.starthelptext:
Activate the upcoming Anvil as soon as you get it.
Try to maintain your speed!
info.trivia: The first version of this level was hated by every single staff member. Pablo did a massive makeover to this level, and added minor things even a year later after it was done.
info.ultimatehint: Who needs to even change gravity? (Also, the Anvil is useful.)

info.awesomehint: Exit the ramp from the side and diagonal your way to victory!
info.desc: There is no qualifying speed. Maneuver through traffic.
info.generalhint:
In Haste mode, the goal is to finish the level above a certain speed. In this level, there is no "certain speed".

On the straightway before the loop, try holding <func:bind jump
info.name: PQ No Gems 05 - Hour
info.starthelptext:
Here, you'll play a level.
If you know diagonal movement, that will come in handy.
info.trivia: The first jump in this level is probably one of the most meticulously edited parts of the entire game. The launch ramp was modified, the position of the Super Speed was changed, the landing zone was extended and changed from 4 tiles wide to 5, then a spli
info.ultimatehint: You'll need to skip the big tube. It's a rather tricky jump...

info.awesomehint: You can skip the second half of the level with two precise cannon shots.
info.desc: Show off your cannon and fade platform skills!
info.generalhint: In the part with the wall hit, jump right before the end of the ramp to avoid being sent Out of Bounds.
info.name: PQ No Gems 38 - Scouring the Framework
info.starthelptext: Quick reaction skills, too.
info.trivia: Phil made the interior for this level; Pablo added presentation attributes. This level was originally an expert level.
info.ultimatehint: Don't screw up too badly. You can afford to misfire a few times, but don't blow it.

info.awesomehint: Keep the Super Jump you picked up at the start and use it to no Gems and rebound to the mud next to the finish.
info.desc: Watch your balance on the moving platforms!
info.generalhint: Keep your balance on the moving platforms! The one at the end of the level can be a pain. Don't give up on it!
info.name: PQ No Gems 72 - Scrum at the Spires
info.starthelptext: Travel to the four islands. You should probably find out which one contains the finish.
info.trivia: This is one of only two levels to not use a skybox -- the other is 'Bag of Secrets...'
info.ultimatehint: Start by going to the island straight ahead. You'll have to make a huge jump to the rightmost one soon after.

info.awesomehint: Essential planning includes skipping as many teleport gates as possible.
info.desc: Planning remains essential.
info.generalhint:
Entrance and exit gates are not identical looking. This could help you determine which way to go.

To get to the finish pad, you'll need a very nice wall hit.
info.name: PQ No Gems 74 - Serendipity Labyrinth
info.starthelptext:
Gates with triangles are entrances;
gates with circles are exits.
info.trivia: Pablo got inspired by Oaky's Serendipity Gardens level and made this as a sequel.
info.ultimatehint:
On the first layer, you can just use the slanted walls to avoid gates that will take you elsewhere in the level.

You can also wall hit to get up to the next level.

info.awesomehint: Go up the red route first, then the middle, followed by the last one. The Time Travels are necessary, but not all of them.
info.desc: Use the alternate routes to grab no Gems as you make three laps around the track.
info.generalhint: To get no Gems, use a fan. In addition, diagonal movement will be of help.
info.name: PQ No Gems 33 - Shelosh
info.starthelptext: Take the route you think is the fastest, as long as you get no Gems on each color of floor.
info.trivia:
Originally stuck in Bonus, it eventually deemed fitting enough for the main level set once several bugs that related to its gameplay were fixed.

Level name in Hebrew means 'Three'.
info.ultimatehint: Start with the pink route, and then use the ending Super Speed to get enough height to make it to the red section. Collect all the Time Travels and no Gems, then choose your route... the pink is the easiest!

info.awesomehint: Jump at precise moments to make it up the ladders much faster. You can also get to no Gems above the starting area without having to go all the way around.
info.desc: The legend returns...
info.generalhint: Stay still while in front of a ladder to climb it.
info.name: PQ No Gems 62 - Take No Gold
info.starthelptext: Get no gold, Jake, before the Mad Monks get you!
info.trivia: Based on the first level of 'Lode Runner: The Legend Returns.'
info.ultimatehint: If you play quickly enough, you might beat this level before HiGuy is able to get his Virtual Machine to load this level in the actual game.

info.awesomehint: The only shortcut is after no Gems, where you can use an Anvil on the bottom Time Travel to get back up to no Gems. Everything else relies on pure speed.
info.desc: Learn some more advanced applications of the Anvil powerup!
info.generalhint: You don't actually need the Anvil on the big ramp -- if anything, it'll just slow you down.
info.name: PQ No Gems 28 - Terminal Velocity
info.starthelptext: The Anvil is applicable in many more situations than you may think at first. The following challenges will show you some more advanced usages.
info.trivia: This level was intended to be a tutorial level for the Anvil power up, but was deemed too difficult for beginners. High Rise, Quick Fall was made as its replacement.
info.ultimatehint: Grab all the Time Travels and keep screw-ups to a minimum and you'll be fine. Also, on the long ramp with the jump, you don't even need to use the Anvil. Just use diagonal movement and you should be fine.

info.awesomehint:
This one is clever, yet tough: Use the checkpoints as a launch pad.
Additionally, start by getting no Gems. You can cross the gap and if you slow down fast enough you won't get a Gem, hit the edge and rebound successfully without falling down.
info.desc: Learn about the fading platforms, preferably without falling off.
info.generalhint: Most of the time, there's no way of telling how each Fade Platform will function -- tread cautiously.
info.name: PQ No Gems 07 - Trained to Fade
info.trivia:
Phil originally developed the Fade Platforms in response for the need of a better trapdoor, one with a similar mechanism to that of the trapdoor, but also something new.
While thinking of an introduction level for the Fade Platforms, Matan stumbled on an early design of a trapdoor introduction level by a different mod (this level no longer exists, sadly).
Liking the idea, but disappointed with its execution, Matan decided to set up a smaller and simpler level with faster challenges in the spirit of the split pathways.
info.ultimatehint: Get the Time Travel first, then go to the Fading Platforms to the left.

info.awesomehint: You may want to use a tree to skip to the end, and then complete the level in reverse.
info.desc: Solve simple puzzles by using the Teleport PowerUp to its utmost advantage.
info.egghint: Remember to pay attention to the caution stripes. After a short balancing act, you will be treated to an indoor slalom.
info.generalhint: The Teleport PowerUp is especially helpful for getting back up from places that are too far down.
info.name: PQ No Gems 10 - Transporter Lock
info.starthelptext: Once you have a Teleport PowerUp, press <func:bind mouseFire> to set your location. Press it again to teleport.
info.trivia: This level replaced an old level that also taught about the Teleporter powerup. While the old level wasn't bad, there were quite a lot of issues with it.
info.ultimatehint: Keep in mind that the Teleport PowerUp has a short delay. By activating it preemptively, you can collect no Gems while the teleportation is occurring and shave off those crucial seconds.

info.awesomehint: Use the bumper at the start to get plenty of speed.
info.desc: Soar through the air with grace!
info.generalhint: Don't forget -- jump right before you use a Super Jump to reach greater heights!
info.name: PQ No Gems 31 - Tricks in the Air
info.trivia: This level was found in a messy, broken, and unfinished state. Even then it was still a fun level to play, though, so Threefolder salvaged the remains and prettied it up a bit.
info.ultimatehint: It is possible to jump over the wall and to the left to land with the Shock Absorber next to the fan.

info.awesomehint: Use the Super Speed!
info.desc: A variety of obstacles in a three-part level. Can you slide your way through?
info.generalhint:
Don't be too concerned if you miss no Gems, as you only need none to complete the level.

When entering the launcher, try to time your entrance so you get launched while right next to the blocks that push you out.
info.name: PQ No Gems 16 - Triple Action
info.trivia:
During construction, this level was often referred to as Ticklish Alligator. Don't let this level bite you!

Originally this was made for the Marble Mini-Golf Community Group Level, but only a third of the level was finished by the deadline. Now you get
info.ultimatehint: If you grab no Gems, you can easily perform a massive shortcut later on. Also, get as many Time Travels as you can. Some are harder than others.

info.awesomehint: Take the marble collision boundaries with no Gems to the next level!
info.desc: Wacky World welcomes you!
info.generalhint: You will have to make a pathway for every island if you wish to survive this ordeal.
info.name: PQ No Gems 67 - Unstable Islands
info.starthelptext: Like Jake Peril, you're not allowed to jump. Unlike him, your camera actually follows you.
info.trivia: Level design based on Wacky World Level #19 in Lode Runner 2.
info.ultimatehint: Speed, and plenty of it.

info.desc: WHERE IS PQ?
info.name: PQ Where?
info.starthelptext: Wait, WHERe IS PQ?

info.awesomehint: The same as UT Hint, but go faster and keep your marble under more control and do not hit the trees.
info.desc: What a wack stadium am I right?!
info.egghint: Go so fast you clip out of the invisible box youre stuck in, then explore the outside until you come across the egg.
info.generalhint: Experiment with the Physics of the Stadium before getting into speedrunning!
info.name: Physics Stadium
info.starthelptext: Your Speed, Your Bounce, Your Super Speed Strength, Your Super Jump Strength and Your Jumping will be changed when you enter the stadium!
info.trivia: In the level's initial state, the values for Speed, Super Speed Strength, Jump and Bounce were way higher, and Gravity and Time Scale also had different, much different values.
info.ultimatehint: Prioritize getting the gems in the air and the Time Travels first. Also, take to the skies if you want more time, you will see.

info.desc: Get all the Gems in this Nostalgic Maze!
info.egghint: Wall-Hit... But Where?
info.generalhint: Make sure to grab the "Bonus Fruit" once it pops out in the center of the Maze!
info.name: Pac-Blast

info.desc: A combination of Pitfalls, Platform Party and Winding Road, but REMADE!! And made for a fit marble! (Playtested by ItzJean, Times decided upon by ItzJean)
info.name: Parkourfalls!
info.starthelptext: Careful! Your road to the finish will not be easy!

info.awesomehint: Finishing sideways gives more style points than an edge-hit, but it's a lot slower. If you get the gem with fewer than 18 seconds on the clock, you should be good.
info.desc: It's like There and Back Again, but it has tons of paths!
info.egghint: Regardless of how you finish the level, you should see it right there.
info.generalhint: Many areas give key information. Look everywhere for powerups and Time Travels.
info.name: Path Finding Paradise
info.starthelptext: Get the gem and head back. Some areas are harder than others. BE CAREFUL!
info.trivia: Development began in the level editor in June 2019, but it soon stopped after I lost the files. Following concept changes, development resumed in March 2020 in Constructor. The delay was probably for the better.
info.ultimatehint: Skip large parts of the level at once to save lots of time. The gravity junction has part of the answer to the Ultimate Time.

info.awesomehint: Find as many time travels both in the main path and the shortcuts as you can to shave off tons of seconds.
info.desc: You can take the main path or just take shortcuts along the way.
info.egghint: Easy to see, hard to get. You might need to get on top of something.
info.generalhint: Remember that the green path is the main path. The shortcuts are yellow. Thus, you'll get more or less gems than you need as a result. Pick your paths carefully. If one path is too hard, then you can always take another.
info.name: Pathfinding Ingenuity
info.starthelptext: The green path is the main path. The yellow paths are just shortcuts.
info.trivia: The floating circles holding the trees aren't made from pie slices. It was made from a simple cyliner tool. I figured that would be easier to convert.
info.ultimatehint: They are many pathways you can use to beat it.

info.desc: When marble skills reach their peak, and challenges go beyond, persistence is all that remains.
info.name: Persistence

info.starthelptext: Up you go, kiddo.
info.name: Pesky
info.desc: Just a quick venture.

info.awesomehint: Go really fast that you'll get the right side of the gem at the spinning platform area  at around 28 to 29 seconds on your time.
info.desc: This level isn't inspired by Physical Activity if you're asking.
info.generalhint: Go fast.
info.name: Physics Course
info.starthelptext: Keep an eye on holes!
info.ultimatehint: Get the time modifiers.

info.awesomehint: Grab each half of the Time Travels on the hairpin for the first two laps. In the third lap, you can save time at the last minute by going through a table on the center of the island.
info.desc: Complete three laps around a racetrack that loops from the pier to a small island.
info.generalhint: Stay above the target speed, but be careful not to go too fast. If you slow down, you're given ten seconds to reach the target speed again. Collect a certain amount of gems in each lap so that you won't waste too much time. When reaching a boost pad, jump
info.name: Pier Pressure
info.starthelptext: Can you feel the summer winds?
info.trivia: The layout and sections of the level are inspired by the levels in Sonic Unleashed's Jungle Joyride.
info.ultimatehint: Stay at the bottom pier on the first lap. Save the top piers for the remaining laps. Grab all of the Time Travels on the hairpin. Go for whatever path you want to take on the grey bridge. Grab some of the Time Travels on the small island in each lap.

info.desc: This is not your ordinary level! Be careful on the Moving/Rotating platforms!
info.egghint: There is a hidden Gravity Modifier somewhere in the level...
info.name: Platform Mess
info.starthelptext: Timing is Key!
Be careful when jumping from platform to platform.
info.name: From Platform to Platform
info.desc: Jump from platform to platform.
Ascend the precipice, then ski to the finish! Now with fewer Time Travels.
info.name: Precipice Revisited
info.starthelptext: Watch your step as you climb up this steep cliff!

info.awesomehint: Go super fast before reaching the 3 by 3 checkpoint platform. Instantly hit your respawn key once you're there. You should get around 22 second Time Travel catch.
info.desc: Precision and accuracy are required to play this level.
info.generalhint: Go fast!
info.name: Precise Angles
info.ultimatehint: Cut corners. Don't hit too high up.

info.awesomehint: Optimization is what you need.
info.desc: Push buttons to unlock switches and powerups in this busy area of nature.
info.egghint: You might have to get it from behind...
info.generalhint: Push the buttons to progress through the level. Should be easy to do, but it might get slightly harder in the side scrolling section.
info.name: Press Garden
info.starthelptext: Find buttons to unlock switches and powerups.
info.trivia: The only moving platform made from constructor is the cube in the side-scrolling section. The song used in this level is from Sonic Mania, like the music used in Studiopolis. The level also required more than 15 parts to make each part of the level work.
info.ultimatehint: Grab time travels to finish as always, but some shortcuts might not work.

info.name: Progression
info.starthelptext: Don't forget to grab the first gem before going out of the building.
info.desc: Progress ahead in this unfinished level.

info.artist: James Colsey/Song by Buzzmusic/Skybox by Threefolder
info.desc: Ascend this progressing paradise. There is more to do here than last time.
info.name: Progression 2
info.starthelptext: Find time modifiers if you are really confident.

info.awesomehint: Grab the first teleporter and don't use them until after rolling off the quarter pipe near the first gem. Then, grab all the Time Travels. Don't use the second teleporter until you're near the second checkpoint. Complete the rest of the level normally.
info.desc: Learn about the propulsion floor and how it can help you increase your speed to reach places from a distance.
info.egghint: Check from behind a certain section.
info.generalhint: It is always the case that orange floors that have emitters on them are propulsion floors. Be sure not to lose control when moving around.
info.name: Propulsion
info.starthelptext: The orange floor to your right is the propulsion floor. Touching it will increase your speed and acceleration.
info.trivia:
This level's main mechanic was inspired by the propulsion gel from Portal 2.

This level also had a lot more vertical wooden support, but it was scrapped becuase one deemed it as over the top.
info.ultimatehint: Skip the first teleporter item and respawn at the first checkpoint after clearing the first challenge. Then, use the second teleporter to geab all the Time Travels in the straight line. Complete the rest of the stage like normal.

info.awesomehint: Skip as several gemfree areas as you can.
info.desc: Overcome various obstacles and unlock the doors to finish.
info.egghint: Grab a Super Jump before heading to the top of the red block.
info.generalhint: Diagonal movement can help you in some of the areas.
info.name: Pursuit
info.starthelptext: Watch out for the hazards ahead!
info.trivia: As of recently, a gravity modifier was replaced with a gravity trigger because the gravity modifier wouldn't send you back to the original rotation.
info.ultimatehint: There are Time Travels hidden in the natural areas. Use the radar to pinpoint them.

info.awesomehint: Plan a route to get the Time Travels in a short interval of time. You don't even have to go crazy fast, unless you know where you're going.
info.desc: Now served with a brand new skybox! Too bad you really won't have the time to contemplate it. Say, look at the Par Time...
info.generalhint: You can use the bouncy edges or the round bumpers by rolling on them and getting a boost upwards in order to break free from the paralysis of the ice and redirect yourself in the air.
info.name: Puzzle 13 - Candice's Flat Pinball
info.starthelptext: Hurry up!
info.trivia:
The level's style and its name are a big reference to Candice's Gym Puzzle in Snowpoint from Pokemon Diamond / Pearl, except there's no ladders or snowballs (MBOUltimate gave the reference). 
 
Also, when you installed the level, you can see the interior has a different name than the level. It's simply because I found the first name not very appetizing. I was too lazy to change the file name, so... gomen nasai!
info.ultimatehint: Follow your instinct and go for the Time Travel on your left. You can also take advantage of the Super Speeds available.

info.awesomehint: Luck is needed, keep collecting time travels though. Its Gem Finding Folly all over again
info.desc: Hunt for gems in the four wildly different quadrants
info.generalhint: Collect the nearby time travels
info.name: Quadrant Collector
info.starthelptext: Go start collecting the gems!
info.ultimatehint: Do your best to  keep collecting time travels as soon as they respawn

info.desc: It is imperitive that you grab Time Travels to beat the qualifying time.
info.name: Rage Against Time
info.starthelptext: Climb up the tower, collect the gems, and grab the Time Travels to beat the clock!

info.desc: Take a trip involving gliding around on rails.
info.generalhint: Be liberal with the Shock Absorber, for it will help greatly.
info.name: Rail Rocket
info.starthelptext: Easy does it.
info.ultimatehint: Diagonal movement is not necessary on the "rails."

info.desc:
This is my very first racing level, so be indulgent, please! 
Anyways, make three laps around this green track lost into this dense forest, avoiding all the hazards on your way.
info.generalhint:
Brown grids will give the marble a speed boost. They behave like auto Super Speeds, if you want, so remember to face forwards when taking a boost. 
Also, as mentioned in the description, get a good handle of your speed, so you don't rush and go Out of Bounds.
info.name: Rain Forest
info.starthelptext: Always remember to face forwards when you reach a speed boost area.
info.trivia:
The original circuit was meant to be a bit wider, but I immediatly thought it would be too long to build, so I compacted it. 
 
Would you believe if I told you it took me a solid 45 minutes to place all the trees, rocks, plants and fix the mis-duplicated elements? 
Add around 20 minutes non-stop to make and correct the level, 2 hours spent on the Constructor, and you should have the total time of the construction of the level. Bring the calculators!
info.ultimatehint: Behave just like in Sky High Circuit. That's the only help I can give you.

info.desc: How many gems can you get until the timer runs out?
info.name: Ramps N Gems
info.starthelptext: Ramps Reloaded 2019 Edition
Part of your daily dose of pointless screwed up levels.
info.desc: I just put some stuff in and the level works... XD
info.name: Random

info.desc: Make your way thorugh this ravine; collect all the gems and finish!
info.egghint: Just jump off the ravine.
info.generalhint: Time yourself on the bumpers.
info.name: Ravine Jumper
