info.starthelptext: Does this level looks familiar to you?
info.trivia: This level is the remake of my old level 'GET OUT !!!!', which was made back in 2008. If you noticed, this level is based on Wall Master from Marble Blast Platinum, as the original level used that interior.
info.ultimatehint: Do not make any mistakes; picking the teleporter first prevents you from waiting the super jump to respawn if you picked suepr jump first.

info.desc: Traverse the paths through the grass, but beware of the hazards ahead!
info.name: Red Roots
info.starthelptext: Use the super speed to launch yourself off the ramp to your right.

info.awesomehint: Try getting the hidden time travel by bouncing off a repulsion floor. Also, try getting the time travel in the hole before grabbing the third gem.
info.desc: Learn about the repulsion floor and how it can help you reach high places.
info.egghint: Find a teleporter in one of the natural areas. You'll be warped to the highest point of the level. Grab a super jump and use it to reach the other high point of the level. There are other ways to get the nest egg by using some other techniques.
info.generalhint:
In most cases, the white flames will indicate that you are on a repulsion floor. Cases like the section with the holes is one exception.

If you are stuck in a hole and can't make it to the top by just bouncing, jump. It generally gives you more height.
info.name: Repulsion
info.starthelptext: The blue floor in front of you is the repulsion floor. Jump off the floor to reach the platform above.
info.trivia:
This level's main mechanic was inspired by the repulsion gel from Portal 2.\
\
There was also another version of this level that wasn't really that good.
info.ultimatehint: There is a time travel on top of a stack of blue crates. Use it to your advantage.

info.name: Reverse Orthogonality
info.starthelptext: Your movement may be restricted, but your possibilities are not.
info.desc: Roll across the beautiful landscape while taking advantage of different physics properties to get the gems... backwards.
info.generalhint: Wall hit up the drop shaft. It's the only insanely difficult part.

info.awesomehint: You'll need to use hazards to your advantage and move fast while collecting Time Travels along the way.
info.desc: Bend the laws of gravity until they break!
info.egghint: You'll have to find a way to get off track...
info.generalhint: Use the move right key for the blue areas. Use the move left key for the red areas. Don't worry about rebounding from gravity to gravity. The Shock Absorber has you covered.
info.name: Rightside Dizzy
info.starthelptext: Blue arrows signify normal gravity. Red arrows signify inverted gravity.
info.trivia:
This level is based on a side-scrolling level in Super Mario Galaxy 2. It is also the first side-scrolling level to include hazards such as bumpers, mines, and ice shards in.

This level is also probably the longest PQ side-scrolling level to date. Not by much, though.
info.ultimatehint: The only efficient way of beating the ultimate time is to do every part well and avoid all hazards.

info.desc: Time to take your ring stunts to the next level.
info.name: Ring Riot

info.desc: What multiple mental breakdowns can make a Level Creator do. This level is meant to not be liked, to be hard and very long. Can you beat this gigantic level?
info.name: Road to Ascension
info.starthelptext: Chapter #1/3: The Beginning.

info.name: Robinet
info.desc: It may look like there are shortcuts but remember to collect the gems!
info.starthelptext: Roll off the ramp and get launched to the left.

info.awesomehint: Go FAST
info.desc: Explore this massive, relaxing level after a long days grinding, or just to have fun!
info.egghint: You may or may not have to steal it from an innocent marble.
info.generalhint: If you're going for the pastest path start at the quarter flat pipe!
info.name: Island Rooftops
info.starthelptext: There are many paths to take, the path behind you leads to the finish.

info.desc: This level is dedicated to hPerks for Secret Santa 2019, which was hosted by Mike. All layers are rotationally symmetrical, but item placements are not.
info.generalhint: When going up the layers, pay careful attention to your spin. Be confident in your landings.
info.name: Rotational Symmetry
info.starthelptext: Mind your spin when landing.
info.trivia: A very quick Google search prevented this level from being named Radial Symmetry.
info.ultimatehint: Find a full minute of time bonus with a good path if you want to get the Ultimate Time.

info.artist: James C./Tested by MikeSan, Thegeniusyoshi, and Threefolder
info.awesomehint: Try to reach for rotating platforms as early as possible to shave off a few seconds. You can also try moving in the opposite direction of the rotating panels.
info.desc: Cautiously make your way through the spinning platforms and collect the gems.
info.egghint: Try looking through the undersides of the hall.
info.generalhint:
Note that some of these spinning platforms can mess with your marble's physics. So try not to slip off of those platforms.

There are also some ways to go through or under these spinning panels.
info.name: Rotazione
info.starthelptext: Control your movement when rolling on the rotating platforms.
info.trivia:
The name of the level, 'Rotazione', is italian for the word 'Spin'. It is similar to how Tiro Test was named.

This level also had to go through so much conversions to eventually work perfectly that help from a staff member was needed.
info.ultimatehint: Grab the Time Travels that are on the spinning platforms to save some time. You may also try skipping a few platforms.

info.awesomehint: Just go fast, im not even kidding, and dont fall, good luck!
info.desc: Roll through the Pink Structures! Shoutouts to Ralph for the Pink skybox <3
info.egghint: Collect all the gems, and then get confused.
info.generalhint: Run the level normally if its your first time playing it, then try to speedrun it!
info.name: Little Pink Venture!
info.starthelptext: Do you dare climb this to the end?
info.trivia: Az wanted me to make a pink level so I did it, yeeah.
info.ultimatehint: Wall-hit the first button, hunt all of the Time Sundials, they can be anywhere.

info.awesomehint: One shot, One go, Full Speed, No checkpoints, can you do it?
info.desc: Slow-mo? Its possible in PQ? Without custom code? Yesss, it is!
info.egghint: A Gyrocopter is going to be needed to reach these kinds of heights!
info.generalhint: If its your first time playing with this mechanic, take it slow, get used to the speeds that the tiles offer you, then try to speedrun it!
info.name: Stop...Slow-Mo!
info.starthelptext: Lets mess with the game!
info.trivia: This is my first PQ level of the 2020s, kinda cool ngl!
info.ultimatehint: No breaks, full speed! And be sure to search around for some extra time before you get into the action.

info.starthelptext: This should be obvious.
info.desc: The first of a few random puzzles.
info.name: Random Puzzle 1

info.desc: Ascend up this pathway filled with bouncy floors and space areas.
info.name: Sanctuary Towers
info.starthelptext: Collect the gems while making your way through this elevated haven.

info.desc: Climb up the course while mastering the challenges of the sand friction.
info.name: Sand Lot
info.starthelptext: Gain some speed to roll up the sandy wall ahead.

info.desc: Wait for the platforms to shrink up in order to get the gems.
info.starthelptext: Don't be confused by the pattern of the platforms.
info.name: Scalene

info.starthelptext: If you think getting TO the gem is hard, wait until you have to come back.
info.name: Sewer Switch
info.desc: Don't worry, marbles can't smell anything.
It's a Ship.
info.name: Ship
info.starthelptext: Mornin' Captain!

info.desc: Practice your anti-recoiling skills in this course.
info.name: Shocking Trial
info.starthelptext: The first part is simple. Just roll up the wall using the oncoming Anti-Recoils.

info.desc: Never shall you traverse a level part right side up.
info.generalhint: When jumping toward a checkpoint, try to land on the powerup. This will allow you to attempt a few challenges more often until you clear them.
info.name: Side Glide
info.starthelptext: There is a gem under the platform with the start pad.
info.ultimatehint: Collect a few Time Travels, one of which is hidden.

info.desc: Hit the red walls to launch yourself forward to get more speed.
info.name: Side Launch
info.starthelptext: Control your spin when slowing down.

info.awesomehint: After an edge-hit, you will exclusively bounce toward the finish. Do not double-dip on the Time Travels.
info.desc: Keep caution while skiing down this mountain of scraps.
info.generalhint: If you cannot see in front of you, the path is most likely in the center.
info.name: Skiing on Scraps
info.starthelptext: Slow down adequately on the turns.
info.trivia: This skiing level is dedicated to Go'way, who loves playing Black Diamond.
info.ultimatehint: Collect one of the three Time Travels in the middle section.

info.generalhint: Don't go slow.
info.name: Sky High Speedway
info.starthelptext: Keep jumping on the straightways to gain speed, and do go faster than you can handle!
info.desc: The minimum speed has vastly increased. Can you stay above it?
Careful or you'll get stuck!
info.name: Skymaze
info.starthelptext: Hm, what could those platforms down there be?

info.awesomehint: Find a good spot and Super Speed to the finish... from the bottom of the level. If you get the Time Travel on the way, that's even better, but be advised: you have only one try at this!
info.desc:
This time, the timing of this tough level is going to be quite tight, so you better climb those muddy mountains without losing any precious second! 
Okay, I lied, it's not really tough at all, and the Par Time is quite a joke, but be fast, no matter what happens.
info.egghint: Buttons can do miracles. Look for a texture incoherence, then head for a tree. You will clearly see the Nest Egg.
info.generalhint: Check the grassy parts, there's a Time Travel that can help you out calm this timer down.
info.name: Slipperier Climb
info.starthelptext: Be fast and don't slip up!
info.trivia:
The design of this level is inspired of an old Marble Blast Elite level I saw on Marson's old videos. 
The name is a cheap remixed ripoff from a Crash Bandicoot level. 
This level had a Sonic dash ring hidden into the interior before (for the Nest Egg), but I removed it because it was accessible without it. This experiment was a success and I might use it in a future level.
info.ultimatehint:
1) Bumpers can be your allies if you use them in a clever way. 
2) Quick respawning can help, especially with the red button.

info.desc: An ultra course about slopes? That is new!
info.name: Slope Inferno
info.starthelptext: Welcome to Slope Inferno!

info.awesomehint: The normal route is just too long to be viable. For starters, you can skip almost all of Double Scoop.
info.desc: Master the slopes in this remake of Slope Inferno.
info.egghint: Around and around the trim you go. Advancing past the trapdoors is a big no-no.
info.generalhint: Take your time. Avoid jumping on the steep slope in Charge Forward, and try not to jump when switching rings in Around the Rings.
info.name: Slope Inferno Reconstructed
info.starthelptext: Conquer the slopes ahead!
info.trivia: Almost every challenge was majorly redesigned or replaced entirely. No more tubes!
info.ultimatehint: It should be obvious that Time Travels are good. Keep in mind that one Super Speed is enough to reach the top of Mountaineering.

info.desc: Gain some momentum to roll up certain slopes in this level.
info.name: Slope Momentum

info.desc: Ascend, then ascend some more, then keep going.
info.generalhint: Slope hits work best when you jump right before the slope. Then you jump both before and when you hit the slope. This is also true for bouncy platforms.
info.ultimatehint: If you don't make too many mistakes this is possible.
info.awesomehint: Basically just nail all the challenges on the first try. Harder than it looks though.
info.name: Sloped Up
info.starthelptext: What's up? Not you, that's for certain.

info.name: Small Simplicity
info.desc: Simply follow the path to the top.
info.artist: James Colsey/Super Stop Powerup by Whirligig and Threefolder

info.name: Spidering
info.desc: Does whatever a spider does.

info.awesomehint: You will need the Super Speed for an edge-hit. There is also a faster way to get the Time Travel on the greeenhouse. In the final section, you can go above the fans and turbines by gaining speed. Just don't hit the huge turbine on your way to the finish.
info.desc: Master the wind using or avoiding fans and turbines in this eco-friendly course.
info.egghint: Go to an area where the three big turbines are and the egg will be hidden in the grass.
info.generalhint: Duct fans will blow you away, while the turbines will suck you in. In this course, they can both be helpful and a hindrance. For fans, move forward as fast as you can to get past them. For turbines, pull back if you think you're being sucked in too fast.
info.name: Spiritus
info.starthelptext: Use the propulsion floors to make it through the fans.
info.trivia: The name of the level, 'Spiritus', means 'wind' in latin.
info.ultimatehint: In the first turbine section, you can shave off some seconds by skipping some corners. Later, edge-hit to the top of the greenhouse to grab a Time Travel that can really save some time.

info.starthelptext: The choice doesn't matter if the objective is the same.
info.name: Split Boundaries
info.desc: Grab the diamonds on both routes. Any method of pathway works well.

info.awesomehint: SANIC SPEED SPRITE CRANBERRY
info.desc: Okay so basically I'm LeBron asking if you want a Sprite Cranberry
info.generalhint: Sprite Cranberry
info.name: Wanna Sprite Cranberry?
info.starthelptext: LeBron hopes you can find the land of SPRITE CRANBERRY. Appease him or die, fool.
info.ultimatehint: Fast Sprite Cranberry

info.desc: Climb up this course by using ramps and jumping up stairs.
info.name: Stepping Slopes

info.desc: Avoid tornadoes in this windy course.
info.name: Storm Chaser
info.starthelptext: Be a proud storm chaser!

info.desc: Inspired by Lightning Ice, this speed level folds back on itself multiple times.
info.generalhint: Stay fast! Moving slowly will cause you to fail various challenges.
info.name: Strata
info.starthelptext: Fast camera turnarounds will go a long way. Do not jump on the mud.
info.ultimatehint: Collect the Time Travels without making mistakes.

info.desc: Test your skills with strategic game mechanics.
info.name: Strategy Helix: MBP

info.desc: Beginner MBP styled level. Enjoy!
info.name: Structure Climber

info.awesomehint: Get 100% in the first section. Then, think about how you can get the rest of the four gems required to finish.
info.desc: Stroll your way through this filmographic lane.
info.egghint: Where do spectators go to get celebrities' autographs?
info.generalhint: You can either dash through the studio or stop to see every stage set. Your choice.
info.name: Studiopolis
info.starthelptext: Lights, Camera, Action!
info.trivia: The music in this level is a vinyl record of Studiopolis Act 1 from Sonic Mania.
info.ultimatehint: Try entering the fastest areas.

info.awesomehint: Keep your speed high and work around obstacles that may slow you down. Cutting corners wherever possible will help too.
info.desc: Rush around this sweet racetrack!
info.generalhint: If you are caught in the upper molasses swamps, keep jumping! The sticky syrup makes it almost impossible to control your marble.
info.name: Sugar Rush
info.ultimatehint: Snag every Time Travel that you can. Working on your ring stunts will help a lot, and so will mastering your landings off of the mountain. If you can quickly make it up the mountain with only one super speed, that will save you several seconds each lap.

info.desc:
Special Level ('Suomi 100'): Finland's 100th anniversary of independence.
[Level released 2017-12-06]

Worried by developments in Russia and Finland, the non-Socialist Senate proposed that Parliament declare Finland's independence, which was voted by the Parliament on December 6, 1917.
On December 18 (December 31 N. S.) the Soviet government issued a Decree, recognizing Finland's independence, and on December 22 (January 4, 1918 N. S.) it was approved by the highest Soviet executive body (VTsIK). Germany and the Scandinavian countries followed without delay. [Wikipedia]
info.name: Suomi 100
Super Manic Bounce
info.generalhint: Cry. Cry a lot.
info.artist: Oaky, Uil, & Threefolder - edited by HiGuy
info.starthelptext: STAYING CALM WON'T HELP YOU ANYMORE!!
info.desc: Because of course the original was too easy for you, right?
Through the hanging pipes we go!
info.generalhint: Take it easy.
info.name: Suspended Pipeline
info.starthelptext: Cool-colored pipes are easy while the red pipes are harder but faster.
info.ultimatehint: Use the red pipes.

info.desc: Time is really screwed up today, wonder what happend to the clock?
info.name: Time's Screwed Up!
info.starthelptext: The clock is so screwed up, it still works when you finish the level and before you start the level

info.awesomehint: Sometimes losing something good actually benefits you in the end.
info.desc: Now you can be Sonic in this simple level!
info.egghint: Eggy likes to sit on the grass under something that blocks the sun.
info.generalhint: Go fast.
info.name: Teleporting Run
info.starthelptext: Oooo! moving asteroids.
info.ultimatehint: I like to go down.

info.awesomehint: At the beginning, there's a little tweak to save some seconds, and you don't even need the help of the bumpers.
info.desc: You gotta be fast, here, you don't have much time!
info.generalhint: Use the cannons to travel to the fourth floor! Keep in mind there are Time Travels scattering around that will considerably help you during this task.
info.name: The Fourth Floor
info.starthelptext: Your jumps will be disabled as soon as you enter the marked area and will be retablished when you enter the cannon.
info.ultimatehint: Some parts can be skipped, can you guess which ones?

info.desc: The night is falling, just like your safety on those fading platforms. Plus it's getting late. Finish the level quickly or your mom is gonna get mad at you again!
info.generalhint: Master the various fading platform challenges. A good sense of timing and platform managing will surely come in handy, as sometimes you must leave some platforms to make your way back.
info.name: The Night Falls
info.starthelptext: As you're going to see, the fading platforms will have different colors, therefore, different functions.
info.trivia:
This level was supposed to be called "Fading Madness", but you know... name originality. Plus there's not many night levels in PQ (by that, I mean real dark night levels, unlike Bag of Secrets and Miscalculation). 
 
Originally, the level was supposed to feature moving fading platforms. Here 's three reasons why it didn't happened: 
 
1) The number of PathNodes would make the whole level lag violently

info.trivia:
This level was originally made for Marble Blast Elite, before being the fourth Naturous level of Marble Blast GLC. The mines here are replaced with ice shards, the windows are actually present in the original MBE version, as well as the treetrunk that was replacing trapdoors in the GLC version. Unfortunately, the crates are still static as PQ does not have crates. The mud half pipe was made by just rotating platforms and the bouncy stairs was originally invisible floors. I must emphasize that this level was intended to be very hard, but still beatable. I make it more reasonably beatable here with two checkpoints.

Original Trivia from GLC:
Made on Christmas 2012, and inspired by Donkey Kong series. This level intentionally made for really hard difficulty, so you will need to complete this level in one go. This level is very hard, and sometimes frustrating, but that was intentionally done. Fast MP and dodging stuff also refers to Touhou unintentionally too.

info.desc:
Everyone loves windmills. Perfectly fitting to a landscape, satistfying when spinning. 
But are they still satistfying and pleasant when they are on your way to the finish? Will your marble blend? Like would have said Tom Dickson, that is the question!
info.generalhint: Get across a riddle of wooden windmills spinning more or less faster. Timing and precision is needed for a level that is sure to spin your head (or make you go "smh", you choose).
info.name: Want some Windmills?
info.starthelptext: The level's design should be familiar to you.
info.trivia:
The title of the level is a rough translation of a french title of a level from King of Clubs, a mini-golf game I used to camp when I was a little bit younger, and it was on the Wii. 
 
The title is "Tu veux des moulins ?" (this is also a good way to see who has the worst french accent). This level had 3 windmills, spinning faster than their predecessors, and the player had to time his putt to make a jump across a gap without being bruh'd or slammed by a windmill.
 
The third windmill was particularly hard to cross, since it was spinning as fast as my washer. Now this level inspired me, and I decided, after a few experiments, to use the same design Training Wheels has. The ending originally had 5 WHOOPIN' WINDMILLS (the one before the finish excluded) to get through on the moving platforms, and I finally thought this would be too harsh as a final challenge, so I sticked with only two, spinning at high speeds.
info.ultimatehint: Don't let any of those windmills stop you. In any way.

info.trivia: This remake has been an idea way before PlatinumQuest was released. I needed to make sure the pipes were used more often by increasing the amount of pipes from eight to forty-eight. Openness was another thing that was taken into consideration, so that the remake feels less like a corridor than the original. For these aspects and a few more, this remake feels like a significant improvement over the original.
info.ultimatehint: The pipes won't be your only means of navigation if you're going for the ultimate score. You may need to use powerups and come up with strategies using them. Again, Time Travels can really benefit in the amount of time needed to grab the gems.

info.trivia:
This version of the level is currently exclusive to the leaderboards. Among the following list of changes from the previous version is the reason this version exists.

-The first section now has inversion floors. To learn more about them, play 'Gravitationalism'.
-All the gems are now red instead of being random colors every visit.
-Slightly adjusted geometry in the grass islands.
-The faded platforms are now yellow and they don't fade to white this time.
-The arc where the third gem is has better texturing.
-The colmesh at the bowl is removed.
-The reason for this version's existence: The purple bump texture is replaced with a mud texture. This is because HiGuy didn't want to work with custom friction code. He and the others working on Packs 60-69 suggested that the purple bump texture should be replaced with something else.
info.ultimatehint: There are Time Travels hidden in the natural areas. Use the radar to pinpoint them.

info.awesomehint: There are two windmills that you can walk on. Each of them have a Time Travel with 10 seconds of time bonus. Grabbing both is guaranteed to give you an Awesome time. You can also skip half of the loop line using a bumper hit. Can you figure out how?
info.desc: Make your way past the sails of each windmill without letting them shove you away.
info.egghint: You can find it where you would usually find an egg's nest.
info.generalhint: This is a tough level. The sails spin fast enough that you have very little reaction time to pass through them. However, nothing about their patterns is random. It really boils down to having good timing. If you fall off the main path, which will lead you to the town, respawn to the last checkpoint you hit using the respawn key. It is also important to remember that because it is a tough level, nothing is wrong with going slowly, unless you're going for the Ultimate or Awesome times.
info.name: Mykonundrum
info.starthelptext: Time your movements carefully to make it past the sails.
info.trivia:
The level's theme is based off of the Greek city of Mykonos, and the windmills are based off of Apotos from Sonic Unleashed. The main gimmick of this level takes inspiration from 'Wan't Some Windmills?' by Ralph.

The level itself also used to be longer, with two more gravity sections, another windmill intersection, a low gravity section where you go down another tower while avoiding obstacles, etc. The download for this level contains all of the interiors, including the ones that were cut from the final product.
info.ultimatehint: Going fast is one thing, but maintaining your speed while doing so in order to pass the sails is another. Hitting the bumpers in the sections that have them can lead to potential shortcuts. Plenty of Time Travels are also within reach, with one of them in a section you can reach using a shortcut.

remarks:

Not even a real Ultra level. Take that.

Original release: 01/23/15

info.desc: Put your agility to the test with this small course.
info.egghint: Skip the ice stairs.
info.generalhint: Get a feel for the ice section and the gem in mid-air between the two slopes before you start to shoot for a really good time.
info.name: Rozi's Short Skill Course
info.trivia: This level originally had a third part to it, which looked like a very blocky diamond shape. It wasn't built very well, and thankfully you don't have to play it.
info.ultimatehint: The small optimizations are key, like jumping as few times as you can on the ice stairs and collecting the first four gems in a counter-clockwise direction, starting with the one on the right.

remarks:
What's the best way to name a level when you can't think of anything good to call it?

Original release: 02/01/15

info.desc: The ultimate test of control and balance.
info.egghint: Can you keep a helicopter until the end?
info.generalhint: Obviously tightropes should be taken slowly until you're more comfortable with them, but do take advantage of the checkpoints so you can replay parts for practice.
info.name: Tightrope Monster Course
info.trivia: The brown obelisks that you see everywhere around the level were made specifically for decorating this level, almost ironically.
info.ultimatehint: The Time Travels aren't necessary, but they do help a lot. You can fall off several times and still get Ultimate, so no need to worry about getting the perfect run.

remarks:
Made purely out of irony, but a fair bit of it is surprisingly playable. I'd love to revisit this sometime and upset the entire community again.

Original release: 02/01/15

info.desc: When one sense is lost, the others are strengthened.
info.generalhint: Your run should be very fluid. Try to avoid stopping as much as you can.
info.name: Rainbow Flats
info.starthelptext: How willing are you to cut corners if you can't jump?
info.trivia: The first version of this level ended right before the sloped bouncy part. Only later did it become a full circuit.
info.ultimatehint: You can totally take the chance on some edge hits for some tiny skips if you'd like.

remarks:
Really just wanted an excuse to use these rainbow textures.

Original release: 02/01/15

info.desc: See what lies in this waterfall.
info.egghint: We know there's something in the waterfall... how about behind?
info.generalhint: Get the higher gem first.
info.name: Waterfall
info.ultimatehint: You should only need one gyrocopter.

remarks:
"Fun with Marble Mini Golf" (or maybe the two M's were the other way around?) was the original title until I decided this level wasn't fun enough for that. Not even a Marble Mini Golf level anyway.

Original release: 02/01/15

info.desc: So many weird angles and maneuvers... you may never want to see a pipe again!
info.generalhint: This is a difficult one. The more awkward parts are in the first half of the level, so things get easier later on.
info.name: Expertubes
info.trivia: The skybox is from Marble Blast Powered Up, more specifically from Grander Finale.

remarks:
My second attempt at a pipe level which ended up not really being as much of a pipe level as it could be. Maybe this just isn't my thing. Somehow one of my hardest levels to date.

Original release: 03/22/15

info.desc: Find the best path, but beware of the hazards!
info.egghint: A Gyrocopter and a Super Jump...
info.generalhint: Take advantage of the PowerUps, especially in the more hazardous areas.
info.name: Path Seeker
info.trivia: The redesign added basically all of the scenery that you can see, and the ice slope used to be a swirl-like shape much like what's found in Mobius Strip.
info.ultimatehint: You can pretty much just go from area to area and get a solid time. Try not to lose too much time from the tornados and fans.

remarks:
Originally made for the PC port, and then I figured out it was bad and made it better.

Original release: 04/21/15

info.desc: Use the floating blocks to reach the towers.
info.generalhint: Finding ways to quickly get from one tower to another is most important. Use those PowerUps!
info.name: Cracked Blocks
info.trivia: The model in the window is the old version of this level, which played pretty tragically in comparison to what this level is now.
info.ultimatehint: A gyrocopter and your blast is the best tool for travel. If you're feeling brave, go for some spawn abusing.

remarks:
The old version of this level can be found behind a window in one of the towers.

Original release: 05/25/15

info.desc: Can't really be any simpler than this.
info.egghint: Past the finish!
info.generalhint: Use the checkpoint at the hazard section if you want some practice with the ending.
info.name: Generic Ascent
info.trivia: Formerly known as "Memories".
info.ultimatehint: The first section before the stairs can be done with two wall hits, and take the hazard section in a counter-clockwise motion.

remarks:
Yes, the name is completely ironic.

Original release: 07/04/15

info.desc: There's nothing here that's too complicated. Maybe a little difficult though.
info.egghint:
Can you get to the top without the teleporter? 
Return to the start pad if you do not see the egg.
info.generalhint: The top teleporter takes you to the finish, the middle one takes you to the ramp area above the start, and the bottom teleporter takes you to the tightrope area. Use the teleporters at the end of each section to return to the start.
info.name: Basic Control Course
info.starthelptext: Save the top floor teleporter for last! It spawns you right before the finish!
info.trivia: There only used to be the "main" part of this level before the tightrope and ramp sections were added only for the sake of pathfinding.
info.ultimatehint: The optimal path doesn't use any of the teleporters. It's not needed for Ultimate Time, but it helps.

remarks:
Not much of this has anything to do with testing your control. Just the tightropes and that's it.

Original release: 08/21/15

info.desc: Make your way through this winding path.
info.egghint: There's no doubt that being able to get on top of the level will get you somewhere.
info.generalhint: Nothing too confusing or too challenging. Do what you think you have to do; this should be easy enough.
info.name: Cocoa Roads
info.trivia: It's pretty clear that the name and build style was inspired by Phil's Choco Valley. It's also pretty clear that said level is in a completely different league than this one.
info.ultimatehint: The easiest shortcut skips half of the ice section. That should be more than enough for you.

remarks:
Can you see the influence from "Choco Valley"?

Original release: 08/29/15

info.desc: Find the gems on the towering pillars, using the half pipe to gain height.
info.egghint: No reason not to try and go for a little height when you have a half pipe. Be careful though, as the egg is just on the border of the Bounds trigger!
info.generalhint: Shoot for the highest gems so you can drop down to the remaining ones.
info.name: Half-Pipe - Pillars
info.starthelptext: Those PowerUps on the other side of the half pipe might come in use...
info.trivia: Inspired by "Halfpipe X" from Marble Blast Advanced.
info.ultimatehint: Ideally, you use the half pipe three times. Twice to get the gems - one set of four on each side - and once more to finish.

remarks:
Inspired by "Halfpipe X" from Marble Blast Advanced.

Original release: 11/01/15

info.desc: Test your fundamental marbling skills on this towering course.
info.egghint: Slide behind a wall make your way up from the bottom again.
info.generalhint: There's nothing here that should be a challenge for a beginner player to do, so you're best bet for improving your time is simply optimizing.
info.name: Rozi's Basic Skill Course
info.ultimatehint: No fancy tricks needed! Get all the Time Travels and do your best not to fall.

remarks:
Often confused with "Rozi's Short Skill Course" for obvious reason. This is the far superior level though.

Original release: 11/11/15

info.desc: Signs can actually do more than just point in the direction you should be headed.
info.egghint: It appears in your path right after the Super Jump. However, it disappears if you touch any signs. You'll have to get creative.
info.generalhint: Without a doubt, the toughest part of the level is the sign "bridge". Fortunately, there's a checkpoint right before it. If you're feeling experimental, try to pass through it in the other direction.
info.name: Super Signs
info.trivia: This level was inspired by "Mirror Supreme" from NaCl586's "Gerson's Level Compilation".
info.ultimatehint: Ultimate Time shouldn't be difficult at all. This is a pretty straightforward level, despite there being other paths that exist.

remarks:
Inspired by "Signs Supreme" from Gerson's Level Compilation.

Original release: 12/20/15

info.desc: Ascend this skyscraper with care.
info.egghint: There are arrows pointing to a trigger that will uncover the egg. You won't be rolling on the normal platforms though.
info.generalhint: Take each part as slowly as you need to. There are four different checkpoints, so don't be worried about losing too much progress at once.
info.name: Construction Tower
info.starthelptext: Luckily for you, everything is stable to travel on.
info.trivia: This level had one of the heaviest makeovers since its original release. The texturing and building were a completely different style, and the current look was inspired by Blasted's Progression 2.
info.ultimatehint: No massive shortcuts here, only some small tricks. Skip the curved trim at the beginning, get the gems and Time Travel on the swaying platform in one motion, and jump off the moving platforms as soon as you can.

remarks:
Had a massive facelift and absolutely needed it. General aesthetic inspired by Blasted's "Progression 2".

Original release: 03/19/16

info.desc: Keep your footing on this small platforming challenge.
info.egghint: The most isolated part of the level has a secret entrance.
info.generalhint: Practice your control while continuously jumping and keep your balance on the red platforms.
info.name: Towering
info.trivia: This level went through four different makeovers until the final output came to be.
info.ultimatehint: The Time Travel on the slope is definitely helpful. The most efficient way of getting it is jumping right before the bouncy floor on the curved slope, to save height.

remarks:
The red blocks didn't move in the original version (I learned how to make triggered moving platforms five years later), but I just wanted an excuse to show off a bit.

Original release: 04/28/16

info.desc: Keep your footing on this simple course.
info.egghint: It's very easy to find! Too bad you can't get to it by just jumping though.
info.generalhint: Don't fall off? Not much more to it than that. Time spent not beating the level tends to not be good.
info.name: Beginner Twist
info.trivia: Since the version in the 50-59 leaderboards pack, a 3 second Time Travel was removed, a checkpoint was added, signs appeared out of nowhere, and a few texturing changes were made to make the level look like an actual friendly beginner level.
info.ultimatehint: I smell a tasty hidden Time Travel somewhere...

remarks:
Was originally part of a collaboration with BPXRockU, but that never happened.

Original release: 04/28/16

info.desc: Run through this quick and easy course while collecting the Time Travels to minimize your time!
info.egghint: The best way to get height is to make down a different direction.
info.generalhint: You can use the top of the pipes to your advantage.
info.name: Red Skill
info.trivia: There used to be an awful red tint to the screen while playing this level to ridiculously emphasize the red theme.
info.ultimatehint: Get the Super Jump before the last gem.

remarks:
The original plan was for this to be the first part of a three-piece level (the original name of the interior was called "TrioRed"), but the other two parts were never built.

Original release: 07/23/16

info.desc: Part of the MBSuper Lost Levels pack. (1/3)
info.egghint: Get to the top of the level! The easiest method of doing so is given away in the level preview.
info.generalhint: Getting in an out of the box area will probably take the most practice. Get the gems in counter-clockwise motion.
info.name: Gem Playground
info.trivia:
One of two levels started by Endy in the level pack. The other is Little Climb of Fate. 

There is a typo in the interior file, but this was intentional as the typo was there when the level was originally abandoned.
info.ultimatehint: Just focus on small tweaks for optimization, like cutting as much time spent between getting the first gem and the pair of gems, or activating the Super Speed at the end as soon as possible.

remarks:
The first of three levels in the MBSuper Lost Levels pack. Typo in the interior file name is intentional.

Original release: 07/23/16

info.desc: Part of the MBSuper Lost Levels pack. (2/3)
info.egghint: Skip every gem but the last one.
info.generalhint: Just practice each section. The sign hit isn't as bad as it could look.
info.name: Little Climb of Fate
info.starthelptext: Can you figure out the puzzles?
info.trivia:
One of two levels started by Endy in the level pack. The other is Gem Playground. 

This level was originally called Lavender Climb of Fate.
info.ultimatehint: The best timesave is skipping the sign hit with an edge hit before it.

remarks:
The second of three levels in the MBSuper Lost Levels pack. The original was called "Lavender Climb of Faith", but the interior was simply named "lcof" and there was no chance of me guessing what the L stood for.

Original release: 07/23/16

info.desc: Part of the MBSuper Lost Levels pack. (3/3)
info.egghint: One of the holes has another secret hole.
info.generalhint: Everything is very straightforward. It's okay to backtrack to get whichever of the gems in the second-to-last pair you may not have picked up going forward.
info.name: Rolling Gold
info.trivia: This was started by Nockess and was originally going to be featured in Rozi's Mini Mod.
info.ultimatehint: Doing an edge hit at the start can be a really helpful way to save time, but not necessary.

remarks:
The third of three levels in the MBSuper Lost Levels pack. Meant to be included in Rozi's Mini Mod at first, but the heavy difference in style prevented that from happening.

Original release: 07/23/16

info.desc: Pass through all the different scenes of this sky land!
info.generalhint: There are four Time Travels in the first section, seven in the second, three in the third, and one in the last. Find as many of them as you can to cut down as much time as possible!
info.name: Sky City
info.starthelptext: There are plenty of Time Travels you can find to lower your time as much as possible!
info.trivia: This is a scrapped level from Rozi's Mini Mod. The interior was made by Lee.

remarks:
A scrapped level from Rozi's Mini Mod, but a really cool showcase of Lee's level building talent.

Original release: 09/25/16

info.desc: It's not much of a challenge to get to the finish, but how fast are you able to do it?
info.egghint: How high can you go?
info.generalhint: This is a decent level to practice spin control while holding down the jump button.
info.name: Novice Tower
info.trivia: The interior was at first built four times too big. It took until well after the original release to fix this.
info.ultimatehint: Double Super Jump!

remarks:
Another situation where the original version didn't have moving platforms, but after I figured out how make them, the easter egg came to be.

Original release: 10/25/16

info.desc: Find the quickest path in this simple course!
info.generalhint: No Time Travels here or any reason to do super fancy tricks. You can be pretty casual about this one.
info.name: Branches
info.ultimatehint: The optimal path generally goes in a clockwise direction, starting with the gem to the left of the start pad.

remarks:
May or may not have been made to sneak into packs 50-59. Clearly that didn't work out.

Original release: 02/23/17

info.desc: There's much to do here. How long will it take you to explore this?
info.egghint: Find your way to the top.
info.generalhint: The radar is absolutely your best friend. Since you know where the gems are, remember where the PowerUps are!
info.name: Hunter's Pursuit
info.starthelptext: It will probably take you a few tries to find a path that will get you a good time. Don't get discouraged!
info.trivia: This level is dedicated to RadiantVibe in efforts to bring more attention to his phenomenal ability to pathfind.
info.ultimatehint: There's a lot of trial and error involved in finding a good path. Use all the PowerUps you need, but don't go too far out of your way to get one.

remarks:
A dedication to RadiantVibe since his pathfinding ability is almost unparalleled.

Original release: 06/21/17

info.awesomehint: Go straight to the bouncy floor after using the anvil and the super bounce. Collect the gem you pass after the gyrocopter section.
info.desc: With a little perserverance, you can bounce back from any mistake.
info.egghint: You know where it is. The entrance isn't too far away. It's just hidden well.
info.generalhint: This level may take a little bit to get used to, so take as much time as you need with each wall-hit.
info.name: Rebound
info.starthelptext: How can you use your wall-hitting skills to get to the finish?
info.trivia: Nockess' first PlatinumQuest level!
info.ultimatehint: The key to getting a solid time is simply getting the hang of each part of the level. Once you're at that point, getting Ultimate Time shouldn't be any trouble.

remarks:
My first PlatinumQuest level!

Original release: 08/27/17

info.awesomehint: Finish by going to the small island and using the cannon after getting the gems there. The rest of the path should be easy to figure out.
info.desc: Hidden in the midst of layers of fog.
info.egghint: What happens when you go in backwards?
info.generalhint: There's not much in terms of harmful here. Explore the level a little bit and see where everything is.
info.name: Secret Island
info.ultimatehint: Try to go to the highest gem last. Look around for some hidden Time Travels as well.

remarks:
I really just wanted an excuse to make a level with the windows. This ended up being one of my favorite levels.

Download a less-graphic-intensive version here:
https://bit.ly/3enEClB

Original release: 12/16/18

info.awesomehint: That curved ramp will do a lot for you. So will an edge hit later on.
info.desc: This is based around speed, but going too fast will send you off the edge.
info.generalhint: Just don't be careless. It isn't rocket science.
info.name: Slope Streak
info.ultimatehint: Making as few stops as possible will be enough to get Ultimate.

remarks:
One of my more simpler creations in recent times.

Original release: 12/22/18

info.awesomehint: Your best opportunity for a skip is using the Super Jump at the broken bridge at the end to the next Super Jump. Other than that, optimize!
info.desc: Climb out of the freezing cold gorge. There may be a nice welcoming at the top.
info.egghint: Take a look at the festivity, won't ya?
info.generalhint: Take it slow to begin with, and better times will come with experience and comfortability.
info.name: Frost Ravine
info.starthelptext: Your footing is crucial here. Parts of the path are very slippery and dangerous, so stay in control!
info.ultimatehint: Same as above, but just be better.

remarks:
Inspired by "The Frozen Gorge" from Fubar. Intended to release this on Christmas, but I ended up doing a lot more with this level than I had planned.

Original release: 12/29/18

info.desc: You should know all of these levels pretty well if you've played much of Marble Blast Gold. The real question is how good are you at keeping your pace?
info.generalhint: Pretty straightforward. There are a handful of checkpoints that'll make this level easier to get the hang of. Don't miss those Time Travels!
info.name: Marble Blast Gold Mashup
info.starthelptext: How many levels do you recognize?

remarks:
My attempt to recreate a handful of Gold levels from scratch!

Original release: 01/15/19

info.awesomehint: At the very least, you can get Awesome Time by doing an edge hit after the first ice section to skip a couple seconds, and then nailing the optimization on the rest.
info.desc: The infamous Director's Cut level has gotten even longer.
info.egghint: The arches aren't there just to be decorative.
info.generalhint: Everything is pretty straightforward. The best way to get through the icy parts is to jump right to the flat platforms and skip the slopes.
info.name: Widow's Peak Extended
info.ultimatehint: Cutting as many corners as you can will help you a lot.

remarks:
First a recreation and then an extension. If I had known how to make moving platforms at the time, I probably would've included those too.

Original release: 03/19/19

info.awesomehint: It's all about finding a consistent jump pattern. You can start off by continuously jumping off the start pad and using the Super Speed at the second slope.
info.desc: Keep your momentum in this uphill battle.
info.generalhint: Try not to go too slow if you want the best time. Use the Super Speed wisely.
info.name: Run to the Top
info.ultimatehint: Shoot for less bouncing on the slopes and more gliding on them.

remarks: Original release: 04/28/19

info.awesomehint: You can get Awesome Time doing the full path, but your optimization has to be really good. Alternatively, you could skip a whole room...
info.desc: Find your way out of this massive cavern.
info.egghint: Ignore the barriers.
info.generalhint: Try to keep a somewhat fluid run. Stopping and slowing down won't help but you can at least get away with it a couple times before you go for a better result.
info.name: Cavern of Cannons
info.trivia: This level first went under development nearly two years before it was released. Procrastination is a wonderful life style.
info.ultimatehint: One of the more unexpected tactits for getting a lower time is deciding whether you should jump on an upward slope or not when managing your speed.

remarks:
A two-year project that was just some eye candy at first, until it turned into something much more spectacular. The original concept was to chase gems after being shot out of the cannons, but the gameplay was fun enough already by the time the level was at the state you see it now.

Original release: 08/20/19

info.awesomehint: Get all the time travels, use Powerups to get to higher platforms quickly, but go faster this time.
info.desc: It's kind of cramped.
info.egghint: Find an opening in some wall that's hard to get to and you'll be teleported where that circular window is. Pretty simple (and generic).
info.generalhint: Don't fall off, take advantage of the checkpoint if needed, and get the higher gems last.
info.name: Cluttered Assortment
info.starthelptext: Mind the trim when you use a Super Jump to go to a higher platform.
info.trivia: This level is a mashup of parts from some custom levels for Marble Blast Ultra.
info.ultimatehint: Get all the time travels, use Powerups to get to higher platforms quickly, and go fast.

remarks:
A mashup of several custom levels from the Marble Blast Ultra PC Port.

Original release: 12/26/19

info.awesomehint: The most important part is making sure you waste as little time in the air as possible, so with 10 gems and a Super Jump in the middle, you shouldn't bounce more than 11 times.
info.desc: Bounce around in a giant bowl made of platforms.
info.egghint: Just a little higher...
info.generalhint: Think about the direction you'll be going after you bounce and look where you're going. Abuse that Super Jump if you need to.
info.name: Ricochet Funnel
info.starthelptext: You can bounce a lot higher than you normally can, and that's without a Super Bounce. Be careful!
info.trivia:
It took upwards of have a dozen different methods to get the interior finally converted. Map2Dif really had a wonderful time with this one. 
49 different files. Oh boy. 

Tested by DKman00 and Xedron.
info.ultimatehint: Use the roof to your advantage when you finish. Try to have as little airtime as possible. Save the Super Jump for the end when you go back up.

remarks:
I've always wanted to make a level like this, but just a normal bowl doesn't give for a whole lot of gameplay. I thought this would be a much more fun concept.

Original release: 05/18/20

info.desc: Use caution as you climb to the top of the tower through the mess of this construction.
info.generalhint: This is all just a long platforming channel with nothing too complex. Follow the path, and take your time until you're comfortable.
info.name: Scaffold Scramble
info.trivia: Before this was turned into a construction-themed level, this was styled after the two "Ascent of Peril" levels by Xelna, with the idea of mixing the two and seeing how closely certain parts could be recreated.

remarks:
In the early stages of building, this was an attempt to recreate Xelna's two "Ascent of Peril" levels and mash them together, but then I wanted to try my hand at making an construction-themed level for Gold and eventually sculpted this.

Original release: 10/18/20

info.awesomehint: As far as major shortcuts go, there really isn't much. However, there are several instances where you can cut off a couple seconds at a time. Fortunately, there aren't any super difficult stunts to pull off.
info.desc: You've probably seen all of this before, although this time there's a lot more to pay attention to. Thankfully, you don't have to read all the names anymore.
info.egghint: Go farther than intended! Threefolder will help you on your way.
info.generalhint: Go slow! This isn't the easiest of levels, so take your time feeling this one out.
info.name: Closer to Freedom
info.starthelptext: Rewind the credits!
info.trivia: This level is built around the interior you see during the credits after beating Manic Bounce.
info.ultimatehint: Nothing too out of the ordinary with this one. Do your best not to fall, and make sure you get all the Time Travels. They can go a long way!

remarks:
A rare sight of a level editor made only with PQ stock interiors and shapes.

Original release: 01/14/21

info.awesomehint: Not much you can skip here. There might be a gyrocopter you missed that may come in handy. If you're feeling really brave, get the first sideways gem before switching gravity.
info.desc: Manic Bounce isn't as... frightening anymore.
info.egghint: Where one has slept before.
info.generalhint: Take your time when you need to. You can fall off a few times and still earn Platinum. If you want to shoot for lower, practice the end section as it's a little more difficult than the rest of the level.
info.name: Lack of Mania
info.starthelptext: It's different from the normal path this time around.
info.trivia: Matan's "Pass It Yourself" levels were the main inspiration here.The final output didn't quite end up being as closely designed as it was originally headed towards, the similarities are still noticeable.
info.ultimatehint: Get those Time Travels! There are quite a few of them, although some of them are difficult to collect. You can still comfortably get Ultimate if you miss a couple.

remarks:
This was first going to basically be "Manic Bounce - Pass It Yourself", and to an extent that's still the case, but not as start-to-finish as the original level is.

Original release: 01/17/21

info.awesomehint: You can go straight to the second cannon from the first.
info.desc: Bend around the wall back to safety.
info.egghint: Probably the only time where hitting the wall is better than avoiding it.
info.generalhint: To an extent, aiming your cannon farther away from the wall can actually make it a bit easier to land on the next platform.
info.name: Curve
info.starthelptext: The ideal areas to land on are the ones with wooden borders on either side of the platform.
info.ultimatehint: Spend as little time as you can in the cannos, especially given that you only have to adjust on one axis.

remarks:
Bend it like Beckham!

Original release: 01/27/21

info.awesomehint: Getting to the cannon with the lower half of the gems and about 20 seconds of real time passed will set you up nicely for Awesome Time. Skip the loop to the finish and just go around the wall.
info.desc: Get to the high ground.
info.egghint: It should be obvious where to go first. A small hole will open afterwards.
info.generalhint: Fortunately nothing here is too complicated, maybe just a little difficult at first. Some parts may need practice but this should be a pretty easy job.
info.name: Divided High
info.starthelptext: Wall-hit your way up! Nowhere in particular you need to land, just have enough speed!
info.trivia: Remember Dividing Flight?
info.ultimatehint: The first half of the level before the cannon is really the only part that involves some actual pathfinding. Get that figured out and the rest should be simple enough.

remarks:
Tried to make something kind of like Dividing Flight. Didn't turn out to be nearly as neat-looking of a level, but at least those curves look nice.

Original release: 02/20/21

info.desc: Weave through this winding level, or find a path that breaks it all.
info.generalhint: The most dangerous parts of the levels are the ones where you have to avoid moving blocks, so take as much time as you need with those.
info.name: Elevation Entwinement
info.trivia: Another one of Nockess' old levels that was started years before completion. At first, this was a level made for Platinum and used a handful of the black and gray textures, hence the original name "Grayscale".

remarks:
Another scrapped project from years ago that was pulled out of the junkyard and made into something much lovelier than it was before.

Winner of Level of the Year 2021.

Original release: 04/02/21

info.desc: An innocent multiplayer map turned into something much more fitting.
info.egghint: Curved ramp! Go super fast!
info.generalhint: No need to do anything too fancy. Going from area to area will do just fine.
info.name: Past Over
info.trivia: Previously named "Kassera", which roughly translates to "discarded". Now a play on words of "passed over"
info.ultimatehint: Get to the high ground early, and finish with the ice section.

info.name: Spin Doctor
info.starthelptext: You'll get very little help here; your eyes and brain will be your guide. Good luck!
info.trivia:
I've been sitting on some of these ideas for almost three years, following the release of Spin Class. The creation process was unique for me: I made the entire level in the LE using the stock MBP building block interiors, to facilitate rapid-fire testing, and then I remade it in Constructor afterwards. Incidentally, I have no idea why the random force platform interior is so horribly misaligned; it was a good test of my mental math skills every time I had to rescale one of them and adjust the positional coordinates accordingly.

Some complex path trigger techniques are used to de-cheese the section with the SS and SJ. To see what I mean, try skipping either the 8th or the 9th gem and then going back for it. It's still possible, but I've made it way harder - and much slower - than doing the level normally.
info.ultimatehint: If you can beat the level without respawns, you can pretty much go as slow as you want. If not... you might struggle.

info.desc: I'm so sorry.
info.name: Redemption

remarks:
I don't care if I'm banned. This level has a story behind it that I want to share.

I joined the Marble Blast community around February 2017. hPerks was one of the first people I've ever talked to in the community, and he quickly became my best friend. I loved him with every fiber of my being and he loved me too. He helped me in so many ways and taught me how to be a better person. I always looked up to him and his kindness, wit, charm. Every day, I thought about how happy I was to have him in my life. Even after we both left the community, I still talked to him a lot, and he continued to support me and be my best friend for five years. He was truly irreplaceable to me. He wasn't just a friend to me, but family, and forever a part of my soul.

In October 2017, I falsified a There and Back Again time of 9.732, which ended up being added to the leaderboards. This wasn't a smart thing for me to do, but I was very naive at the time. After more than two years of hiding this secret from my best friend, someone who I knew took honesty & Marble Blast seriously, I finally confessed it to him. He wasn't upset with me. We talked about it, cracked a few jokes, and we then continued on. I always thought about sitting down and grinding out TaBA to beat my cheated time, but never did.

What happened 10 days ago, I can't put it into words.

This level is a direct copy of There and Back Again, but with a Qualify Time of 9.732 and some extra interiors that serve as decoration. I intended to keep playing this level until I successfully beaten that time. After 16 minutes of attempts, I fluked it and got 8.965. It's finally over. I sat and cried.

I can finally feel peace and relief for finishing what I've started. I can now forgive myself for what I've done in the past.
Rest in peace, Owen. I love you so fucking much. - Kathryn

The ice area has, what else, ice, coupled with shards and a water section with two Bubble PowerUps. info.generalhint: There is a fire area and an ice area. Both of them have Fireballs and other PowerUps to help you. But there are some differences between the two. The fire area has lava that acts as a bouncy floor and has high friction, along with land mines scattered about. The ice area has, what else, ice, coupled with shards and a water section with two Bubble PowerUps. Use the Fireballs to launch you up to higher ground when you don't have a Super Jump with you, but beware that the effect for each of them lasts for 7 seconds.
info.name: Requisite
info.trivia: The level name, 'Requisite', is a synonym for the phrase 'fire and ice'. The level's layout and structure is similar to that of Jumphouse from Marble It Up: Mayhem! Each area has a different shade of glass in the windows. The fire area has a lighter shade, the ice area has a darker shade, while the center area has the base skin. The lava texture in this level is the same one seen in the level 'Blazing Margherita' by Ralph.

info.starthelptext: None of the PowerUps or Fade Platforms here respawn.
info.trivia:
I decided to make this level when I saw Mario Kart Tour's GBA Sky Garden and decided that it sucked, so I made my own, inspired by both. Namely the U-turn with the ramp in MKSC and MKDS that was replaced with a simple mushroom was what really set me off.

For the turn that goes around the island with the house on it, I originally wanted to have a wall connecting the track to the island similar to the wall under the last U-turn but vertical. I also wanted to have a fence on the inside of the turn with flowers under it to reference both its appearance in Mario Kart Tour and the wall that's there in Super Circuit, but both of these proved to be too complicated, and I just didn't do it. Would've been nice, though.

This level was also made and released for playtesting before this track was added to Mario Kart 8 Deluxe. I was just lazy and took forever to properly finish it. I didn't know that the Tour and Deluxe version had a shortcut on the last turn before, either, so that's cool that this shares that. Also makes me less mad at the simplifications since it's really just the bouncy mushroom that I think is oversimplified now. No justice for GBA Cheep Cheep Island, though, they absolutely ruined that course.
info.ultimatehint:
The first two Time Travels with the targets require Super Speeds to get to, like the nearby signs say. Use them wisely! The first is easiest to collect by jumping off of the ramp before using the Super Speed, while the second is easier to collect by using the Super Speed on the ramp and simply rolling.

The two Time Travels at the very end of the lap can be collected by bouncing off of the blue ramp that precedes them.

remarks:
A combination of the old MKSC/MKDS and new MKT (and later MK8DX after the making of this level) versions of Sky Garden. Inspired by me thinking the level was oversimplified and making my own out of spite.

2022-04-07 [v2] Nerfed the AT by 5 seconds.

info.desc: In mathematics, a square is the result of multiplying a number by itself, or raising to the power of 2. How well do you know your squares?
info.generalhint: As you'd expect, you have to use your mathematic skills to enter the correct squares. Any value that is the product of two identical numbers being multiplied by each other has a gem inside and thus, is the correct answer. Any incorrect square will blow you away. The three squares with the clock emblem each have a Time Travel with 5 seconds of time bonus. Also, there is no time limit. So you can take as much time as you need to solve this Nukesweeper game, while using checkpoints to save your progress.
info.name: Squared Sweeper
info.trivia: This level, and by extension, all of the Nukesweeper levels of its kind, are inspired by the Minesweeper game released in 1989. The mathematical aspect of the level is also inspired by Primesweeper by hPerks. The font used for the squares is the font from the Sword Art Online game. The clock emblem is a free vector from 'vecteezy.com'.

info.desc: Welcome to my very first Constructor level I made! Anyways, this place seems relaxing at your first glance, but you don't have time to relax in this tropical paradise filled with moving platforms and obstacles, do you? Collect all seven Gems and get to the finish before it's too late!

info.generalhint: When crossing the moving platforms, you'll have to keep your balance and agility, especially at the segment just before the cannon. For the first two Gems, use the Checkpoints to your advantage, but don't take too long because you must finish the level before it's too late. There are many Time Travels and Sundials in this level, so be sure to pick some up if you're going for the Platinum Time.

info.trivia: As stated in the description, this level is my very first Constructor level I made. It is also my very first level I've ever uploaded. Not to mention that "seomdeul" is a South Korean word meaning "islands".

Needless to say, collecting many TTs and SDs is important for beating Ultimate Times.

info.starthelptext: Touch these ice blocks to melt them!
info.trivia:
"Eoleum" means "ice" in Korean. The concept of ice blocks containing items was inspired by the Item Crystals from Super Mario Galaxy games. The cannon section just after the checkpoint was also inspired by Little Pink Venture.

Icy fun fact: The ice floor below the level is actually a giant ice arrow sign interior flipped upside down.
info.ultimatehint:
Many Time Travels and Sundials in this level are encased in ice blocks, so collect most of them. However, there are also some Time Penalty items in the level, so be careful. Needless to say, don't hit any of the ice shards! Every time you hit an ice shard, you'll be frozen and not be able to move for a 43200th of a day.

Tip: The radar can detect TTs and SDs as well. Use the radar to your advantage!

info.desc: Learn Prime and Square numbers the fun way by meeting the brand new element, Number Panels!
info.egghint: It's just above the start pad, but how can you reach it?
info.generalhint: In this level, there are two types of Number Panels: White Prime Panels and blue Square Panels. When crossing Prime Panels, you should step on prime numbers (numbers with exactly two divisiors) only, and when crossing Square Panels, you should step on square numbers (numbers with an odd number of divisiors) only. If you step on an incorrect Number Panel or a black trim, you'll be instantly knocked out of the level!
info.name: Knowledge of Primes and Squares
info.starthelptext: Don't step on a composite number or a 1. They are bad!
info.trivia:
The concepts of Prime Panels and Square Panels were inspired by Primesweeper and Squared Sweeper, respectively. The pillars supporting the platforms were also inspired by Fiery Rush.

Fun fact: Originally this level had fewer checkpoints, which made this level really hard. Now there are more of them making this level easy.
info.ultimatehint:
Time Travels placed on Number Panels will always last for the number below it in seconds. For example, if a TT is placed on a number 5, then it will last for 5 seconds. Collect many of them and you'll beat the Ultimate Time if you're fast enough. Also, memorize which Number Panels you have to step on - This is especially important for the no-jump zones!

Tip: You can use the checkpoints as a launch pad. The Super Bounce can also be used to "jump" in the no-jump zones.

info.desc: This satisfying observation has got great views, getting over 6 yells!
info.egghint: One of the students left it somewhere in the dimension while filming the scene, and forgot to bring it back... Now it's your chance to ste... just kidding, retrieve it and return it to its owner! But where's it? Reach the first checkpoint, turn left, and do some parkour to find it!
info.generalhint: Gwacheon Munwon Middle School 3-6 class students made a parody of TWICE - TT Music Video as a graduation UCC. They made many different CG dimensions for various scenes using their computers, and used some kind of interdimensional portals to enter the dimensions, just to film the scenes. But for some reason you got trapped in one of the dimensions, namely the dark town where it's always nighttime! The portal located high above the sky is the only way out, but it will close in nine minutes, and it requires the power of the thirty-six Gems scattered around the town. Thankfully, the students made the CGs for the dark rooftop scene pretty small, so this level should be short. But still, this level is all about agility. Be very careful not to fall off when jumping from roof to roof, especially on moving ice platforms, something that wasn't possible before. When crossing the tightropes, try to align yourself to the middle of the ropes. At the random force floor section, try holding down the jump button while collecting the red Gems.
info.name: Navigating the tSohggVGO6Y Town
info.starthelptext: Scary, isn't it?
info.trivia: This level's theme is based off of Sana's Kick-Ass scene (the dark rooftop scene) from TWICE - TT Music Video (youtube.com/watch?v=ePpPVE-GGJw). tSohggVGO6Y is also a YouTube video ID for a parody video from Gwacheon Munwon Middle School 3-6 class (youtube.com/watch?v=tSohggVGO6Y). Oh, and finally frictions on moving platforms! Yay!
info.ultimatehint: There are many places where you can cut corners. Use the slanted parts of the roofs to your advantage. Don't forget to collect all those TTs! The random force floor can be a killer, though.

info.awesomehint: Ah yes. The Awesome Time. From Marble Blast Ultra. I loved that feature from back in Marble Blast Ultra in 2006 on the Xbox 360! My favorite part is that it was there.
info.desc: Getting blown by this level will blast your marbles in no time!
info.egghint: This basement balcony lends quite a view!
info.generalhint:
Starting Islands - You can use the top of the bumpers to help you make it up to the ice platforms. The fans spin clockwise on both sides, so stay in the openings. Don't forget your blast!

House Island - The bottom fan won't blow you off if you jump, but the top one will only blow you off if you do. Don't get caught in front of both at once!

Slopes Island - Perhaps there's something else here that can help you fight the winds...

Tower Island - The fans are your friends here. And you won't need to worry about the mines on your final jump to the gem.

Ride Island - Stay above the fans, and you'll be carried to your goal. Don't forget about your Blast in case you don't reach high enough!

End Island - Three fans are greater than one. You don't need any outside help. You can use this and the tornado island to cross as well without going all the way back to the bottom.
info.name: Current Events
info.starthelptext: Each of the four corner islands has a challenge for you to overcome.
info.trivia:
The idea for the spinners using MBU fans was what inspired this level. The layout just popped in my head one day as well, and then I decided to theme the level around fans with a tornado in it.

This is the sixth custom level ever to use MBU shapes, and the first to use ones from Marble Blast Mobile! The other five before this were Playground of Peril by Ignas, Gosub 20 by Go'way, Standoff by Endy, Duplex by Connie, and King of the Ring 2 by yours truly.
info.ultimatehint:
Starting Islands - There are Time Travels above both of the spinning blocks. You can blast from the ice or off of the bumpers to reach them. Just be careful where you land! There's another Time Travel inside the tornado, too.

Tower Island - If you time it right, you can dodge the mines and skip straight to the Super Jump using the Ultra Blast.

Ride Island - There are multiple ways to use your Blast creatively here. You weren't coming to the HINTS section for a clear answer, though, were you?

info.trivia:
This is another tribute to a long-lost MBP level, the original being a simple gem collection level set in a similar gyro-like structure. It was revamped entirely into full-blown Gem Hunt.

There's a weird camera bug visible in this level's live preview: it causes the camera to jitter weirdly when the only difference between two path nodes is rotation around the forward axis. There's nothing I can do about it; bother HiGuy about it.

Also, if you're reading this, you're beautiful. <3

Avoid using the pink wall to flip, if you can. There's also a pretty clever way to collect some yellow and blue Gems from the wrong orientation.

remarks:
Level 3 in Lucilla's Level Pack 0. Difficulty: PQ Intermediate.
Personal best: 94

info.desc: I hope you can count to sixteen.
info.egghint: Have you heard of integer overflow?
info.eggsolution: Let the fade platforms go through one full cycle without you, while you wait on the start platform. Around the 53rd second, they'll be back, though their fading cycles will be slightly out of sync with their movement cycle. If you now ride the platforms, the Nest Egg will be there.
info.generalhint:
This level is a 4-bit binary counter! Each fade platform represents a bit of a number that increments from 0 up to 16 throughout the course of the level. Know binary in order to predict when which platforms will appear and disappear, or you'll have to learn the level through trial and error.

Orange = 1, pink = 2, blue = 4, green = 8.
info.name: Binary Counter
info.starthelptext: Jump on the fade platforms as soon as they appear.
info.trivia:
This is the final level in my first level pack, intended as a sort of bonus. It intentionally defies the static, rookie-like feel of the remaining levels, and feels a lot more like a level that would've been shoved into the Bonus category if it had appeared in PlatinumQuest. It also foreshadows the theme of what's coming next!

I am absolutely obsessed with binary, and I can just as well talk to you for hours about how awesome it is as I can have a heated argument with you if, like hPerks, you like base twelve.

Also, if you're reading this, you're beautiful. <3
info.ultimatehint: No traplaunches needed.

info.desc: Getting a gem always requires going the extra mile, but only one gem is needed to qualify.
info.egghint: Behind the finish pad, left hole.
info.eggsolution: Following the egg hint in the menu will lead you to another. And another. And another. Eventually, you'll be told to jump at the start pad from above. A teleporter there will catch you and teleport you to the Nest Egg.
info.generalhint: Not all extra miles are created equal. Some of the Gems are much easier to collect than others, so choose the one that suits you. And don't forget that there are extra miles for Time Travels, too.
info.name: Challenging Collection
info.trivia:
Challenging Collection was born out of a synergy of two ideas. The idea of a Quota level with only one Gem required to finish felt like a unique take on the Quota mode, but I wasn't sure how to make it work. Then I remembered a very old level idea called Collection Challenges, where every Gem was going to require a tiny challenge to collect. Just swapping the two words in the original name made the two ideas work together.

Constructor was very stubborn about one particular brush in this level's interior, calling it "malformed" and deleting it twice in a row.

Also, if you're reading this, you're beautiful. <3
info.ultimatehint: You'll need to find the perfect combination of extra miles and shortcuts. It's probably a good idea to collect the Gem on the fading bridge, because the accompanying Time Travel makes it worth it, and most other Gems are less convenient.

remarks:
Level 5 in Lucilla's Level Pack 0. Difficulty: PQ Beginner.
Personal best: 34.649

info.desc: Have you ever been to a 5 K race?
info.egghint: You'll need to find a hidden powerup first.
info.eggsolution: After Super Speeding, wall-hit to reach the top of the scenery with the huge ice shards. You'll find a Gyrocopter there. Duplicate it and fly over to the huge ice shards on the opposite side of the level. There you'll find a Gravity Modifier off the cliff. Float down the cliff with your duplicated Gyrocopter active to claim the Nest Egg.
info.generalhint:
The entire level is ice, so there's no reason not to be almost constantly jumping.

The blue targets mark lap checkpoints. These keep track of whether you're traversing the lap in the right order, and act as respawn points.
info.name: Ice Shard Circuit
info.starthelptext: Don't let the knockback throw you off the track when you thaw!
info.trivia:
Originally, I had an idea for an "Ice Shard Parkour", a level that was going to be all about doing difficult jumps by emerging from Ice Shards with the right velocity. But at one point I had a vision of a circuit, and the two combined into one, which became this level.

Fun fact: one brush in this level is doubly sheared, which left a ditch out of sight. I wanted to fill it in at first, but on second thought decided to keep it and give it a new purpose - but psst, you can't know what it is!

Also, if you're reading this, you're beautiful. <3
info.ultimatehint:
This one's all about consistency. Your route here doesn't have to be flawless, but you do need to be able to execute it three times in a row without freezing or slipping.

You have one lifeline for a minor mess-up. If you find a cute little skip that saves about 5 seconds, you can get another lifeline every lap you perform it.

remarks:
Level 2 in Lucilla's Level Pack 0. Difficulty: PQ Expert.
Personal best: 1:27.084

info.desc: Hunt for the many Gems in my little realm, shaped with detail and care.
info.generalhint: Watch out on the upper layers! All spawn points are on the bottom half of the level, so if you fall, you have to get back up. The Teleporters are meant to help you return to them once you've reached them once.
info.name: Luci's Hunting Grounds
info.trivia:
The description doesn't lie when it says this level was "shaped with detail and care". Trimming the interior, especially the upper parts, took way too long with all the precise corner-chiseling, and even the faces that are out of sight have the correct rotation and scaling of their textures. The flower colors you'll find in this level are also a subtle detail: their colors are red, yellow, and blue, just like the Gems you're hunting.

Grinding this level was a nightmare. I got a score of 124 early on, so I initially set the Ultimate Score to 120, but I was never able to get even close to it a second time. Eventually I decided I'll lower it to 105 - having gotten scores above 105 a few times by then - and proceeded to fail to get the new lower Ultimate Score for probably an hour or so. But I suppose the plus side is that now all top 5 scores on this level for me are Ultimate.

Also, if you're reading this, you're beautiful. <3
info.ultimatehint:
Have a PowerUp in your inventory at all times. They can reduce the travel times between consecutive gem spawns to just a few seconds. Also, don't even bother if your first spawn gives you the platinum gem in the upper layers, inside the tornado.

Speaking of the upper layers, there's more ways to get up there than you might think. A Super Jump or Gyrocopter is straightforward, but you can also slope hit with a Super Speed or even use the tornado to your advantage.
