info.desc: Can you move faster in 40 seconds?
info.name: Crimson Orthodox

remarks: Thank you Ralph for this skybox!

info.desc: Keep your balance and roll your way through this dance!
info.easteregghint: After ascending up, it is above you. But how will you get the egg?
info.egghint: This field is for PQ levels, which this level is not.
info.generalhint: Keep your balance, and get on the platform right as it's in reach.
info.name: Platforms in Motion
info.starthelptext: Survive the moving platform ordeals ahead!
info.ultimatehint: No, it doesn't involve traplaunching. Check under a platform, and figure it out from there.

remarks:
Some parts inspired by "Moving challenge II" from Marble Blast Future.
Also my first level with moving platforms. Hope to do more in the future!

info.desc: Stroll around the Moving Castle and avoid being knocked around or falling off!
info.easteregghint: I will be... kind of shocked if anyone found this without the aid of someone else/without the Editor.
info.generalhint: Be vigilent, don't rush parts, time every move you do. Approach this level without a speedrunner mindset at first.
info.name: Queen's Hideaway
info.starthelptext: Be careful when speeding into the Castle.
info.trivia: This level was made in a approximately 1-2 days, due to boredom, partially.

info.awesomehint: Find the right path!
info.desc: Roll around and collect the gems on this snowy and slippery level.
info.easteregghint: Don't fill out this field for PQ levels. Easter Eggs are in the other games!
info.egghint: Honestly, it's really easy. I just could not resist.
info.generalhint: Find all the gems in this snowy maze!
info.name: Winter Wonderland
info.starthelptext: See how fast you can find the gems!
info.trivia: Share some fun trivia about this level!
info.ultimatehint: Diagonal movement plays key.

info.awesomehint: Skip cycles on the spiral-patterned moving platforms and get Time Travels. And, play it perfectly, what else you expect from a hard level?
info.desc: It's when everything starts to translate.
info.egghint: It's on the bridge. Simple enough.
info.generalhint: Pay attention to how the platforms move. A very common motif in this area is the spiral-patterned moving platforms, where the safest platforms to stay on are the innermost platforms because they move the slowest.
info.name: Platformer's Philosophy
info.starthelptext: Red areas are unsafe!
info.trivia: Another level with a lot of moving platforms. However, this time they ressembles rotating platforms which this game engine is unable to do. The moving trims is another thing that I would like to experiment as a level element. This level is generally made from moving platforms that are moving back and forth as an obstacle as well as others that serves similarly as rotating platforms. The name of this level (and perhaps the level too) is inspired by a boss level/song named Frey's Philosophy, from a game named Lanota. The moving trim also perhaps refers to another game named Cytus. Well, those games are rhythm games that probably have no relation with Marble Blast. Level originated from Level 8 of Marble Blast GLC 3, and Stage 3-8 of Great Marble Adventure
info.ultimatehint: Consistency is everything. Stay on safe platforms if there's a risk of falling.

info.desc: bulka

info.awesomehint: Grab the first time travel, and never let the time restarts.
info.desc: It's just a straight path to the finish, but with challenges on the way.
info.egghint: The only clear hidden spot, but how you would reach there?
info.generalhint: Use the radar to track how many gems you have collected in the ramp section. Also, it is quite obvious which branch you should choose in the beginning.
info.name: Azure Fortress
info.starthelptext:
The path to finish is straight.
It's up to you how you are going to go there.
info.trivia: Originally named Straight Path, this level was an introduction to bouncy floors and mud in Marble Blast GLC 4. This level was then featured as Stage 4-3 of Great Marble Adventure.
info.ultimatehint: Find a good path to collect all gems while still having the Time Travel effects active in the ramp section.

info.awesomehint: Use the first moving platform to go up, collect the gems in the reverse order, then use the second moving platform to go up and continue with the normal path.
info.desc: When things moves in a twisty manner, it's important to understand how they move.
info.egghint: Climb to the roof.
info.generalhint: Understand the movement/rotation pattern of every moving platform is important. Pay attention on which area of platform will be on top/bottom when rotated. Finding safespots on those also helps.
info.name: Pagoda Heights
info.starthelptext: Does this level looks familiar to you?
info.trivia: It's all started with the music I made, Lamentations of Spoiled Past, which sounds like an oriental-chinese music. This gave me idea to decorate the level with eastern ornaments such as tori gate and shrine roof. Moving platforms that moves in a spiral pa
info.ultimatehint: Understanding when and how to navigate the moving platforms is actually somewhat similar to the skills in the previous stage.

info.awesomehint: Ok you are not doing that.
info.desc: I don't slide... We slide.
info.egghint: If you don't do a sign hit, what are you even doing?
info.generalhint: Generally, don't roll over the red ice.
info.name: Puzzle 15 - Overcomplicated
info.starthelptext: Follow the trail... or take a shortcut over the red ice.
info.trivia: Puzzle 15 was originally planned to be a 2D puzzle, but that didn't catch on.
info.ultimatehint: You'll not gonna hit that first concrete, do you?

remarks: I FINALLY DID IT

info.name: Material Challenge
info.desc: Roll through different materials and collect gems!

info.name: Going to the goal
info.starthelptext: Take the help of hazards and powerups to reach to the finish.
info.desc: Reach to the finish.

info.name: Bounce Mini Course
info.desc: Use Super Bounce PowerUps and complete the course!

info.awesomehint: You can skip the underwater section altogether with a precise edge-hit. Everything else: go fast!
info.desc: When you're up, it's always easy. It's when you're down below that the going gets rough.
info.egghint: You'll need the shock absorber for this one.
info.generalhint: A simple level, but the underground area may present some difficulty. You'll need good jumping skills in order to pass it.
info.name: PQ No TTs 37: Above and Below
info.trivia: The camera path for this level was not changed at all from how it appeared in PlatinumQuest Trailer #1.
info.ultimatehint: A matter of going fast, but then again, that's always the case.

info.awesomehint: Before going up the first elevators, you should have 5 Gems. Make sure to catch the Gems closest to you as well as zero Time Travels.
info.desc: Play on this beautiful construction site for a bridge. Observe the maritime traffic.
info.generalhint: Some Gems are far more difficult to collect than others. Wisely choose which seven you'd like to skip.
info.name: PQ No TTs 63: A Bridge Too Hard
info.starthelptext: You look like a fit marble. It should be no problem climbing up some of the ropes here.
info.trivia: There used to be a Time Travel on the ship below, but it was removed as it made speedrunning the level far too frustrating.
info.ultimatehint: It's a good idea to catch the easy Gems on the top of the level, as well as some freebies scattered around. There is also no very nice 10 seconds Time Travel on the sand part of the bridge.

info.awesomehint: Turns out you're not even taught the method required to get the best time. Perhaps you need to Vice your way to it?
info.desc: Learn about several techniques that will come in handy, including the Wall Hit and Diagonal Movement.
info.egghint: The egg's location is... shocking.
info.generalhint:
You can also use Diagonal Movement with <func:bind moveforward> and <func:bind moveright> instead of <func:bind moveforward> and <func:bind moveleft>, if you prefer. It really doesn't matter.
Also, try not to rely on the guides for Diagonal Movement, as no other levels will help you in that way.

The Platinum Time requires you to use Diagonal Momvement, and possibly catch no Time Travel on the way.
info.name: PQ No TTs 14: Advanced Techniques
info.starthelptext: Roll down the slope as fast as you can and jump right before you hit the wall.
info.trivia: This level was created around the time when the current version of Training Wheels was made. This was done because an older version of that level taught you the techniques that this level does.
info.ultimatehint:
Use Diagonal Movement at the first Wall Hit to grab no high-up Time Travel.
In general, you'll want to use Diagonal Movement as much as possible for this and pretty much every other level.

info.awesomehint:
Gravity might be your very undoing here due to the speed your marble will move.
Nonetheless, you can use it to gain slight bounces every time you hit a brick, then hit a brick adjacent to it.
This way you can clear several bricks much more quickly while slowly falling down.
info.desc: Marblaxia contacted DOH for help, and it had trapped you in this Breakout-type level. Clear the board to escape!
info.generalhint: Move right and left quickly while bouncing on walls to gain much-needed height.
info.name: PQ No TTs 80: Arkanoid
info.trivia:
Originally meant to be part of the puzzle series along with Racing Spirits, the idea was left abandoned before picking it up at the end of development. It was created, tested and completed in just two hours.
This level was inspired by the famous Arkanoid games, which Matan spent too many hours on in his childhood.

Also, if you aren't humming to yourself the jingle that played at the start of every level, then what is wrong with you?!
info.ultimatehint: Clear the right side's no Time Travels and then go to the Dragon's mouth. Clear the top area and finish with the neck.

info.awesomehint: Switching gravity. Not even once.
info.desc: Looks can be deceiving.
info.generalhint: You will need to know your diagonal movement and wall hitting skills for this one.
info.name: PQ No TTs 83: Azimuth
info.trivia: This level was made while we were still learning what kind of levels we wanted for PlatinumQuest. You can see it didn't quite make the cut.
info.ultimatehint: You can finish sideways, and no Time Travels can be gotten in one sweep using a Super Jump.

info.artist: Phil, fixed by Threefolder, edited by Yoshicraft224
info.awesomehint: You may want to skip one or two of the Gems closest to the start and do a cool edge hit instead.
info.desc:
Most is magnificent...
All is...?
info.egghint: Did you read the level's description?
info.generalhint:
Be careful on the thin paths, and watch out for surprises.
There's a Gem right behind the start pad, so you really only have to collect 9 on the main structure to be able to finish.
info.name: PQ No TTs 57: Bag of Secrets...
info.trivia: PlatinumQuest originally had you unlock all levels in your own path, and this level was supposed to have an alternative exit that allowed you to skip further on the quest.
info.ultimatehint: Just go for the Gems that are lowest on the structure. The ones near the top aren't necessary and may just waste your time.

info.awesomehint: Preserve the Super Speed.
info.desc: Get into the swing of things.
info.egghint: Edge hit.
info.generalhint:
If you play with the music off, it's time to crank it up.

Count the beats in your head. The platforms switch every measure.

The last area's a bit tough, try to remember where the platforms will appear!
info.name: PQ No TTs 68: Blast to the Beat
info.starthelptext: If you wish to restart the level, try to do so on the beat so that the music doesn't de-sync.
info.trivia:
Yes, this level was inspired by Super Mario Galaxy.

After appearing in PlatinumQuest Trailer #2, it also spawned a "beep-block" custom level craze in the community that lasted a few weeks.
info.ultimatehint: Don't get caught up in one area for too long. Find a path that will allow you to speed through in the least amount of cycles possible.

info.awesomehint: Smart planning with the way you get the Gems and bounce off of walls can save you serious time. Use the Bubble in new ways!
info.desc: Swim through the floating water pockets in this cavern using your trusty Bubble.
info.generalhint:
Watch your momentum! Smacking into a wall with the bubble active will bounce you pretty far back.
If you're descending, try alternative between having the bubble on and off to slowly fall.
info.name: PQ No TTs 15: Bubble Cavern
info.starthelptext: Don't ask how the metal beams keep the water floating. We're not entirely sure, either.
info.trivia: Originally the Bumper section came before the Gem section, and used Ice Shards instead of Bumpers.
info.ultimatehint: You will need to collect no Time Travel here, and switch between having your Bubble on and off throughout your navigation in the water. Keep moving at all times.

info.awesomehint: Get no Time Travels, but beware the zero in the air will be tough.
info.desc: Your camera is stuck in an isometric view. Get used to it and control the marble in a different way.
info.generalhint: The controls are the same as a normal level, but you'll have to realize that the gameplay will change a bit.
info.name: PQ No TTs 75: Camera Woes
info.trivia: Inspired by Crash Bandicoot's ball-playing levels, Matan wanted to create a 4-levels series, but lost motivation faster than he should have had. The code for this camera view exists though, so custom levels can use it.
info.ultimatehint: The path with the fade platforms is harder, but saves more time.

info.awesomehint: The closest Gems to you should be the ones you go for. You will have to one-shot every Gem and no Time Travel you go for. The first Gem and no Time Travel can be gotten together before going back to the cannons. Ensure the Gems you pick are the ones you'll bounce back to the starting area with.
info.desc: Test your sniping skills by picking off the Gems, or challenge yourself going for no harder Time Travels.
info.egghint: Explore the level, this one is really cool to find. Use the checkpoints to assist you.
info.generalhint: Go for the easier Gems. Since there are two Checkpoints next to the start pad, you can use them whenever you pick up a Gem.
info.name: PQ No TTs 58: Cannon Sniper
info.starthelptext: The cannon in front sends you to the finish.
info.trivia: Originally based on a crappy level of Matan's called Pipe Sniper, this level soon became inspired by an old custom level called 'Aim or Shame'. Eventually, a construction theme was deemed best, and that's the result you see in front of you.
info.ultimatehint: Don't miss TOO much, and definitely go for no Time Travels.

info.artist: Ian, replicated by Threefolder, edited by Yoshicraft224
info.awesomehint: Use the Teleport Powerup on the central ice area below the Start Pad. After that you can grab a few Gems, make it to the top tightrope and back down on the sand slopes. Use the Teleport Powerup and get the remaining ice Gems, then do the outside challenges before falling down to the water section.
info.desc: Find as many Gems as you can. You don't have much time!
info.generalhint: The Teleport Powerup can be helpful to get whisked back to the top. Likewise, collect the Gems you'll find the easiest.
info.name: PQ No TTs 30: Castle Colossus
info.trivia:
The beginning of the camera path for this level is based on its appearance in PlatinumQuest Trailer #1.

This level had to be remade entirely from scratch because no one on the Platinum Team had the QuArK file for it.
info.ultimatehint: Don't bother with the Gems on the green outside bits. Focus on the Gems near the center of the level, and don't fall to the water area until you have less than 3 to go.

info.awesomehint: There's a nice route that takes no Time Travels and it's not hard to figure out. At the end you'll have to make a run to the finish or else you can't get this low time.
info.desc: Grab the Gems on this dizzying structure.
info.generalhint: The finish is a bit tricky to get to. You'll have to wait for some platforms to move by so you can use them to bridge the gap.
info.name: PQ No TTs 33: Centripetal Force
info.starthelptext: Make sure to take your momentum into account before you jump.
info.trivia: This level was created immediately after rotating platforms with real physics were deemed possible in the Torque engine.
info.ultimatehint: Playing the waiting game is sometimes a necessary evil.

info.awesomehint: Plan your TT catches for moments where you need to slow down. Try to avoid hitting the second sandy wall - time it so that you hit the slope at the top. There's a fun timesaver at the end of the 3rd lap - hint: you'll finish sideways!
info.desc: Chase after the Gems around the track. Can you get them all in 3 laps?
info.generalhint: Don't be afraid to slow down to grab Gems picking up speed behind you. Be mindful of the Par Time, though.
info.name: PQ No TTs 70: Chasetrack
info.starthelptext: No cheating - you still have to do 3 laps!
info.trivia: The .mcs code for this level was generated entirely via Python. This level, with two paths each having over 200 pathnodes, plus a Technostick-style conveyor belt, would have taken weeks to make otherwise.
info.ultimatehint: Don't go for all the TTs in one lap - split them up so that you take different paths each lap, to avoid slowdown. The 45-degree trim is hugely important for keeping your speed.

info.awesomehint:
Go up the right slide first, clearing part of the top area, before using the Anvil + Super Bounce to get to the uppermost blue Gem, followed by the bouncy floor poles.
Afterwards clear the Gems in the sands before doing the structure's various challenges.
The Platinum Gem should be done last.
info.desc: A beautiful playground for the child in you, riddled with fun and secrets waiting to be found.
info.egghint: Hopefully you've been practicing your pole-jumping skills.
info.generalhint: Make sure you check out the whole structure, and visit every nook and cranny you can think of.
info.name: PQ No TTs 48: Child's Play
info.trivia: Pablo released this level without being able to beat it himself.
info.ultimatehint: Use your radar to discover cleverly hidden Gems. There's even a platinum Gem somewhere...

info.awesomehint: Jumping on the ice slope is the key to this run. Don't get frozen though, there are plenty of spots to do that.
info.desc: Mind the Ice Shards.
info.generalhint: The moving platform section is probably the hardest part. Don't overcomplicate things, just try to find a straight-forward path up the icy slopes. If you can't do that, you can always stay on the moving platform and dodge the walls instead -- though, you'll lose a fair amount of time doing so.
info.name: PQ No TTs 46: Chilled
info.starthelptext:
You'll have to find a way to gain enough speed to finish.
Try not to freeze!
info.trivia:
This level and its general style were inspired by Freezing Point.

Originally, this level was in the Intermediate category, but the beginning section was enough to move it to Advanced.
info.ultimatehint: As long as you don't get frozen, you should be on the right track. Make sure to grab no Time Travels!

info.awesomehint:
There's lots to do here:
-Memorise Gem spawn locations against teleporter locations so you can be whisked back to the selector after EVERY SPAWN!
-Have a Gyrocopter, at the very least, equipped with you so you can get up slopes a lot more easily.
-Grab no Time Travels in your way, do not go out of the way unless they are worth it!
-Have great spawns, restart if necessary. Platinums not required.
-If you have a spawn with Gems around the sandy teleporters, use the telepoters to stop time temporarily as you go across it towards the next Gem.
-The selector may be used as a scouting area to see the Gem spawn. Don't leave its area though or time will continue its countdown!
-The water can be used to gain massive speed boost to get up slopes.
info.desc: Explore this huge kingdom, racing to the Gems wherever they spawn.
info.egghint: The peak. The top. The zenith. The summit. The climax. The apogee. Thesaurus has more words for this but let's stop here now.
info.generalhint: Your marble speed is DOUBLED in this level! Combine this with diagonal movement to make your way across the bowl in record time. Braking might be an issue, though.
info.name: PQ No TTs 51: Citadel
info.starthelptext: This is the selector, which doesn't stop the clock. The sand pits teleport you back here.
info.trivia: This level used to be much more slippery, but later in development, traction was increased a fair amount to keep up with the speed increase.
info.ultimatehint: Since this level is so big, there's a very good chance that you'll constantly see Gems spawn miles away from each other. If this happens too much in your run, you may need to restart, though the sandy Teleporter areas are incredibly useful for moving around. Knowing where they are will come a long way.

info.artist: Ian, replicated by Threefolder, edited by Yoshicraft224
info.awesomehint: Plan your jump pattern carefully, that makes it a lot easier.
info.desc: Skillshot the Gems on your way down!
info.egghint: See that fade platform behind the start pad? ...Good luck.
info.generalhint: You'll need to use plenty of diagonal movement for this one. Don't get caught on the bumpers in the pit by jumping and moving as close as possible to the wall.
info.name: PQ No TTs 35: Climb and Plummet
info.trivia: This is another level that had to be remade from scratch due to the Platinum Team not having a copy of its QuArK file.
info.ultimatehint: It's faster to grab some Gems and no Time Travels on the way down, rather than on the way up.

info.awesomehint: Get no Time Travels, and remember you don't need every single Gem on the first lap.
info.desc: If you miss a Gem on the first lap, you can always grab it the second time around.
info.egghint: Remember how to loop exit?
info.generalhint:
Make sure you have all the Gems before you complete your second lap or you'll have to restart the level.
As always with this sort of level, speed control is a necessity.
info.name: PQ No TTs 69: Conservation of Momentum
info.starthelptext: Haven't I seen this level before?
info.trivia: The ending of this level used to be much different -- after the space ramp, you would slam into a sandy wall and be teleported to just before the finish line. It was scrapped in favor of a more fluid approach.
info.ultimatehint: Slow down in the Ice Shard area so that you can grab both the Gem and no Time Travel. You'll also, obviously, want to collect as many Time Travels as you can.

info.awesomehint: How crazy are you to perform the obvious stunt?
info.desc: Don't forget your hard hat.
info.egghint: Between a wall and a camera place.
info.generalhint: Know when to go fast, and when to go slow.
info.name: PQ No TTs 45: Dangerous Development
info.starthelptext: This is a construction zone, so make sure to control your speed!
info.trivia:
The background cranes were the first thing created for this level.

This level's name is also an accurate description of PlatinumQuest itself.
info.ultimatehint: There aren't many shortcuts to find, so just try not to fall off too much.

info.awesomehint: Diagonal into no Time Travel and the rest is history.
info.desc: Four challenges, zero Time Travels, and only three seconds. Can you do it?
info.egghint: Look for a hidden switch.
info.generalhint:
No Time Travel re-spawns every 15 seconds, but it re-spawns only 7 times.
Whereas the checkpoints normally discard any of your active Time Travel bonus, in this level they do not, so you should use them to your advantage.
info.name: PQ No TTs 60: Dependency
info.starthelptext: No Time Travel lasts for 20 seconds, and will respawn every 15 seconds, but it will only respawn 7 times!
info.trivia:
The central starting area was done by Oaky; the four challenges were created by Andrew.

The concept of no Time Travel only respawning a certain amount of times was implemented late in development.
info.ultimatehint: The order you do everything doesn't matter -- just keep coming back to get no Time Travel.

info.awesomehint: One of these platforms may seem like it gives marginal returns, but in the long run it saves the most.
info.desc: The longer you stay on these platforms, the less safe the ground becomes.
info.egghint: Go right for justice! Or the Nest Egg, whichever works for you.
info.generalhint: Some Fade Platforms will disappear after your marble touches them for a certain amount of times. Every time you touch them, they will fade out a little more. Some will disappear more slowly than others, so you can stay on them longer.
info.name: PQ No TTs 34: Diminishing Returns
info.starthelptext: No boxed Time Travels should be collected by constantly jumping from below them.
info.trivia:
This level is in fact a tutorial level! Matan needed to make it as else you'd only meet these Fade Platforms in Miscalculation.
Matan had no idea how to make the level design for this level and simply winged it.

Fun Fact: These kind of Fade Platforms are only found in Matan's levels in PlatinumQuest.
info.ultimatehint: Time Travels won't increase profits, but to really succeed here, you will have to cut corners.

info.awesomehint: Lots of speed and a number of Time Travels are all you need. Seriously though, slow down before you fall to the other side of the level!!
info.desc: Doesn't look too strange now, but just you wait.
info.generalhint: Watch out for when the path gets steep, as well as the end of the road. Remember to jump in order to build up speed!
info.name: PQ No TTs 77: Dizzying Road
info.starthelptext: Building speed will certainly be helpful, except remember to slow down at the end of this path.
info.trivia: A highly contested level in that some people liked it, some didn't and some thought it to be really horrible. What's your opinion?
info.ultimatehint: No Time Travels and some diagonal movement should suffice to beat this challenge, assuming you slowed down enough towards the end..

info.awesomehint: Clear out the area furthest away from the start, and work your way towards the start point. After that, do the loop, grab a couple of Gems at most and start the second floor.
info.desc: That corner Gem is HiGuy's fault.
info.generalhint: The lack of checkpoints means you will have to think before moving to the next areas.
info.name: PQ No TTs 82: Double Maze
info.trivia: This level is in fact two Puzzle series floors that Matan made and joined them into one.
info.ultimatehint: Jumping right before hitting the Gravity Modifier on the ice loop will give you some speed boost. You can, technicaly, finish the loop without the time restarting.

info.awesomehint:
Uhhhh...

Get no Time Travels?
info.desc: It can be an uphill battle to stay on the course.
info.egghint: One of the most hated Nest Eggs by the development team, much to Matan's delight. Time your jump!
info.generalhint: You can get through pretty quickly, but you must get aligned with the ending launch ramp if you want to actually finish.
info.name: PQ No TTs 17: Downhill and Out of Here!!
info.trivia:
When first making the level, Matan just understood how to use QuArK's slope making system and how easy it was.
Easy, no fuss, no misalignments or texture misalignments too.
Originally this level had brown wall texturing only, and wouldn't convert using standard map2dif as it threw vislink errors everywhere.

Matan ended up making three versions of this level. The first an absolute disaster, the second was this level just with a 90-degree rotated start, and this being the third. It converted without problems thanks to map2dif_plus from Seizure22.
info.ultimatehint: It's useful to move diagonally here, as well as jumping to get plenty of speed boost.

info.awesomehint: There are two cool wall hits to do: one at the start and one at the end. Make sure to get no Time Travels as well!
info.desc: Discover the Quota mode in this level. There are 40 Gems in this level total, but you'll only need half of them to finish.
info.generalhint: Quota mode allows you to create your own path in a level, by skipping Gems that might be too hard or too out of the way for you, while still allowing you to finish.
info.name: PQ No TTs 03: Downhill Skipping
info.starthelptext: You don't have to regret your decisions here.
info.trivia: This level replaced an old Quota tutorial somewhat late in development. The old level was designed to be more open-ended, but testing showed that it was far too confusing.
info.ultimatehint: Make sure to grab enough Gems at the beginning of the level. No Time Travels could help...

info.awesomehint: Go fast and super tight, and try to abuse the marble collision boundary!
info.desc: The evil Titiritero has enchanted all of the Gems and cursed none of the Time Travels. Will you be able to best him?
info.generalhint:
Avoid the Time Penalties! Go slower than you think you need to in order to stay on the level, unless you're a seasoned player.
Either way, you should have no problems staying under Par.
info.name: PQ No TTs 07: El Titiritero
info.starthelptext: Foolish marble! Why do you even bother challenging me?
info.trivia: The paths that the items follow were originally going to be entirely random, but this was never implemented out of fear of creating a heavily RNG-based level.
info.ultimatehint: The Gems and Time Penatlies don't follow random paths. You can easily plan your route.

info.awesomehint: You're going to circle a bit around the logo, and miss zero of the small Time Travels that is ever slightly out of your way.
info.desc:
Another game with its logo put as an actual level.
Clearly original and creative!
Well done Matan!
info.generalhint: A simple level, the Par Time is there for a challenge if you desire to aim for all the Gems.
info.name: PQ No TTs 79: Emblem
info.trivia: When seeing the level, Threefolder was jealous that Matan could make a better PlatinumQuest logo than him. On a related note the map file is an absolute mess in order to make the level look good.
info.ultimatehint: If you zoom quickly into zero of edge Time Travels, you can look back and activate the Super Speed to stop yourself from falling.

info.awesomehint: You'll need precision here as the Fade Platform cycles decide your end time. You'll need to drop down to the last two floors from Fade Platforms that aren't part of the cycle.
info.desc: Get the Gems on each level, then descend to the next!
info.generalhint: Use the fade platforms that disappear on touch to stay on a layer while the periodically fading platforms do their thing. Alternatively rest on the checkpoint platforms for a quick breather.
info.name: PQ No TTs 29: Evaporation
info.starthelptext: Move quickly so that you don't fall through before you have to.
info.trivia: Midway through development, Fade Platforms were changed to smoothly fade out, instead of turning white before disappearing -- as that "flashing" behavior was a bug. After that change, this level became nearly unplayable -- there was no longer a warning "flash" to tell the player to jump. The "flash" bug was re-implemented as a design choice later on.
info.ultimatehint: No Time Travels are tricky to get but quite necessary.

info.awesomehint:
Besides planetary-spawns luck, you need to get no Time Travels as often as possible.
Due to the sloped structure of the level you will have to think which Gems to collect first, and ensure you can manage the jumps between the inner and outer rings.
info.desc: Boldly roll where no marble has rolled before.
info.generalhint:
Tip: Make sure to jump off the planet from the sides next to the closest ring if you wish to easily leave it.

Fun Fact: When Narvoxx made this level for the Hunt Level competition, he called it 'Rings Around Saturn.'
info.name: PQ No TTs 21: Exoplanet
info.trivia: The original version of this level also had a fourth ring, which was next to the planet itself and rendered movement from one half of the level to its underside impossible.
info.ultimatehint:
You can also use the planet to turn gravity to your liking instead of using the Gravity Modifiers. Make sure to jump away at the right time!
In addition, collect as many Time Travels as possible!

info.awesomehint: You'll need to make three edge hits and have proper marble spin control to get to the Space and Bouncy room with two seconds or less on the clock. Another edge hit in that room and you're good to get to the finish in record time!
info.desc: Different types of friction floors affect your control over the marble.
info.egghint: The Egg is in front of you, but the edge hit will take a few attempts. Find the best spot!
info.generalhint: Jumping while on surfaces of lower frictions (ice, mud and space) allows you to use air movement and adjust your direction properly. This will make such surfaces much easier to navigate.
info.name: PQ No TTs 01: Feeling Frictional
info.starthelptext: Time Travels with a Gold band stop the time. Red banded ones add to your time and you must avoid them.
info.trivia: Matan originally planned a winding grass path for the level's end, but in the end decided to finish the level in a much simpler manner.
info.ultimatehint:
The more Time Travels you collect, the lower the end time will be, and therefore you won't be able to beat this Ultimate Time. This level teaches you to go out of the way for no helpful items and don't create a path using them.

DANGER: DO NOT JUMP OVER THE WINDOWS!!

info.awesomehint: Aim and shoot as fast as possible. You will need zero Time Travels as well.
info.desc: Master PQ's cannon feature.
info.egghint: Having a Blast, except several times.
info.generalhint: The second cannon in the level and the section with the moving space platforms will both take you several tries to nail down. Don't get discouraged!
info.name: PQ No TTs 56: Fire when Ready
info.starthelptext: Are you ready to tackle this battlefield, warrior?
info.trivia: This level was hated by most of the team and was deemed near unplayable before the cannon guides were added in. Now it's a bit better.
info.ultimatehint: The cannon with the moving space platforms has a lot of power in it... just aim up and... to the right??!

info.awesomehint:
You can save a bit of time by doing an unorthodox route, and miss no Time Travel Trigger with it.

Fun fact: You can jump on the grass to go faster, thanks to friction mechanics.
info.desc: Chip hits the ice and decides to chill out. Then he runs into a fake wall and turns the maze into a Thrash-A-Thon.
info.egghint: Align.
info.generalhint: Jumping on grass allows you to gain more speed. Alternatively use the grass to break a lot faster.
info.name: PQ No TTs 81: Four Corners
info.starthelptext: Kidding! No fake walls here!! Do grab the Gems though, will you?
info.trivia:
Inspired by Chip's Challenge ice levels, though the fake walls were skipped for sanity's sake.

The no Time Travel (Penalty?) triggers aren't placed at random, as they follow a specific ruleset.
info.ultimatehint: Make your own route, as long as you can stay consistent. Some are actually faster than others. Perhaps the golden rule here is that opposites attract.

info.awesomehint:
If you're half-way through the level (the checkpoint right after the ice shards hole) with up to 18 seconds on the clock, then continue. Otherwise restart and figure out how to do this low.

Also, you can skip the first set of ice shards. For the end use a Super Speed with a wall hit to do a nice skip.
info.desc: Not all ice shards are cold-hearted.
info.generalhint: If you choose the mud path, you can only jump at the lowest point.
info.name: PQ No TTs 28: Freezing Point
info.starthelptext: Skid down the slope! You'll have another chance to get the Gems if you miss any.
info.trivia: The original version of this level had moving platforms occasionally block some of the Ice Shards in the Super Speed section, but they were removed because they caused very odd bugs on Mac computers.
info.ultimatehint: After you hit an ice shard inside the hole, try and jump. Doing so will allow you to get other Gems before freezing again. Likewise, a good jump on the ice shard on the side at the end can throw you through the hole at the top.

info.awesomehint: Actually it's better to leave one of the Gems surrounding the blades not taken, because you can take it after the gravity loop and go directly for the zero gravity section. You need to start anti-clockwise so that the purple Gem aligns, then no Sundial or the black Gem, blue Gem and gravity loop. From the zero gravity zone, the three propeller Gems can be gotten without any problems (start with the one nearest to PhilsEmpire Graffiti), then do the bumper Gems and the teleporter Gems. The cannon and water challenge are last.
info.desc: You've had the opportunity to learn and practice all the skills that will be required of you. Now prove that you know them!
info.generalhint: Don't forget -- use your Radar (Press <func:bind radarSwitch> to toggle) to find any Gems you haven't collected yet!
info.name: PQ No TTs 19: From Under the Dragon's Wing
info.starthelptext: Don't forget to travel around the gravity loop!
info.trivia:
This level was inspired by Marble Blast Gold's last beginner level, Grand Finale. You can see references to it throughout the design.
The level name is a reference to Matan.
info.ultimatehint: It's probably the best way if you take the blades' Gems and its surrounding first before going onto the gravity loop. The rest of it is up to you. See how fast you are because the bumpers and Gems will require good timing.

info.awesomehint: Start by doing this level backwards, getting what normally is the first Gem as the last one. Don't use the cannon at all for this challenge!
info.desc: The expert levels are starting to heat up...
info.generalhint: All of the challenges in this level revolve around the Fire Blast -- it's up to you to determine how to use it.
info.name: PQ No TTs 61: Frozen Flames
info.starthelptext: Head straight after launching from the cannon.
info.trivia: It's not unlikely that this level is what prevented the Fireball powerup from being cut.
info.ultimatehint: You need to find an optimal path through all of the Ice Shard mazes. Keep on the lookout for shortcuts only possible with the Fire Blast ability.

info.artist: Leaf1741, replicated by Andrew, edited by Yoshicraft224
info.awesomehint: You'll have to constantly be on the lookout for no respawning Time Travels and create some sort of a route based on them. They will give you enough time to make it past this challenge.
info.desc: Find a path as you hunt around in this level for the Gems.
info.generalhint:
This level looks familiar...
But the tunnel system doesn't exist any more.
info.name: PQ No TTs 42: Gem Finding Folly
info.trivia: One of the few levels the staff enjoyed so much they converted it to Hunt mode, and it was still pretty fun.
info.ultimatehint: The Super Jumps are incredibly useful. The Teleporter powerups have the potential to be useful as well, but they're far more of a gamble.

info.awesomehint: Start with the Gems in front of you and collect both no Time Travel or a Sundial, then collect the Gems to the left of the start pad. From this point, clear out each section before moving to the next one. Be efficient though by ensuring you make a single pass as much as possible.
info.desc: A luscious playground, bountiful with Gems... and yours to explore.
info.egghint: You will need both diagonal movement and wall-hitting skills to grab this one.
info.generalhint:
As with Hunt Mode, every colored Gem is worth a different amount of points. Unlike Hunt Mode, all Gems are available to collect at the start. In some Gem Madness levels, it may be possible to collect all the Gems!

Hint: use the Radar!
info.name: PQ No TTs 12: Gems Ahoy!
info.starthelptext:
It's Gem Madness time!
How many points can you collect before time runs out?!
info.trivia: This level's name was inspired by an old custom level, called 'Fans Ahoy!'
info.ultimatehint: There is plenty of time here, and you should be able to create a large path that collects almost all of the Gems with ease. Clear out one section at a time!

info.awesomehint: Go left first, and clear out the Gems and no Time Travels there and behind the start area. From there keep going in counter clockwise fashion, then clear a bit of the center, followed by the Gems and no Time Travels in the Moving Platforms section. Wrap it up through the centre directly to the finish.
info.desc: Grab them all to finish!
info.egghint: Too easy to find, but may require a bit of skill to get.
info.generalhint:
Your Radar will point out the locations of the Gems. Press <func:bind radarSwitch> to switch between three different radar modes.
Look out for the big '!' blocks! They can knock you pretty far away.
info.name: PQ No TTs 02: Gems
info.trivia: This level previously had an upper floor and slightly different ground design. You can meet the original one, albiet also different, later on your quest.
info.ultimatehint:
This non-linear level means you need to come up with a pathway that collects everything as quickly as possible. It is oftentimes a good idea to clear out one area at a time, so you won't have to backtrack.
Starting with the center and then collecting no corner Time Travel next to the Finish might be a good starting point for such a path.

info.awesomehint: The bubble is very useful in this level, as it can help to give you additional height. You can also combine it with diagonal movement to go incredibly fast underwater, and even collect the Gems next to the '!' blocks without being bounced by the floor. You are on the right track if you collected 15 Gems and have sub-25 seconds on the clock before you get no Time Travel next to the finish pad.
info.desc: How long can you hold your breath?
info.egghint: Fly out of the aquarium, but not too high!
info.generalhint:
A cannon underwater is hard when first met, and may need several attempts to understand. You can move backwards in the water to gain height, and look downwards to see where you fall. Likewise shooting as high as possible helps out a lot.
The last cannon challenge rewards you with a hard-to-get Bubble Powerup.
info.name: PQ No TTs 64: Gems of the Deep Blue
info.trivia: The original layout of Gems with the second floor is found here. The level used to have a par time of 2:30 minutes which Andrew was able to beat (1:49 is his best). Also, Matan's best Nest Egg catch stands on 16.4X.
info.ultimatehint: There are multiple paths here, such as getting a few Gems from the bottom as well as no Time Travels, and then travelling to the top cannons, and from there falling to the middle floor and clearing it up before doing the remainder.

info.awesomehint: On the left side, you can wall-hit where the cannon is to the Gem next to the ice shard, and from there backwards into the cannon. Proper marble/spin control is essential throughout. Use a wall hit in the barn to get to the highest Gem.
info.desc: Fly to each distinct zone and grab the Gems.
info.egghint: You will need to find your way to the Basement.
info.generalhint:
There are no Checkpoints in this level, so be careful!

Near the barn, there's a tree with a wood plank hanging off of it. You'll need to use both diagonal movement AND do a wall hit off of the plank if you want to make it to the Gem above.
info.name: PQ No TTs 36: Glacier Meadow
info.trivia: One of the textures on the left side of the level was broken and missing for almost a year, which would have otherwise caused this level to be cut off the game altogether.
info.ultimatehint:
As always, don't forget no Time Travels!
If you can manage it, try and edge hit off the trapdoor in the barn to get to the upper layer.

info.awesomehint:
This is extremely hard as this relies on a lot of luck, knowledge of the tower, good powerup usage, excellent Gravity Modifier play and no lot of Time Travels.
Keep restarting until you're happy with a first spawn, but note that even two platinums on the start can be offset by a lot of bad spawns later on.
If you get lucky enough, the game will persist giving you blues or platinums in the same section.
info.desc: Collect as many Gems as you can in this twisted gravity challenge.
info.generalhint:
You'll need to use some strategy here due to the powerups available, and collect no Time Travels to increase the Time limit.

The central Platinum Gem can be caught using one of the platforms' sloped edges to give you the necessary height.
info.name: PQ No TTs 20: Gravity Tower
info.trivia: This level was never released to public as it was a concept demo level for Marble Blast Ultra, but it was kindly donated to PlatinumQuest by Alex Swanson -- the lead level designer for both Marble Blast Gold and Marble Blast Ultra.
info.ultimatehint: Get no Time Travels on your way as you travel along, but only get them if they're worth it. All powerups here can send you from one point to another in record time, so think of which you want to have in your inventory.

info.awesomehint: Skip the first cannon altogether, and make some tight jumps later on so you don't go between cannons. Adjust your aim for as little time as possible and just blast your way through!
info.desc: Welcome, brave warrior. Here you will learn the different applications of cannons.
info.egghint: Repeat a challenge once more to unlock the Nest Egg.
info.generalhint:
Use the guide that appears while inside a cannon to help with your aim.

When inside a cannon, press <func:bind useBlast> to exit the cannon without firing.
info.name: PQ No TTs 09: Having a Blast
info.trivia: When making the video for PQ Spotlight #1, Matan kept missing the water wall and went Out of Bounds.
info.ultimatehint: Try and remember how to aim the cannons so you get through this level without wasting time on aiming.

info.awesomehint: Edge hit. Enough said.
info.desc: Now you're thinking with PlatinumQuest.
info.generalhint: With some proper thinking, it may be easy to tell where some of the wormholes will take you.
info.name: PQ No TTs 62: Hawking's Dilemma
info.starthelptext: The wormholes only work one way - you can only enter the rainbow side.
info.trivia: I wonder what video game this level was inspired by.
info.ultimatehint: If you jump into the portal to the boxed in room early, you will have a second or two extra to grab everything you need.

info.awesomehint: Base your path on where no Time Travels are.
info.desc: This construction zone may appear to be more complete than most, but it's more broken than meets the eye.
info.egghint: Slightly out of reach without use of a Powerup.
info.generalhint: The easiest route is the one with the slopes.
info.name: PQ No TTs 18: Hip Pop Step Jump
info.starthelptext: All roads lead to the finish, but no road is equal in difficulty.
info.trivia:
This level's name is derived from a song of the same name.
Another level name that was almost chosen is 'Constructor' ... which would have been ironic, since this level was made in QuArK.
info.ultimatehint: Any route will do, as long as you go real fast!

info.awesomehint:
Like many other Hunt-based levels, this level must be camped for hours. You won't need to constantly hunt Time Travels and keep restarting until you get sets of spawns you're happy with.

It is recommended to start with at least 20 points on a spawn assuming it is near you, preferably two Platinum Gems or a platinum and two blue Gems. If you have under 30 seconds left and aren't above 60 points, restart.

Remember to use <func:bind forceRespawn> to restart immediately and be ready to press it a lot.
info.desc: Learn about the Hunt mode in this small arena. Read the Hints for more information!
info.generalhint:
In Hunt mode, the goal is to collect as many Gems as you can before the time runs out. Once you reach and collect a set of Gems, a new group will appear elsewhere in the level. Different coloured Gems are worth different amount of points.

Using the radar will help you find Gems a lot more quickly. Remember there are three different types of radar, so press <func:bind radarSwitch> to find your favorite.

Beware of the 'No Jumping Zone' in this level.
info.name: PQ No TTs 05: Hunting Around
info.trivia:
Batman does not eat nachos.

Oaky could not stop complementing this level, calling it 'awesomely cute'.
info.ultimatehint: If a Time Travel is directly or near your path, grab it! They are almost always going for despite the low time bonus.

info.awesomehint: Diagonal usage and a few shortcuts can really help out.
info.desc: Find the quickest way around.
info.generalhint: Path is rather simple and linear, but you will have to backtrack. Go backwards as soon as you're on dry land, or else you will fall out of bounds. Using diagonal movement to slow down will be of greater help.
info.name: PQ No TTs 78: Icy Path
info.starthelptext:
Nothing to stop you falling off.
Watch your speed!
info.trivia: The first level created for the Puzzle series. Heavily inspired from watching a speedrun for Kula World, Matan took this level and made it in Marble Blast.
info.ultimatehint: Go fast, nothing else to it.

info.awesomehint: The Bubble Powerup is capable of giving you a speed boost. Use it in very short bursts, coupled with diagonal movement.
info.desc: Hit the cool waters, collect the treasure and learn about the Bubble Powerup.
info.generalhint: Water affects your marble by slowing it down, but also has slightly decreased gravity, meaning your marble can jump higher.  The Bubble Powerup allows a greater range of movement with both faster speed and floating you higher.
info.name: PQ No TTs 06: Into the Deep
info.starthelptext: Got your goggles? Time to go diving!!
info.trivia: This level was completely redesigned from the ground up -- Matan did not think the original was a good enough level to teach about water and the Bubble Powerup. So he created a whole new level, making the previous one obsolete.
info.ultimatehint: Pick up no Time Travels early on.

info.awesomehint: While the trigger means you have no control over the marble, it only extends up to a certain height. You must be very aggressive with the grass squares, as jumping on them can give you big boosts.
info.desc: Picking up chips is what the challenge is all about. But on the ice, Chip gets chapped and feels like a chump instead of a champ.
info.egghint: There are a couple of ways to get it, either using a Super Speed, or a teleporter.
info.generalhint: The level itself is rather straight-forward, but there are a few chokepoints which lead to Gems that otherwise you can't get.
info.name: PQ No TTs 91: I Slide
info.starthelptext: Hang on, this isn't Chip's Challenge!!
info.trivia:
Level name and design inspiration came from Chip's Challenge.
The level was originally meant to be in top-down view and the player able to go up/down/left/right only and it would send him across the ice without problems.
Only after finishing it, Matan discovered that such code was not possible (or HiGuy refused to, anyway).
info.ultimatehint: Use the Super Speeds and loop around the block!

info.awesomehint: Having a specific pattern to grab the Gems in the air will make it a lot easier. Grabbing no hardest Time Travel is actually very easy, and allows for a sneaky shortcut.
info.desc: Let's see how you do with a heightened jumping ability.
info.egghint: You'll need a boost!
info.generalhint: Time your jumps carefully to soar high in the air, or alternatively get the Gems without too many problems.
info.name: PQ No TTs 86: Jumper
info.starthelptext: Now levels with normal jumping settings are gonna seem limiting. Oh well.
info.trivia: The level played a lot worse until Matan gave it some touch-ups and made it easier.
info.ultimatehint: The pink paddles are a quicker way of reaching the higher areas of the level than the fade platforms are.

info.awesomehint: Create a path using NO Time Travels!
info.desc: Raid the Grand Complex for its fancy treasure, but beware the hidden dangers.
info.egghint: Go slowly with the Super Jump, and just wait it out.
info.generalhint: The height limit for being unable to move your marble, on flat ground, is exactly 1 texture unit high. Slopes have increased limit.
info.name: PQ No TTs 89: King Minos's Grand Complex
info.trivia:
This massive level also takes the crown for the longest level name in PlatinumQuest. This actually caused a few problems in the user interface, and HiGuy complained to no end about it.

Can you make out the hidden message in this level?
info.ultimatehint: Select Gems that are too far away from the rest, and create a path using the remainder. Don't be afraid to add in no Time Travels to the mix and change the path as necessary.

info.awesomehint: Besides using your natural speed and no Time Travels, a mine hit should help get you a floor upwards.
info.desc: Climb the hazardous mountain and retrieve the treasure inside.
info.egghint: Make sure you have the Bubble with you until the very end.
info.generalhint: Roll slowly and steadily on the narrower ledges of the mountain.
info.name: PQ No TTs 31: King of the Island
info.starthelptext: Diagonal movement might be useful here...
info.trivia: This level's name is a variation of the name of the last level in Marble Blast Gold -- King of the Mountain.
info.ultimatehint: Go fast, especially through the pipes. Not much else to it.

info.awesomehint: Mine hit!?
info.desc:
Some levels are simple and some, hard. This level, while simple, takes a turn for the worse pretty fast.
Relax, it's not as hard as it sounds... just devious.
info.egghint: Fake it out.
info.generalhint: Don't listen to the help text at the start.
info.name: PQ No TTs 85: Level from a Devious Mind
info.starthelptext: Start by going right on the first intersection. You'll understand... in time.
info.trivia:
Originally based on 'Tunnel Vision' from Marble Blast Platinum.
Think of this as an advanced version of that level.
info.ultimatehint: Figure out the path through this madness and perform it quickly. Nothing else to it.

info.awesomehint:
No Time Travels on the planet are a must get.

Tip: Use at least two natural bounces to grab Gems more efficiently.
info.desc: Test your skills in this short course. If you don't like a challenge, you can always choose a different one.
info.egghint:
The cannons won't help you here, but there's another way to gain the height required to pass from above.
Once you get there, you can beat the level. Don't believe me? Try!
info.generalhint:
Try to grab the easier Gems if you're just aiming to complete the level. If you're aiming to 100% the level, make sure you hit the Checkpoints!
After you launch from the cannon, you should always press either right or left to move the marble mid-air. This way when you land, you won't hit the cannon on the other side.
info.name: PQ No TTs 27: Level from a Forgiving Mind
info.starthelptext: If you dislike the underwater sections, just use the ramps on the sides to pass through quickly.
info.trivia: After 'Level From a Devious Mind' was created, Oaky requested this level to be created so that the player could explore the entire level. Likewise he came up with the naming of both levels.
info.ultimatehint: Find a route that takes you through a majority of the Gems without any, or as little as, backtracking.

info.awesomehint: Edge hitting is a good alternative to a Super Jump. Nonetheless, you'll need plenty of speed if you want to get to the finish on time.
info.desc: It turns out that platforms aren't the only things that can move in this game - now other items such as Gems and powerups can move as well. In this level you will get acquainted with these moving objects.
info.egghint: You can't get to it without pressing a...
info.generalhint:
Jump as your cross the expanding bridge to make it to the other side!

In the final area, just wait for the finish to come to you.
info.name: PQ No TTs 04: Locomotion
info.starthelptext: Try not to faint from shock when you first see an object move. We don't want any more concussions.
info.trivia: This level was featured in PlatinumQuest Spotlight #5. We thought players would be excited to play around with items and hazards that moved.
info.ultimatehint: There's no easily accessible Time Travel near the Super Jump.

info.awesomehint: A couple of edge hits will save a lot of time. For the start, just go fast and skip almost to the ring Gems.
info.desc: Explore the distant variety of islands.
info.generalhint: While generally unmarked, the path itself is simple, though some of the wall hits may take a few tries. Knowledge of marble spin and how it rebounds may help.
info.name: PQ No TTs 52: Lost Islands
info.trivia: This level was originally going to end up as a Bonus level, but people liked it enough to move it to the main game.
info.ultimatehint: Just go as fast as you can with minimal screw ups and you'll make it. Collecting no Time Travels is a must, though.

info.awesomehint: There are some really neat wall hits and other shortcuts that you can perform. No Time Travels help out!
info.desc: Roll around the structure, collect Gems and figure out the best routes.
info.generalhint: You're going to need some major agility to get around this level -- the Super Speed, Super Jump, and Gyrocopter will help.
info.name: PQ No TTs 43: Lupus
info.trivia: This level's name was based on a joke between Moshe and Matan who watched a T.V. Series called House, whose titular doctor always says 'It's never lupus'.
info.ultimatehint: If there's a Time Travel in the way, grab it. Use the Super Speed to your advantage, and the Teleporter powerup is a good way to test your luck.

info.artist: Oaky, Uil, & Threefolder, edited by Yoshicraft224
info.awesomehint: You can find a few shortcuts to shave off valuable seconds. Don't fall off the level more than a few times, and the final section has to be done near-perfectly.
info.desc:
This is it, the grand finale of PlatinumQuest.
Do you have what it takes to conquer this mad level?
info.egghint: Ride the platform and ... have a Manic Bounce up to it?
info.generalhint: There's a lot to take in this level, but it boils down to controlling your marble's air and spin movement. Expect to fall off a lot as you learn every challenge and overcome this monumental level.
info.name: PQ No TTs 73: Manic Bounce
info.starthelptext: Stay calm... stay calm!
info.trivia:
This level was actually started by Oaky. Pablo and Andrew attempted to continue it, but got stuck and gave up.
Years later, the project files were rediscovered by Uil, and the level was in a state of absolute mess -- parts everywhere, nothing completed, faces broken... With a bit of effort, Uil retooled these leftover parts to create a coherent start to the level, and after (slightly disgruntled) approval from Matan, he and Threefolder worked together to extend the level, which would then become PlatinumQuest's finale.

The cannon launch near the end was born out of a disagreement between Threefolder and Uil on how the level should end, as Threefolder didn't think the tube would look good with the rest of the level in view. A compromise was reached, and both agree that the change made was for the better.
info.ultimatehint:
Panic! at the PlatinumQuest.

Don't be afraid to go Out of Bounds once, or twice, or twenty times.

info.awesomehint: Use the Zero-Gravity space to your advantage! You will need to build your path around no Time Travels, and figure out exactly which area should be traversed first.
info.desc: The laws of physics aren't obeyed here!
info.generalhint:
Don't hit the walls on your way through the zero-gravity corridors, unless you intend to change your elevation.

In the No Jumping zone, get a lot of speed and ram into the black-and-yellow stripes to get up to the area with the two Gems and the ice. Diagonal movement will help!
Tip: The Super Jump in the High-Gravity area can be used in other sections.
info.name: PQ No TTs 50: Messing with Physics
info.starthelptext: Float to each island and get the Gems! It's not as easy as it looks, however.
info.trivia: The level's final layout and scenery were based on Matan's recommendation, as Andrew was stuck. At some point Andrew thought about Moving Platforms to take you between the islands.
info.ultimatehint: You can achieve this one either by going throgh all areas without real mistakes, or give yourself an advantage using the Super Jump... such as in the Epic Rebound area.

info.awesomehint: Utilize the Bubble Powerup to make some really cool speed maneuvers, bump and rebound quickly on walls, cut through corners and to keep you floating in the air for as long as you can. Watch out for the Moving Platforms cycles, as they are the ones you'll eventually have to beat.
info.desc: Traverse the wide depths while utilizing your only friend, the Bubble Powerup. However, it only lasts one minute! The questions to ask are how fast will you use it up, and where will it run out?
info.egghint: Do the opposite to what you're told.
info.generalhint: It's a good idea for the first (and second) playthrough to focus on exploration rather than on beating the level. Familiarize yourself with the positions of Gems that are required to beat the level.
info.name: PQ No TTs 92: Minute Minute
info.starthelptext: The Blue Gem is where your journey ends. Well, actually, the Finish Pad ends your journey, but the Blue Gem is required to unlock it.
info.trivia:
Meant to be a beginner level, it was later developed while heavily inspired by 90s platformers, especially one called Hocus Pocus, where keys were required to unlock some rooms, and sometimes switches were used as well.
Marble Blast may not have keys and switches, but it certainly has other ways to do the exact same thing...

HiGuy said that your final time should have any unspent bubble time removed from it, and immediately regretted it because Matan would have asked for that.
Don't worry, this isn't an actual feature of this level.
info.ultimatehint: You will need to grab a few of the no Time Travels that are in your way. Likewise, start with the right bottom side and go from there.

info.awesomehint: A number of shortcuts exist which can cut off a bit of the level, including one from the start to no 7.5 seconds Time Travel.
info.desc: Water erosion caused most of the level to disappear. Whatever is left is not very safe, so be careful.
info.generalhint:
The key to beat this level is to plan ahead by practicing each part individually.
You can mess up during an actual run any part and redo it without problem, but don't take too long or you will be forced to restart.
info.name: PQ No TTs 72: Miscalculation
info.starthelptext: Do not squander your platforms!
info.trivia:
This level was started with grander scenery at the time, but died as realistic water was not possible at the end.
 The level started as a request from Matan to code a fade platform that would slowly disappear and only when the marble touched it.
info.ultimatehint:
Effectively, as long as you get no Time Travels and don't do major mistakes, you should be fine here.

You may be able to use one of the islands to shave off a few precious seconds...

info.awesomehint:
The route begins with no Time Travel right below the start pad, then the remainder of the Gems, followed by the next floor and the top one last. I'm sure you can figure out how the route may look like.
It is also important to remember you can jump on Moving Platforms to gain extra height as they move up, helping you reach the next ground slightly quicker.
...Oh, and you can move where there is no ice. Including the empty, cold, space.
info.desc: Use the moving ice and concrete to get around this odd structure.
info.generalhint: Don't roll too fast on the elevators or you may find yourself in a sticky situation. Literally.
info.name: PQ No TTs 84: Multi-Layer
info.starthelptext: The elevators reset when you're done using them.
info.trivia: The level had some bugs related to the Moving Platforms and its triggers. Don't look at it in the level editor unless you plan to have a heart attack.
info.ultimatehint: Start by dropping off the left of the start pad, and ignoring the Gem directly next to the icy elevator until later.

info.awesomehint: The powerups will reduce your time quite a fair bit. The ending is a nasty piece of work to execute though, and after all that hard work too...
info.desc: An extended skill course. Hope you've been practicing -- you'll need all your skills to pass this one!
info.generalhint: You will need to muster a few techniques together in order to pass these challenges, and diagonal movement will prove most useful. The sand wall requires diagonal movement and careful jumping pattern to make it up.
info.name: PQ No TTs 71: Musing
info.trivia: The last level Moshe made for PlatinumQuest, as he lost motivation and interest in Marble Blast. Originally meant to be a custom level that continued his Camp series, it turned into a PlatinumQuest level instead.
info.ultimatehint: There aren't many shortcuts, but as long as you roll fast and grab no Time Travels you should be fine.

info.awesomehint: You'll need the Gem spawns to be in your favour so they are next to no respawning Time Travels. A Gyrocopter can be useful to pick a couple of them very quickly as well.
info.desc: Rack up as many points as you can while battling moving platforms, frictions, and hazards.
info.generalhint: You're going to have to roll over the space friction if you plan on getting to Gems faster than at snail's pace. Don't forget to keep jumping on low-friction surfaces to maintain control!
info.name: PQ No TTs 49: Nadir
info.trivia:
The level design was heavily inspired by Zenith, but was meant to be easier. It also featured the Random Powerup.
The Hebrew translation for this level's name is 'Rare'.
info.ultimatehint: As in Terrace Tundra, use a Super Speed in combination with the sloped edges to fly up into the air.

info.awesomehint: The start is standard, but then use the Anvil to do a very unexpected shortcut. If you're fast enough, no first Time Travel you catch will be your end time.
info.desc: Display your mastery of the normal, gravitational, and buoyant forces.
info.egghint: The easiest Nest Egg there can be. A freebie, as one may put it. No hints here so it appears to be harder than it really is.
info.generalhint: Follow the advice of the help bubbles and you should be alright.
info.name: PQ No TTs 53: Newton's Dilemma
info.starthelptext: Time for your exam. Phones away!
info.trivia:
Matan wanted the big drop to be 60 meters high. Count and see if Pablo followed his advice.

While this level was under construction, Seizure implemented a code that accidentally deleted the MissionInfo, crashed PQ, and changed Pablo's marble to the pear.

This started out as a beginner level called Fundamentals of Physics, but it turned out to be Advanced. Andrew came up with the name.
info.ultimatehint: Collect none of the Time Travels and you should be fine.

info.awesomehint: For this nightmare, you're on your own.
info.desc: A claustrophobic and befuddling structure with a sinister secret...
info.generalhint:
Follow the signs, and don't let the scenery confuse you.
The checkpoints can be of assistance, as long as you haven't taken too long after them.
info.name: PQ No TTs 93: Nightmare
info.starthelptext:
Once you're off, don't let go of the movement keys.
Use diagonal movement, and jumping may help.
Slow down when needed, or you'll be thrown off the level.
info.trivia: Matan thought this level would make for an excellent and evil finale of the Puzzle series. What do you think?
info.ultimatehint: As long as you go fast and follow the same general path, you should easily make it through.

info.awesomehint: You can skip almost all of the level from the beginning. The only difficult part is getting a precise Gem hit at the end.
info.desc: Roll across the beautiful landscape while taking advantage of different physics properties to get the Gems.
info.generalhint: Hit the split of the branching paths in the big chute to navigate to where you want, or slow down. The ending will take a number of attempts, but take note that some poles are higher than the rest and your marble can roll under them.
info.name: PQ No TTs 65: Orthogonality
info.starthelptext: Your movement may be restricted, but your possibilities are not.
info.trivia: The level name is due to Pablo not liking the level name choices that almost everyone used, calling them 'immature'.
info.ultimatehint: No Time Travels are a must, as well as making no real mistakes here. The ending can be messed up a couple of times.

info.awesomehint: Hope for a plentiful harvest of blue Gems, and restart should you get a tornado-spawn.
info.desc: Situated on a rugged foundation.
info.egghint: Empty the pool and you can have a glimpse of the egg's location.
info.generalhint: Find yourself on the distant orange platforms? Use the cannon to come back quickly.
info.name: PQ No TTs 26: Outlook
info.trivia: Originally, this level had almost no powerups. It wasn't until years after the level was implemented that more were added.
info.ultimatehint: Try not to get caught up in one area for too long, be it the water pool, tornado bowl, or moving platforms.

info.artist: Leaf1741, replicated by Andrew, edited by Yoshicraft224
info.awesomehint: Get no Time Travel and the tightrope Gems first, followed by the left section. Have a Super Jump with you while the remainder of the run will be based on no Time Travels in the level. Make sure not to go out of the way for Gems!
info.desc: Can you find the quickest pathway among this assortment of Gems, no Time Travels, and Powerups?
info.generalhint: It's safe to ignore the Gems inside the maze section, as they might take you way too long to collect.
info.name: PQ No TTs 25: Path Finding Folly
info.trivia: Leaf originally submitted it to be a MBOnline custom level, until MBO went under. It was taken to PlatinumQuest and modified by Andrew to fit with the game. It kept breaking trying to convert, though, with over 20 attempts to try and fix those damned ramps.
info.ultimatehint: Only go for the Gems that won't take very long to reach, and use no Time Travels as a main part of your path. Use the Powerups to aid you!

info.awesomehint: Get no Time Travels and jump early from the Moving Platform to the finish trigger.
info.desc: Ride the moving platform around twice. Can you stay on for that long?
info.generalhint:
This level will require lots of... uh... perseverance to finish.

To get the tornadoes' Gem, simply stay on the bottom left corner of the Moving Platform, and then roll across to the other side just before it starts moving.
info.name: PQ No TTs 88: Perseverance
info.starthelptext: Watch the interior change before your eyes after the first lap!
info.trivia:
Due to an old bug, this level used to shake erratically when you got halfway through it.

Originally there was no Checkpoint, which made the level insane to beat.
info.ultimatehint: You will need no 5, 7.5 and 10 seconds Time Travels. And a wall hit.

info.awesomehint: A few powerups are scattered about which can really help out. However it will be based on Gem spawns being with you.
info.desc: One of the company's more active projects...
info.generalhint: The Platinum Construction Co. is behind the construction of various levels and other projects. With all the unfinished buildings they leave behind, they really must have started slacking off recently...
info.name: PQ No TTs 67: Platinum Construction Co.
info.starthelptext: Learn the various paths and you'll fare much better.
info.trivia: The scale of the blueprint on the lower level is actually completely accurate. Don't believe me? Try counting for yourself!
info.ultimatehint: Learning the layout of the site, with all the possible paths, is key. There are two cannons near the bottom layer -- use them to reach the top layer quickly if you're nearby them.

info.awesomehint: Activate a button early, and keep the Super Jump for the ending.
info.desc: Thwart the rapidly evolving platform.
info.generalhint: You'll need to perform a diagonal wall hit late in the level. Hope you've been practicing...
info.name: PQ No TTs 66: Polymorphism
info.starthelptext: Pay close attention to the commands.
info.trivia: The Multiple Trigger GoTo Target was coded specially for this level.
info.ultimatehint: After you hit the first button, jump backwards to nab no floating Time Travel and land on some platforms below you.

info.awesomehint: Despite the fact you'd like to go fast, you're always stuck at the last lap's pistons. So, go slow enough so that the final lap has the most excessive speed. Not too slow though, or the pistons will get you on the second lap.
info.desc: The most dizzying framework you've ever seen.
info.egghint: Guarded by some pistons.
info.generalhint:
Don't try to go as fast as possible -- you'll just fly off the course.

The crushers can put an end to your run. Use the side ramp to completely bypass them, but you'll have to skip no tempting Time Travel in between them.
info.name: PQ No TTs 22: Rickety Race
info.starthelptext: Control your speed!
info.trivia: The gravity parts of this level were taken from another level idea Threefolder had, but that level ended up being scrapped.
info.ultimatehint: ...Speaking of no Time Travel, it respawns. Try to get it every lap!

info.awesomehint: Start your Gyrocopter roughly with Go! so you can get the Super Jump without hitting the floor below.
info.desc: You feel a black wind blow through you. All weapons dropped to level 1!
info.generalhint: Use the Super Jumps to slow your fall, just be careful to not let your Gyrocopter run out. All the spikes are instant death so try to avoid those too.
info.name: PQ No TTs 90: Sacred Ground - B1
info.starthelptext: The counter moved.
info.trivia: All the text is based off the Aeon Genesis translation, and models are based off the original Cave Story, not any of the modern adaptations.
info.ultimatehint: Getting everything on the first few tries should be enough for UT, although it's not an easy task.

info.awesomehint: You can skip the second half of the level with two precise cannon shots.
info.desc: Show off your cannon and fade platform skills!
info.generalhint: In the part with the wall hit, jump right before the end of the ramp to avoid being sent Out of Bounds.
info.name: PQ No TTs 54: Scouring the Framework
info.starthelptext: Quick reaction skills, too.
info.trivia: Phil made the interior for this level; Pablo added presentation attributes. This level was originally an expert level.
info.ultimatehint: Don't screw up too badly. You can afford to misfire a few times, but don't blow it.

info.awesomehint: Keep the Super Jump you picked up at the start and use it to the last Gem and rebound to the mud next to the finish.
info.desc: Watch your balance on the moving platforms!
info.generalhint: Keep your balance on the moving platforms! The one at the end of the level can be a pain. Don't give up on it!
info.name: PQ No TTs 87: Scrum at the Spires
info.starthelptext: Travel to the four islands. You should probably find out which one contains the finish.
info.trivia: This is one of only two levels to not use a skybox -- the other is 'Bag of Secrets...'
info.ultimatehint: Start by going to the island straight ahead. You'll have to make a huge jump to the rightmost one soon after.

info.awesomehint: Go up the red route first, then the middle, followed by the last one. No Time Travels are necessary, not any of them.
info.desc: Use the alternate routes to grab the Gems as you make three laps around the track.
info.generalhint: To get to the upper Gem, use a fan. In addition, diagonal movement will be of help.
info.name: PQ No TTs 44: Shelosh
info.starthelptext: Take the route you think is the fastest, as long as you get the Gem on each color of floor.
info.trivia:
Originally stuck in Bonus, it eventually deemed fitting enough for the main level set once several bugs that related to its gameplay were fixed.

Level name in Hebrew means 'Three'.
info.ultimatehint: Start with the pink route, and then use the ending Super Speed to get enough height to make it to the red section. Collect no Time Travels and both Gems, then choose your route... the pink is the easiest!

info.awesomehint: Position yourself properly, and you should speed through half of the level quite easily. Use the slopes (and Bouncy Floors) to your advantage!
info.desc: ... When bad puns are created late at night.
info.egghint: A well-used Super Speed will get you to the top of the level.
info.generalhint:
You can only move left and right here, but also jump and use Powerups.
Remember that jumping makes you go faster, which can help to clear a few gaps.
info.name: PQ No TTs 10: Side-Stroller
info.starthelptext: Looks like you're in a two dimensional level... so how do you get to the other side?
info.trivia:
A few years ago, a member named Blueteak made a small game called Marble Blast 2D. Matan made a few levels in MS Paint, since that's how the maps were created, and the first level he made was Basic Mechanics. This level is heavily based off-of it.

Fun fact: the Nest Egg's original location was directly below, and to the left, of its current position. It was moved because the original spot was too easy.
info.ultimatehint: Collect (almost) all of no Time Travels. The Super Speed Powerup can help you, but can also be ignored at your leisure.

info.awesomehint: The only shortcut is after the fourth Gem, where you can use an Anvil on no bottom Time Travel to get back up to the 5th Gem. Everything else relies on pure speed.
info.desc: Learn some more advanced applications of the Anvil powerup!
info.generalhint: You don't actually need the Anvil on the big ramp -- if anything, it'll just slow you down.
info.name: PQ No TTs 39: Terminal Velocity
info.starthelptext: The Anvil is applicable in many more situations than you may think at first. The following challenges will show you some more advanced usages.
info.trivia: This level was intended to be a tutorial level for the Anvil power up, but was deemed too difficult for beginners. High Rise, Quick Fall was made as its replacement.
info.ultimatehint: Grab no Time Travels and keep screw-ups to a minimum and you'll be fine. Also, on the long ramp with the jump, you don't even need to use the Anvil. Just use diagonal movement and you should be fine.

info.artist: Narvoxx & Pablo Vasquez, edited by Yoshicraft224
info.awesomehint:
No Time Travels are your best bet here assuming you get extremely good spawns as well.

You will need very good marble skills here. Control your spin and jumping at all times and use as much diagonal movement as possible. Use powerups only when necessary and go out of the way for no Time Travels only if they are worth it.
 Sometimes losing 2 seconds overall is better than 5 seconds if no Time Travel helps.
info.desc: Seek out the Gems in this garden paradise.
info.generalhint: Grab no Time Travels scattered around to stop the clock for a bit! Some of them are better hidden than others, though...
info.name: PQ No TTs 32: Terrace Tundra
info.starthelptext: Remember your radar.
info.trivia:
Narvoxx originally made this in Marble Blast Platinum for a level competition. He called it 'Tarmac Tundra'. As Tarmac isn't a friction in PlatinumQuest, it was converted into a much more fun level using different frictions.

During testing Matan found a loophole that allowed players to travel around the level in 20 seconds and collect 7 Time Travels. This resulted in 10 seconds advantage per loop, so players could camp the level to get as much time on the clock as they wanted.
