After hours of work and testing, Matan greatly increased the respawn time of Time Travels, but also increased the chances of which blue and platinum Gems spawn.
info.ultimatehint: You should use the powerups here for your advantage. It's obvious how a Gyrocopter and a Super Jump will help you, but the Super Speed allows for some nifty movement when combined with the trim slopes.

info.artist: Oaky, finished by Pablo Vasquez, edited by Yoshicraft224
info.awesomehint: You'll have to devise a route here, but let's be honest, it could get rather maddening.
info.desc: Gather up as many points as possible. Planning will be essential if you wish to do well!
info.egghint: The answer is: he did.
info.generalhint:
This garden is more dynamic than it looks at first glance...
Try exploring it and see what you can find.
info.name: PQ No TTs 41: The Spoils of Serendipity Gardens
info.starthelptext: Will you be able to loot any of the platinum Gems?
info.trivia: This level was shown off in Feature Spotlight #3.
info.ultimatehint: Don't spend too long in one area. There are Gems everywhere! You'll probably need both platinum Gems to reach the Ultimate Score, so make sure you know where those are.

info.awesomehint:
This one is clever, yet tough: Use the checkpoints as a launch pad.
Additionally, start by getting the right Gem first. You can cross the gap and if you slow down fast enough you will get the Gem, hit the edge and rebound successfully without falling down.
info.desc: Learn about the fading platforms, preferably without falling off.
info.generalhint: Most of the time, there's no way of telling how each Fade Platform will function -- tread cautiously.
info.name: PQ No TTs 06: Trained to Fade
info.trivia:
Phil originally developed the Fade Platforms in response for the need of a better trapdoor, one with a similar mechanism to that of the trapdoor, but also something new.
While thinking of an introduction level for the Fade Platforms, Matan stumbled on an early design of a trapdoor introduction level by a different mod (this level no longer exists, sadly).
Liking the idea, but disappointed with its execution, Matan decided to set up a smaller and simpler level with faster challenges in the spirit of the split pathways.
info.ultimatehint: Get no Time Travel first, then go to the Fading Platforms to the left.

info.awesomehint: You may want to use a tree to skip to the end, and then complete the level in reverse.
info.desc: Solve simple puzzles by using the Teleport PowerUp to its utmost advantage.
info.egghint: Remember to pay attention to the caution stripes. After a short balancing act, you will be treated to an indoor slalom.
info.generalhint: The Teleport PowerUp is especially helpful for getting back up from places that are too far down.
info.name: PQ No TTs 11: Transporter Lock
info.starthelptext: Once you have a Teleport PowerUp, press <func:bind mouseFire> to set your location. Press it again to teleport.
info.trivia: This level replaced an old level that also taught about the Teleporter powerup. While the old level wasn't bad, there were quite a lot of issues with it.
info.ultimatehint: Keep in mind that the Teleport PowerUp has a short delay. By activating it preemptively, you can collect the Gems while the teleportation is occurring and shave off those crucial seconds.

info.awesomehint: Just like Pitfalls!
info.desc: Roll along the winding road, avoiding its gaps and obstacles.
info.generalhint: One of the earliest levels created for PlatinumQuest, it was obviously inspired by Marble Blast Gold's beginner level, Pitfalls.
info.name: PQ No TTs 74: Treacherous Pits
info.trivia: One of the very first levels made by Matan for PlatinumQuest, it utilized the newly made Fade Platforms, but was scrapped for just not being too original or creative.
info.ultimatehint: You won't need the Time Travels not here as long as you move fast enough. Of course getting one or two would help.

info.awesomehint: You can cut through the level quite easily with three Fireballs.
info.desc: Since the Ice Shard incident, these things have gone out of control. After thorough research we developed the Fireball Powerup, which may be our best hope.
info.egghint: Clear the Ice Shards!... or not.
info.generalhint:
The Fireball will not enter your inventory, but instead be used instantly and be active for a set amount of time. The timer next to your marble indicates how long your Fireball will remain active, and whether you have a Fire Blast charged or not.
In addition, every time you hit an Ice Shard, you will lose half a second on your Fireball.
info.name: PQ No TTs 16: Trial by Fire
info.starthelptext: Let's crank up the heat on those pesky Ice Shards!!
info.trivia:
Pablo came up with the level name. His alternatives were: Back Burner and Burning the Midnight Oil.
Also if you want, try and beat this level without using the Fireball powerup... it is EXTREMELY HARD!
info.ultimatehint: You can use the Fire Blast coupled with the slope in front of the Moving Platform to easily skip it. In addition, using Jump and Fire Blast can clear a lot of height and net you no Time Travels a lot more quickly, or skip certain challenges.

info.awesomehint: Use the Super Speed!
info.desc: A variety of obstacles in a three-part level. Can you slide your way through?
info.generalhint:
Don't be too concerned if you miss one Gem, as you only need four out of five to complete the level.

When entering the launcher, try to time your entrance so you get launched while right next to the blocks that push you out.
info.name: PQ No TTs 23: Triple Action
info.trivia:
During construction, this level was often referred to as Ticklish Alligator. Don't let this level bite you!

Originally this was made for the Marble Mini-Golf Community Group Level, but only a third of the level was finished by the deadline. Now you get the full version!
info.ultimatehint: If you grab the first four Gems, you can easily perform a massive shortcut later on. Also, get as many Time Travels as you can. Some are harder than others.

info.awesomehint: Ideally, you want a starting spawn with two blues or more, and the yellow island potentially spawns four blues in one cluster. Try to have at least 80 gems as the clock hits 1 minute, this includes collecting zero Time Travels.
info.desc: Seek the Gems that are spread across three distinct islands!
info.generalhint: The cannons aren't the only way to move between islands. Try using a powerup, or find a teleporter!
info.name: PQ No TTs 24: Triple Trail
info.trivia: Older versions of this level allowed the player to gain an infinite amount of time through collecting the then-quickly respawning Time Travels over and over again.
info.ultimatehint: No Time Travels take 80 seconds to respawn, so you can't collect each of them twice, adding a full minute to your time limit. Keeping track of the islands may also help for pathing.

info.awesomehint: Time the first wheel cycle and watch the rest fall into place. Oh, and wheels can be useful!
info.desc: Practice your climbing and landing skills.
info.generalhint: The wheels are very slow. You should be able to shoot through the gaps if you time your shot right as a blade moves out of the way.
info.name: PQ No TTs 13: Verticality
info.starthelptext: Control your spin to make sure that you stay on the level when you land.
info.trivia: Matan recommended adding grass to the triangle cutouts on the walls.
info.ultimatehint: Diagonal movement can slow you down even faster after launching from a cannon.

info.awesomehint: You'll need no Time Travels, twice. You will also require luck so you get good Gem spawns and not some crappy ones.
info.desc: A unique playground composed of three distinctive zones. Watch out for the hazardous construction area, or sit back and enjoy the flora.
info.generalhint: Use the Bumpers in the water to your advantage. They can give you the height you need to escape the pool much more easily.
info.name: PQ No TTs 40: Vibrancy Grounds
info.trivia: Inspired by 'Color Twist' by CyberFox in Marble Blast Advanced, a similar yet larger level was created in PlatinumQuest. The result was a good looking level that didn't play well. Eventually, that level was remade into this one.
info.ultimatehint: Use the Super Jump and the level's sloped structure to your advantage.

info.awesomehint: Nothing special here. Make sure you know where to shoot with each cannon.
info.desc: Find the path through the ever-changing hallways.
info.generalhint: Things are not always what they seem...
info.name: PQ No TTs 55: Waves in the Dark
info.starthelptext:
Ride this platform across the water.
You'll need to take a bit of a detour, though.
info.trivia: This level was partially inspired by both Antichamber and The Stanley Parable. Surprisingly, it wasn't inspired by Portal at all.
info.ultimatehint: Go for no highest value Time Travels, and take your time near the end of the level.

info.awesomehint: Go back and jump over the big gap.
info.desc: Take an introductory lap for this puzzle series.
info.generalhint: Jump while on the ice to help you maintain momentum. Use the curves to your advantage!
info.name: PQ No TTs 76: Welcome Lap
info.starthelptext: On the ice you can't move your marble, but you can still jump.
info.trivia: Some people preferred this level to be an actual laps level rather than have Gems. Matan felt it would make the level too long and hard.
info.ultimatehint: Jump as you're about to fall on the big downwards slope with no Time Travel. This means you won't have too much speed as you fall down on it, and thus can quietly press backwards and slow down at the end.

info.awesomehint: You'll need some good luck here, both in Gem spawns, but also with the tides being in your favour. Keep retrying and get a feel for the level, as a few shortcuts can't hurt.
info.desc: A playground with a twist.
info.egghint:
Did this egg bore a hole into a wall? Or maybe the hole was already there, and it fell in? What kind of bird lays an egg inside a cave?
Whatever... the point is that cave eggs exist and you need to find this one.
info.generalhint:
The bubble powerup has several maneuvers, some of which are based on jumping and activating the bubble at the same time.
If you can't be bothered, just grab a Super Jump or a Gyrocopter to help you out.
Be patient, the level has plenty of high-scoring Gems and their chances to spawn are higher than normal.
info.name: PQ No TTs 47: Wonky Waters
info.starthelptext: Collect as many Gems as you can while fighting the unsteady tides.
info.trivia:
Matan wanted to try out a playground-styled level for Hunt mode, but one with depth as well, this level was the result. The big ray wall texturing on the slopes that define the level's depth took 3 hours to create.
The code to make the water move was simple enough in the old standalone, but absolutely pissed off HiGuy when he had to recreate in order to make it Online compatible.
info.ultimatehint: Have you explored the whole level yet? There are ways to get some extra playing time!

info.awesomehint: The biggest two shortcuts are based on an edge hit at the start and using the Shock Absorber at the end... only once!
info.desc: These skyscrapers may be incomplete, but that won't stop you from rolling around on them, will it?
info.egghint: Easy to see, hard to get. Try an edge hit.
info.generalhint: Don't get distracted by the moving parts, as most of them will move into place before you reach them.
info.name: PQ No TTs 38: Work in Progress
info.trivia: This level's name was very appropriate during its' creation. It was started, creation went smoothly, but then Threefolder couldn't figure out how to end it. It then went on hiatus for over a month, while two different levels were completed.
info.ultimatehint: OSHA did in fact approve a few shortcuts for this level, but they won't tell you where...

info.awesomehint: Slow down before getting to the bouncy part, or else you'll be too high off the ground! That won't help you get the time you want.
info.desc: Get the gems on the way to the finish!
info.generalhint: Jump and roll forwards while on the half-pipe to make your marble higher off the ground!
info.name: Frictional Half-Pipe
info.trivia: This is a result of me when playing in Constructor for too long.
info.ultimatehint: It is nesessary to get all Time Travels.

remarks: Not much to say here.

info.desc: Complete level using Super Speed.
info.starthelptext: Grab the gems!
info.name: Super Speed

info.desc: Don't get blown off this tiny course!
info.generalhint: Use the fans in all their intended ways.
info.name: Fight The Wind!
info.starthelptext: Fans can helpful and harmful to the marble.

remarks: My attempt at a Duct Fan tutorial level.

info.desc: Go to each section to grab a gem , then go to the goal. Try to get the best time!
info.name: Marble Agility Course (Light)
info.starthelptext: How will you go the finish?

remarks: Comment Below!

info.starthelptext: Leap over the gaps to grab the floating gems.
info.desc: Cross over the deadly gaps to get the required objects floating above them.
info.name: Hop for gems

remarks: Comment below how is the level!

info.desc: Avoid the hazards on different surfaces so as not to fall off!
info.starthelptext: Jump on this bumper to begin.
info.name: Escape the hazards

remarks: Comment Below!

info.desc: Test your rolling and jumping skills!
info.name: Hop Hop
info.starthelptext: Try to collect all Time Travels!

info.desc: Solve all the challenges involving the Teleporter.
info.easteregghint: A teleporter somewhere will take you directly to the egg. Can you find where it is?
info.generalhint: Yellow tiles are instant OOB. Blue tiles will wait a specific amount of time before sending you OOB.
info.name: Warp Trials
info.starthelptext: Welcome to Warp Trials! Several challenges await you.
info.trivia: This level was originally called "Teleport Practice".
info.ultimatehint: Take shortcuts, and most importantly, don't fall off!

remarks: Name suggested by Ralph

info.desc: NOW IM 11YEARS OLD!
info.starthelptext: hi im kodas314 and this is 13.12.24 (13 december 2024 year) and it's my birthday!!
info.name: 11th KODAS'ES BIRTHDAY

remarks: yahooo!

info.name: Chain Necklace
info.desc: Literally, the chain.
Aim the ball carefully.
info.name: Extreme Bouncing!

info.desc: This pipeway used to take place somewhere...
info.name: Obsolete Pipeway

info.desc: Keep the balance.
info.name: Slanted Tightrope Climbing

info.desc: Grab the gems in these castles and fly over the lava chamber to the finish!
info.starthelptext: In the lava chamber of the castle fly to the goal!
info.name: Short level

remarks: comment below!

info.awesomehint: Ehh...
info.desc: Oh wow, blue looks so good in this.
info.easteregghint: Don't fill out this field for PQ levels. Easter Eggs are in the other games!
info.egghint: Get the gravity modifier and land on the finish sign. You'll see it.
info.generalhint: If you are stuck in a 1x1 block where it requires you to wallhit, please consider restarting your game.
info.name: Dizzy Wallhit 2
info.starthelptext: Watch your speed!
info.trivia: I skipped my swimming break so that I can make this level.
info.ultimatehint: You can find a gravity modifier in one of the holes to win fast.

remarks: replace old level

info.desc: You expect something more? It's just a Dumb Platform.
info.generalhint: Make sure to grab every gem as fast as you possibly can.
info.name: Dumb Platform
info.starthelptext: There's more than one way to skin a cat, unless you optimise.
info.trivia: Did you know? This is DoxtonPink's first Constructor level! Can you tell?

info.desc: Alright seriously? What is this? Amateur hour?
info.generalhint:
If you haven't played Dumb Platform, then here's the hint from that level:

Make sure to grab every gem as fast as you possibly can.
info.name: Dumber Platform
info.starthelptext: You know the routine.
info.trivia: Did you know? Constructor hates it when you try to make more than one triggered platform! Until a fix came for csx3dif (Thanks Randomity!)

info.desc: The multiplayer level from MBU & the series from MBP is remade for MBG!
info.name: MBG Battlecube
info.starthelptext: Get 25 gems in 2 minutes!

info.desc: It think you should complete this level without jumping.
info.name: Broken Jump Button

info.desc: There's more?! Let's hope this is the end, my brain can't handle this anymore.
info.easteregghint: You may not finish without all the gems!
info.generalhint:
The hint from the previous two levels (Dumb Platform and Dumber Platform) is relevant here, if you don't remember it, it goes something like this:

Make sure to grab every gem as fast as you possibly can.
info.name: Dumbest Platform
info.starthelptext: Just roll.
info.trivia:
Did you know? This is a reupload! The original version of this level has a static finish pad, which doesn't work on Haxe port. The onBound trigger was bugged on Webport.

You can find the original upload in the creator's level forum!

info.desc: Jump through platforms and don't fall!
info.name: Platform Dance
Quick Agility Course
info.desc: See how quickly you reach to the goal collecting all the gems without falling.
info.starthelptext: Ready..Set..Go!

info.awesomehint: Before going up the first elevators, you should have 0 Gems. Make sure to catch no Gems closest to you as well as zero Time Travels.
info.desc: Play on this beautiful construction site for a bridge. Observe the maritime traffic.
info.generalhint: No Gems are far more difficult to collect than others. Wisely choose which zero you'd like to skip.
info.name: PQ NGTT 33: A Bridge Too Hard
info.starthelptext: You look like a fit marble. It should be no problem climbing up some of the ropes here.
info.trivia: There used to be a Time Travel on the ship below, but it was removed as it made speedrunning the level far too frustrating.
info.ultimatehint: It's a good idea to catch no easy Gems on the top of the level, as well as some freebies scattered around. There is also no very nice 10 seconds Time Travel on the sand part of the bridge.

info.awesomehint: Switching gravity. Not even once.
info.desc: Looks can be deceiving.
info.generalhint: You will need to know your diagonal movement and wall hitting skills for this one.
info.name: PQ NGTT 49: Azimuth
info.trivia: This level was made while we were still learning what kind of levels we wanted for PlatinumQuest. You can see it didn't quite make the cut.
info.ultimatehint: You can finish sideways, and no Time Travels can be gotten in one sweep using a Super Jump.

info.artist: Phil, fixed by Threefolder, edited by Yoshicraft224
info.awesomehint: You may want to skip zero or zero of the Gems closest to the start and do a cool edge hit instead.
info.desc:
Most is magnificent...
All is...?
info.egghint: Did you read the level's description?
info.generalhint:
Be careful on the thin paths, and watch out for surprises.
There's no Gem right behind the start pad, so you really only have to collect 0 on the main structure to be able to finish.
info.name: PQ NGTT 28: Bag of Secrets...
info.trivia: PlatinumQuest originally had you unlock all levels in your own path, and this level was supposed to have an alternative exit that allowed you to skip further on the quest.
info.ultimatehint: Just go for no Gems that are lowest on the structure. The zero near the top aren't necessary and may just waste your time.

info.awesomehint: Preserve the Super Speed.
info.desc: Get into the swing of things.
info.egghint: Edge hit.
info.generalhint:
If you play with the music off, it's time to crank it up.

Count the beats in your head. The platforms switch every measure.

The last area's a bit tough, try to remember where the platforms will appear!
info.name: PQ NGTT 37: Blast to the Beat
info.starthelptext: If you wish to restart the level, try to do so on the beat so that the music doesn't de-sync.
info.trivia:
Yes, this level was inspired by Super Mario Galaxy.

After appearing in PlatinumQuest Trailer #2, it also spawned a "beep-block" custom level craze in the community that lasted a few weeks.
info.ultimatehint: Don't get caught up in one area for too long. Find a path that will allow you to speed through in the least amount of cycles possible.

info.awesomehint: Smart planning with the way you get no Gems and bounce off of walls can save you serious time. Use the Bubble in new ways!
info.desc: Swim through the floating water pockets in this cavern using your trusty Bubble.
info.generalhint:
Watch your momentum! Smacking into a wall with the bubble active will bounce you pretty far back.
If you're descending, try alternative between having the bubble on and off to slowly fall.
info.name: PQ NGTT 09: Bubble Cavern
info.starthelptext: Don't ask how the metal beams keep the water floating. We're not entirely sure, either.
info.trivia: Originally the Bumper section came before the no Gem section, and used Ice Shards instead of Bumpers.
info.ultimatehint: You will need to collect no Time Travel here, and switch between having your Bubble on and off throughout your navigation in the water. Keep moving at all times.

info.awesomehint: Get no Time Travels, but beware the zero in the air will be tough.
info.desc: Your camera is stuck in an isometric view. Get used to it and control the marble in a different way.
info.generalhint: The controls are the same as a normal level, but you'll have to realize that the gameplay will change a bit.
info.name: PQ NGTT 43: Camera Woes
info.trivia: Inspired by Crash Bandicoot's ball-playing levels, Matan wanted to create a 4-levels series, but lost motivation faster than he should have had. The code for this camera view exists though, so custom levels can use it.
info.ultimatehint: The path with the fade platforms is harder, but saves more time.

info.awesomehint: The closest Gems to you should be the zero you go for. You will have to one-shot no Gems or Time Travels you go for. The no Gems or Time Travels can be gotten together before going back to the cannons. Ensure the Gems you pick are the zero you'll bounce back to the starting area with.
info.desc: Test your sniping skills by picking off no Gems, or challenge yourself going for no harder Time Travels.
info.egghint: Explore the level, this one is really cool to find. Use the checkpoints to assist you.
info.generalhint: Go for no easier Gems. Since there are two Checkpoints next to the start pad, you can use them whenever you pick up no Gem.
info.name: PQ NGTT 29: Cannon Sniper
info.starthelptext: The cannon in front sends you to the finish.
info.trivia: Originally based on a crappy level of Matan's called Pipe Sniper, this level soon became inspired by an old custom level called 'Aim or Shame'. Eventually, a construction theme was deemed best, and that's the result you see in front of you.
info.ultimatehint: Don't miss TOO much, and definitely go for no Time Travels.

info.artist: Ian, replicated by Threefolder, edited by Yoshicraft224
info.awesomehint: Use the Teleport Powerup on the central ice area below the Start Pad. After that you can grab no Gems, make it to the top tightrope and back down on the sand slopes. Use the Teleport Powerup and get no remaining ice Gems, then do the outside challenges before falling down to the water section.
info.desc: Find as many Gems as you can. You don't have much time!
info.generalhint: The Teleport Powerup can be helpful to get whisked back to the top. Likewise, collect no Gems you'll find the easiest.
info.name: PQ NGTT 16: Castle Colossus
info.trivia:
The beginning of the camera path for this level is based on its appearance in PlatinumQuest Trailer #1.

This level had to be remade entirely from scratch because no one on the Platinum Team had the QuArK file for it.
info.ultimatehint: Don't bother with no Gems on the green outside bits. Focus on no Gems near the center of the level, and don't fall to the water area until you have less than 3 to go.

info.awesomehint: There's a nice route that takes no Time Travels and it's not hard to figure out. At the end you'll have to make a run to the finish or else you can't get this low time.
info.desc: Grab no Gems on this dizzying structure.
info.generalhint: The finish is a bit tricky to get to. You'll have to wait for some platforms to move by so you can use them to bridge the gap.
info.name: PQ NGTT 18: Centripetal Force
info.starthelptext: Make sure to take your momentum into account before you jump.
info.trivia: This level was created immediately after rotating platforms with real physics were deemed possible in the Torque engine.
info.ultimatehint: Playing the waiting game is sometimes a necessary evil.

info.awesomehint: Plan your TT catches for moments where you need to slow down. Try to avoid hitting the second sandy wall - time it so that you hit the slope at the top. There's a fun timesaver at the end of the 3rd lap - hint: you'll finish sideways!
info.desc: Chase after no Gems around the track. Can you get them all in 3 laps?
info.generalhint: Don't be afraid to slow down to grab no Gems picking up speed behind you. Be mindful of the Par Time, though.
info.name: PQ NGTT 39: Chasetrack
info.starthelptext: No cheating - you still have to do 3 laps!
info.trivia: The .mcs code for this level was generated entirely via Python. This level, with two paths each having over 200 pathnodes, plus a Technostick-style conveyor belt, would have taken weeks to make otherwise.
info.ultimatehint: Don't go for all the TTs in one lap - split them up so that you take different paths each lap, to avoid slowdown. The 45-degree trim is hugely important for keeping your speed.

info.awesomehint: Jumping on the ice slope is the key to this run. Don't get frozen though, there are plenty of spots to do that.
info.desc: Mind the Ice Shards.
info.generalhint: The moving platform section is probably the hardest part. Don't overcomplicate things, just try to find a straight-forward path up the icy slopes. If you can't do that, you can always stay on the moving platform and dodge the walls instead -- though, you'll lose a fair amount of time doing so.
info.name: PQ NGTT 23: Chilled
info.starthelptext:
You'll have to find a way to gain enough speed to finish.
Try not to freeze!
info.trivia:
This level and its general style were inspired by Freezing Point.

Originally, this level was in the Intermediate category, but the beginning section was enough to move it to Advanced.
info.ultimatehint: As long as you don't get frozen, you should be on the right track. Make sure to grab no Time Travels!

info.artist: Ian, replicated by Threefolder, edited by Yoshicraft224
info.awesomehint: Plan your jump pattern carefully, that makes it a lot easier.
info.desc: Skillshot no Gems on your way down!
info.egghint: See that fade platform behind the start pad? ...Good luck.
info.generalhint: You'll need to use plenty of diagonal movement for this one. Don't get caught on the bumpers in the pit by jumping and moving as close as possible to the wall.
info.name: PQ NGTT 19: Climb and Plummet
info.trivia: This is another level that had to be remade from scratch due to the Platinum Team not having a copy of its QuArK file.
info.ultimatehint: It's faster to grab no Gems or Time Travels on the way down, rather than on the way up.

info.awesomehint: Get no Time Travels, and remember you don't need every single Gem on the first lap.
info.desc: If you miss a Gem on the first lap, you can always grab none the second time around.
info.egghint: Remember how to loop exit?
info.generalhint:
Make sure you have no Gems before you complete your second lap or you'll have to restart the level.
As always with this sort of level, speed control is a necessity.
info.name: PQ NGTT 38: Conservation of Momentum
info.starthelptext: Haven't I seen this level before?
info.trivia: The ending of this level used to be much different -- after the space ramp, you would slam into a sandy wall and be teleported to just before the finish line. It was scrapped in favor of a more fluid approach.
info.ultimatehint: Slow down in the Ice Shard area so that you can grab no Gems or Time Travels. You'll also, obviously, want to collect as many Time Travels as you can.

info.awesomehint: Diagonal into no Time Travel and the rest is history.
info.desc: Four challenges, zero Time Travels, and only three seconds. Can you do it?
info.egghint: Look for a hidden switch.
info.generalhint:
No Time Travel re-spawns every 15 seconds, but it re-spawns only 7 times.
Whereas the checkpoints normally discard any of your active Time Travel bonus, in this level they do not, so you should use them to your advantage.
info.name: PQ NGTT 30: Dependency
info.starthelptext: No Time Travel lasts for 20 seconds, and will respawn every 15 seconds, but it will only respawn 7 times!
info.trivia:
The central starting area was done by Oaky; the four challenges were created by Andrew.

The concept of no Time Travel only respawning a certain amount of times was implemented late in development.
info.ultimatehint: The order you do everything doesn't matter -- just keep coming back to get no Time Travel.

info.awesomehint: Clear out the area furthest away from the start, and work your way towards the start point. After that, do the loop, grab no Gems at most and start the second floor.
info.desc: No corner Gem is HiGuy's fault.
info.generalhint: The lack of checkpoints means you will have to think before moving to the next areas.
info.name: PQ NGTT 48: Double Maze
info.trivia: This level is in fact two Puzzle series floors that Matan made and joined them into one.
info.ultimatehint: Jumping right before hitting the Gravity Modifier on the ice loop will give you some speed boost. You can, technicaly, finish the loop without the time restarting.

info.awesomehint: There are two cool wall hits to do: one at the start and one at the end. Make sure to get no Time Travels as well!
info.desc: Discover no Quota mode in this level. There are 0 Gems in this level total, but you'll only need half of them to finish.
info.generalhint: Quota mode allows you to create your own path in a level, by skipping Gems that might be too hard or too out of the way for you, while still allowing you to finish.
info.name: PQ NGTT 02: Downhill Skipping
info.starthelptext: You don't have to regret your decisions here.
info.trivia: This level replaced an old Quota tutorial somewhat late in development. The old level was designed to be more open-ended, but testing showed that it was far too confusing.
info.ultimatehint: Make sure to grab no Gems at the beginning of the level. No Time Travels could help...

info.awesomehint: Go fast and super tight, and try to abuse the marble collision boundary!
info.desc: The evil Titiritero has enchanted none of the no Gems and cursed none of the Time Travels. Will you be able to best him?
info.generalhint:
Avoid the Time Penalties! Go slower than you think you need to in order to stay on the level, unless you're a seasoned player.
Either way, you should have no problems staying under Par.
info.name: PQ NGTT 06: El Titiritero
info.starthelptext: Foolish marble! Why do you even bother challenging me?
info.trivia: The paths that the items follow were originally going to be entirely random, but this was never implemented out of fear of creating a heavily RNG-based level.
info.ultimatehint: No Gems or Time Penatlies don't follow random paths. You can easily plan your route.

info.awesomehint: You're going to circle a bit around the logo, and miss zero of the small Time Travels that is ever slightly out of your way.
info.desc:
Another game with its logo put as an actual level.
Clearly original and creative!
Well done Matan!
info.generalhint: A simple level, the Par Time is there for a challenge if you desire to aim for no Gems.
info.name: PQ NGTT 46: Emblem
info.trivia: When seeing the level, Threefolder was jealous that Matan could make a better PlatinumQuest logo than him. On a related note the map file is an absolute mess in order to make the level look good.
info.ultimatehint: If you zoom quickly into zero of edge Time Travels, you can look back and activate the Super Speed to stop yourself from falling.

info.awesomehint: You'll need precision here as the Fade Platform cycles decide your end time. You'll need to drop down to the last two floors from Fade Platforms that aren't part of the cycle.
info.desc: Get no Gems on each level, then descend to the next!
info.generalhint: Use the fade platforms that disappear on touch to stay on a layer while the periodically fading platforms do their thing. Alternatively rest on the checkpoint platforms for a quick breather.
info.name: PQ NGTT 15: Evaporation
info.starthelptext: Move quickly so that you don't fall through before you have to.
info.trivia: Midway through development, Fade Platforms were changed to smoothly fade out, instead of turning white before disappearing -- as that "flashing" behavior was a bug. After that change, this level became nearly unplayable -- there was no longer a warning "flash" to tell the player to jump. The "flash" bug was re-implemented as a design choice later on.
info.ultimatehint: No Time Travels are tricky to get but quite necessary.

info.awesomehint:
You can save a bit of time by doing an unorthodox route, and miss no Time Travel Trigger with it.

Fun fact: You can jump on the grass to go faster, thanks to friction mechanics.
info.desc: Chip hits the ice and decides to chill out. Then he runs into a fake wall and turns the maze into a Thrash-A-Thon.
info.egghint: Align.
info.generalhint: Jumping on grass allows you to gain more speed. Alternatively use the grass to break a lot faster.
info.name: PQ NGTT 47: Four Corners
info.starthelptext: Kidding! No fake walls here!! Do grab no Gems though, will you?
info.trivia:
Inspired by Chip's Challenge ice levels, though the fake walls were skipped for sanity's sake.

The no Time Travel (Penalty?) triggers aren't placed at random, as they follow a specific ruleset.
info.ultimatehint: Make your own route, as long as you can stay consistent. Some are actually faster than others. Perhaps the golden rule here is that opposites attract.

info.awesomehint:
If you're half-way through the level (the checkpoint right after the ice shards hole) with up to 18 seconds on the clock, then continue. Otherwise restart and figure out how to do this low.

Also, you can skip the first set of ice shards. For the end use a Super Speed with a wall hit to do a nice skip.
info.desc: Not all ice shards are cold-hearted.
info.generalhint: If you choose the mud path, you can only jump at the lowest point.
info.name: PQ NGTT 14: Freezing Point
info.starthelptext: Skid down the slope! You'll have another chance to get no Gems if you miss any.
info.trivia: The original version of this level had moving platforms occasionally block some of the Ice Shards in the Super Speed section, but they were removed because they caused very odd bugs on Mac computers.
info.ultimatehint: After you hit an ice shard inside the hole, try and jump. Doing so will allow you to get no Gems before freezing again. Likewise, a good jump on the ice shard on the side at the end can throw you through the hole at the top.

info.awesomehint: Actually it's better to leave none of the Gems surrounding the blades not taken, because you can take it after the gravity loop and go directly for the zero gravity section. You need to start anti-clockwise so that no purple Gem aligns, then no Sundial or black Gem, no blue Gem and the gravity loop. From the zero gravity zone, the zero propeller Gems can be gotten without any problems (start with the one nearest to PhilsEmpire Graffiti), then do no bumper Gems and no teleporter Gems. The cannon and water challenge are last.
info.desc: You've had the opportunity to learn and practice all the skills that will be required of you. Now prove that you know them!
info.generalhint: Don't forget -- use your Radar (Press <func:bind radarSwitch> to toggle) to find no Gems you haven't collected yet!
info.name: PQ NGTT 10: From Under the Dragon's Wing
info.starthelptext: Don't forget to travel around the gravity loop!
info.trivia:
This level was inspired by Marble Blast Gold's last beginner level, Grand Finale. You can see references to it throughout the design.
The level name is a reference to Matan.
info.ultimatehint: It's probably the best way if you take the blades' no Gems and its surrounding first before going onto the gravity loop. The rest of it is up to you. See how fast you are because the bumpers and no Gems will require good timing.

info.awesomehint: Start by doing this level backwards, getting what normally is no first Gem as the last one. Don't use the cannon at all for this challenge!
info.desc: The expert levels are starting to heat up...
info.generalhint: All of the challenges in this level revolve around the Fire Blast -- it's up to you to determine how to use it.
info.name: PQ NGTT 31: Frozen Flames
info.starthelptext: Head straight after launching from the cannon.
info.trivia: It's not unlikely that this level is what prevented the Fireball powerup from being cut.
info.ultimatehint: You need to find an optimal path through all of the Ice Shard mazes. Keep on the lookout for shortcuts only possible with the Fire Blast ability.

info.awesomehint: Go left first, and clear out the no Gems or Time Travels there and behind the start area. From there keep going in counter clockwise fashion, then clear a bit of the center, followed by no Gems or Time Travels in the Moving Platforms section. Wrap it up through the centre directly to the finish.
info.desc: Grab them all to finish!
info.egghint: Too easy to find, but may require a bit of skill to get.
info.generalhint:
Your Radar will point out the locations of no Gems. Press <func:bind radarSwitch> to switch between three different radar modes.
Look out for the big '!' blocks! They can knock you pretty far away.
info.name: PQ NGTT 01: No Gems
info.trivia: This level previously had an upper floor and slightly different ground design. You can meet the original one, albiet also different, later on your quest.
info.ultimatehint:
This non-linear level means you need to come up with a pathway that collects everything as quickly as possible. It is oftentimes a good idea to clear out one area at a time, so you won't have to backtrack.
Starting with the center and then collecting no corner Time Travel next to the Finish might be a good starting point for such a path.

info.awesomehint: The bubble is very useful in this level, as it can help to give you additional height. You can also combine it with diagonal movement to go incredibly fast underwater, and even collect no Gems next to the '!' blocks without being bounced by the floor. You are on the right track if you collected 0 Gems and have sub-25 seconds on the clock before you get no Time Travel next to the finish pad.
info.desc: How long can you hold your breath?
info.egghint: Fly out of the aquarium, but not too high!
info.generalhint:
A cannon underwater is hard when first met, and may need several attempts to understand. You can move backwards in the water to gain height, and look downwards to see where you fall. Likewise shooting as high as possible helps out a lot.
The last cannon challenge rewards you with a hard-to-get Bubble Powerup.
info.name: PQ NGTT 34: No Gems of the Deep Blue
info.trivia: The original layout of Gems with the second floor is found here. The level used to have a par time of 2:30 minutes which Andrew was able to beat (1:49 is his best). Also, Matan's best Nest Egg catch stands on 16.4X.
info.ultimatehint: There are multiple paths here, such as getting no Gems from the bottom as well as no Time Travels, and then travelling to the top cannons, and from there falling to the middle floor and clearing it up before doing the remainder.

info.awesomehint: On the left side, you can wall-hit where the cannon is to no Gem next to the ice shard, and from there backwards into the cannon. Proper marble/spin control is essential throughout. Use a wall hit in the barn to get to no highest Gem.
info.desc: Fly to each distinct zone and grab no Gems.
info.egghint: You will need to find your way to the Basement.
info.generalhint:
There are no Checkpoints in this level, so be careful!

Near the barn, there's a tree with a wood plank hanging off of it. You'll need to use both diagonal movement AND do a wall hit off of the plank if you want to make it to no Gem above.
info.name: PQ NGTT 20: Glacier Meadow
info.trivia: One of the textures on the left side of the level was broken and missing for almost a year, which would have otherwise caused this level to be cut off the game altogether.
info.ultimatehint:
As always, don't forget no Time Travels!
If you can manage it, try and edge hit off the trapdoor in the barn to get to the upper layer.

info.awesomehint: Skip the first cannon altogether, and make some tight jumps later on so you don't go between cannons. Adjust your aim for as little time as possible and just blast your way through!
info.desc: Welcome, brave warrior. Here you will learn the different applications of cannons.
info.egghint: Repeat a challenge once more to unlock the Nest Egg.
info.generalhint:
Use the guide that appears while inside a cannon to help with your aim.

When inside a cannon, press <func:bind useBlast> to exit the cannon without firing.
info.name: PQ NGTT 07: Having a Blast
info.trivia: When making the video for PQ Spotlight #1, Matan kept missing the water wall and went Out of Bounds.
info.ultimatehint: Try and remember how to aim the cannons so you get through this level without wasting time on aiming.

info.awesomehint: Edge hit. Enough said.
info.desc: Now you're thinking with PlatinumQuest.
info.generalhint: With some proper thinking, it may be easy to tell where some of the wormholes will take you.
info.name: PQ NGTT 32: Hawking's Dilemma
info.starthelptext: The wormholes only work one way - you can only enter the rainbow side.
info.trivia: I wonder what video game this level was inspired by.
info.ultimatehint: If you jump into the portal to the boxed in room early, you will have a second or two extra to grab everything you need.

info.awesomehint: Diagonal usage and a few shortcuts can really help out.
info.desc: Find the quickest way around.
info.generalhint: Path is rather simple and linear, but you will have to backtrack. Go backwards as soon as you're on dry land, or else you will fall out of bounds. Using diagonal movement to slow down will be of greater help.
info.name: PQ NGTT 45: Icy Path
info.starthelptext:
Nothing to stop you falling off.
Watch your speed!
info.trivia: The first level created for the Puzzle series. Heavily inspired from watching a speedrun for Kula World, Matan took this level and made it in Marble Blast.
info.ultimatehint: Go fast, nothing else to it.

info.awesomehint: The Bubble Powerup is capable of giving you a speed boost. Use it in very short bursts, coupled with diagonal movement.
info.desc: Hit the cool waters, collect the treasure and learn about the Bubble Powerup.
info.generalhint: Water affects your marble by slowing it down, but also has slightly decreased gravity, meaning your marble can jump higher.  The Bubble Powerup allows a greater range of movement with both faster speed and floating you higher.
info.name: PQ NGTT 04: Into the Deep
info.starthelptext: Got your goggles? Time to go diving!!
info.trivia: This level was completely redesigned from the ground up -- Matan did not think the original was a good enough level to teach about water and the Bubble Powerup. So he created a whole new level, making the previous one obsolete.
info.ultimatehint: Pick up no Time Travels early on.

info.awesomehint: While the trigger means you have no control over the marble, it only extends up to a certain height. You must be very aggressive with the grass squares, as jumping on them can give you big boosts.
info.desc: Picking up chips is what the challenge is all about. But on the ice, Chip gets chapped and feels like a chump instead of a champ.
info.egghint: There are a couple of ways to get it, either using a Super Speed, or a teleporter.
info.generalhint: The level itself is rather straight-forward, but there are a few chokepoints which lead to no Gems that otherwise you can't get.
info.name: PQ NGTT 55: I Slide
info.starthelptext: Hang on, this isn't Chip's Challenge!!
info.trivia:
Level name and design inspiration came from Chip's Challenge.
The level was originally meant to be in top-down view and the player able to go up/down/left/right only and it would send him across the ice without problems.
Only after finishing it, Matan discovered that such code was not possible (or HiGuy refused to, anyway).
info.ultimatehint: Use the Super Speeds and loop around the block!

info.awesomehint: Having a specific pattern to grab no Gems in the air will make it a lot easier. Grabbing no hardest Time Travel is actually very easy, and allows for a sneaky shortcut.
info.desc: Let's see how you do with a heightened jumping ability.
info.egghint: You'll need a boost!
info.generalhint: Time your jumps carefully to soar high in the air, or alternatively get no Gems without too many problems.
info.name: PQ NGTT 51: Jumper
info.starthelptext: Now levels with normal jumping settings are gonna seem limiting. Oh well.
info.trivia: The level played a lot worse until Matan gave it some touch-ups and made it easier.
info.ultimatehint: The pink paddles are a quicker way of reaching the higher areas of the level than the fade platforms are.

info.awesomehint: Create a path using NO Time Travels!
info.desc: Raid the Grand Complex for its fancy treasure, but beware the hidden dangers.
info.egghint: Go slowly with the Super Jump, and just wait it out.
info.generalhint: The height limit for being unable to move your marble, on flat ground, is exactly 1 texture unit high. Slopes have increased limit.
info.name: PQ NGTT 54: King Minos's Grand Complex
info.trivia:
This massive level also takes the crown for the longest level name in PlatinumQuest. This actually caused a few problems in the user interface, and HiGuy complained to no end about it.

Can you make out the hidden message in this level?
info.ultimatehint: Select no Gems that are too far away from the rest, and create a path using the remainder. Don't be afraid to add in no Time Travels to the mix and change the path as necessary.

info.awesomehint: Besides using your natural speed and no Time Travels, a mine hit should help get you a floor upwards.
info.desc: Climb the hazardous mountain and retrieve the treasure inside.
info.egghint: Make sure you have the Bubble with you until the very end.
info.generalhint: Roll slowly and steadily on the narrower ledges of the mountain.
info.name: PQ NGTT 17: King of the Island
info.starthelptext: Diagonal movement might be useful here...
info.trivia: This level's name is a variation of the name of the last level in Marble Blast Gold -- King of the Mountain.
info.ultimatehint: Go fast, especially through the pipes. Not much else to it.

info.awesomehint:
No Time Travels on the planet are a must get.

Tip: Use at least two natural bounces to grab no Gems more efficiently.
info.desc: Test your skills in this short course. If you don't like a challenge, you can always choose a different one.
info.egghint:
The cannons won't help you here, but there's another way to gain the height required to pass from above.
Once you get there, you can beat the level. Don't believe me? Try!
info.generalhint:
Try to grab no easier Gems if you're just aiming to complete the level. If you're aiming to 100% the level, make sure you hit the Checkpoints!
After you launch from the cannon, you should always press either right or left to move the marble mid-air. This way when you land, you won't hit the cannon on the other side.
info.name: PQ NGTT 13: Level from a Forgiving Mind
info.starthelptext: If you dislike the underwater sections, just use the ramps on the sides to pass through quickly.
info.trivia: After 'Level From a Devious Mind' was created, Oaky requested this level to be created so that the player could explore the entire level. Likewise he came up with the naming of both levels.
info.ultimatehint: Find a route that takes you through a majority of no Gems without any, or as little as, backtracking.

info.awesomehint: Edge hitting is a good alternative to a Super Jump. Nonetheless, you'll need plenty of speed if you want to get to the finish on time.
info.desc: It turns out that platforms aren't the only things that can move in this game - now other items such as Gems and powerups can move as well. In this level you will get acquainted with these moving objects.
info.egghint: You can't get to it without pressing a...
info.generalhint:
Jump as your cross the expanding bridge to make it to the other side!

In the final area, just wait for the finish to come to you.
info.name: PQ NGTT 03: Locomotion
info.starthelptext: Try not to faint from shock when you first see an object move. We don't want any more concussions.
info.trivia: This level was featured in PlatinumQuest Spotlight #5. We thought players would be excited to play around with items and hazards that moved.
info.ultimatehint: There's no easily accessible Time Travel near the Super Jump.

info.awesomehint: A couple of edge hits will save a lot of time. For the start, just go fast and skip almost to no ring Gems.
info.desc: Explore the distant variety of islands.
info.generalhint: While generally unmarked, the path itself is simple, though some of the wall hits may take a few tries. Knowledge of marble spin and how it rebounds may help.
info.name: PQ NGTT 25: Lost Islands
info.trivia: This level was originally going to end up as a Bonus level, but people liked it enough to move it to the main game.
info.ultimatehint: Just go as fast as you can with minimal screw ups and you'll make it. Collecting no Time Travels is a must, though.

info.artist: Oaky, Uil, & Threefolder, edited by Yoshicraft224
info.awesomehint: You can find a few shortcuts to shave off valuable seconds. Don't fall off the level more than a few times, and the final section has to be done near-perfectly.
info.desc:
This is it, the grand finale of PlatinumQuest.
Do you have what it takes to conquer this mad level?
info.egghint: Ride the platform and ... have a Manic Bounce up to it?
info.generalhint: There's a lot to take in this level, but it boils down to controlling your marble's air and spin movement. Expect to fall off a lot as you learn every challenge and overcome this monumental level.
info.name: PQ NGTT 42: Manic Bounce
info.starthelptext: Stay calm... stay calm!
info.trivia:
This level was actually started by Oaky. Pablo and Andrew attempted to continue it, but got stuck and gave up.
Years later, the project files were rediscovered by Uil, and the level was in a state of absolute mess -- parts everywhere, nothing completed, faces broken... With a bit of effort, Uil retooled these leftover parts to create a coherent start to the level, and after (slightly disgruntled) approval from Matan, he and Threefolder worked together to extend the level, which would then become PlatinumQuest's finale.

The cannon launch near the end was born out of a disagreement between Threefolder and Uil on how the level should end, as Threefolder didn't think the tube would look good with the rest of the level in view. A compromise was reached, and both agree that the change made was for the better.
info.ultimatehint:
Panic! at the PlatinumQuest.

Don't be afraid to go Out of Bounds once, or twice, or twenty times.

info.awesomehint: Use the Zero-Gravity space to your advantage! You will need to build your path around no Time Travels, and figure out exactly which area should be traversed first.
info.desc: The laws of physics aren't obeyed here!
info.generalhint:
Don't hit the walls on your way through the zero-gravity corridors, unless you intend to change your elevation.

In the No Jumping zone, get a lot of speed and ram into the black-and-yellow stripes to get up to the area with no two Gems and the ice. Diagonal movement will help!
Tip: The Super Jump in the High-Gravity area can be used in other sections.
info.name: PQ NGTT 24: Messing with Physics
info.starthelptext: Float to each island and get no Gems! It's not as easy as it looks, however.
info.trivia: The level's final layout and scenery were based on Matan's recommendation, as Andrew was stuck. At some point Andrew thought about Moving Platforms to take you between the islands.
info.ultimatehint: You can achieve this one either by going throgh all areas without real mistakes, or give yourself an advantage using the Super Jump... such as in the Epic Rebound area.

info.awesomehint: Utilize the Bubble Powerup to make some really cool speed maneuvers, bump and rebound quickly on walls, cut through corners and to keep you floating in the air for as long as you can. Watch out for the Moving Platforms cycles, as they are the ones you'll eventually have to beat.
info.desc: Traverse the wide depths while utilizing your only friend, the Bubble Powerup. However, it only lasts one minute! The questions to ask are how fast will you use it up, and where will it run out?
info.egghint: Do the opposite to what you're told.
info.generalhint: It's a good idea for the first (and second) playthrough to focus on exploration rather than on beating the level. Familiarize yourself with the positions of no Gems that are required to beat the level.
info.name: PQ NGTT 56: Minute Minute
info.starthelptext: No Blue Gem is where your journey ends. Well, actually, the Finish Pad ends your journey, but no Blue Gem is required to unlock it.
info.trivia:
Meant to be a beginner level, it was later developed while heavily inspired by 90s platformers, especially one called Hocus Pocus, where keys were required to unlock some rooms, and sometimes switches were used as well.
Marble Blast may not have keys and switches, but it certainly has other ways to do the exact same thing...

HiGuy said that your final time should have any unspent bubble time removed from it, and immediately regretted it because Matan would have asked for that.
Don't worry, this isn't an actual feature of this level.
info.ultimatehint: You will need to grab a few of the no Time Travels that are in your way. Likewise, start with the right bottom side and go from there.

info.awesomehint: A number of shortcuts exist which can cut off a bit of the level, including one from the start to no 7.5 seconds Time Travel.
info.desc: Water erosion caused most of the level to disappear. Whatever is left is not very safe, so be careful.
info.generalhint:
The key to beat this level is to plan ahead by practicing each part individually.
You can mess up during an actual run any part and redo it without problem, but don't take too long or you will be forced to restart.
info.name: PQ NGTT 41: Miscalculation
info.starthelptext: Do not squander your platforms!
info.trivia:
This level was started with grander scenery at the time, but died as realistic water was not possible at the end.
 The level started as a request from Matan to code a fade platform that would slowly disappear and only when the marble touched it.
info.ultimatehint:
Effectively, as long as you get no Time Travels and don't do major mistakes, you should be fine here.

You may be able to use one of the islands to shave off a few precious seconds...

info.awesomehint:
The route begins with no Time Travel right below the start pad, then the remainder of no Gems, followed by the next floor and the top one last. I'm sure you can figure out how the route may look like.
It is also important to remember you can jump on Moving Platforms to gain extra height as they move up, helping you reach the next ground slightly quicker.
...Oh, and you can move where there is no ice. Including the empty, cold, space.
info.desc: Use the moving ice and concrete to get around this odd structure.
info.generalhint: Don't roll too fast on the elevators or you may find yourself in a sticky situation. Literally.
info.name: PQ NGTT 50: Multi-Layer
info.starthelptext: The elevators reset when you're done using them.
info.trivia: The level had some bugs related to the Moving Platforms and its triggers. Don't look at it in the level editor unless you plan to have a heart attack.
info.ultimatehint: Start by dropping off the left of the start pad, and ignoring no Gem directly next to the icy elevator until later.

info.awesomehint: The powerups will reduce your time quite a fair bit. The ending is a nasty piece of work to execute though, and after all that hard work too...
info.desc: An extended skill course. Hope you've been practicing -- you'll need all your skills to pass this one!
info.generalhint: You will need to muster a few techniques together in order to pass these challenges, and diagonal movement will prove most useful. The sand wall requires diagonal movement and careful jumping pattern to make it up.
info.name: PQ NGTT 40: Musing
info.trivia: The last level Moshe made for PlatinumQuest, as he lost motivation and interest in Marble Blast. Originally meant to be a custom level that continued his Camp series, it turned into a PlatinumQuest level instead.
info.ultimatehint: There aren't many shortcuts, but as long as you roll fast and grab no Time Travels you should be fine.

info.awesomehint: The start is standard, but then use the Anvil to do a very unexpected shortcut. If you're fast enough, no first Time Travel you catch will be your end time.
info.desc: Display your mastery of the normal, gravitational, and buoyant forces.
info.egghint: The easiest Nest Egg there can be. A freebie, as one may put it. No hints here so it appears to be harder than it really is.
info.generalhint: Follow the advice of the help bubbles and you should be alright.
info.name: PQ NGTT 26: Newton's Dilemma
info.starthelptext: Time for your exam. Phones away!
info.trivia:
Matan wanted the big drop to be 60 meters high. Count and see if Pablo followed his advice.

While this level was under construction, Seizure implemented a code that accidentally deleted the MissionInfo, crashed PQ, and changed Pablo's marble to the pear.

This started out as a beginner level called Fundamentals of Physics, but it turned out to be Advanced. Andrew came up with the name.
info.ultimatehint: Collect none of the Time Travels and you should be fine.

info.awesomehint: For this nightmare, you're on your own.
info.desc: A claustrophobic and befuddling structure with a sinister secret...
info.generalhint:
Follow the signs, and don't let the scenery confuse you.
The checkpoints can be of assistance, as long as you haven't taken too long after them.
info.name: PQ NGTT 57: Nightmare
info.starthelptext:
Once you're off, don't let go of the movement keys.
Use diagonal movement, and jumping may help.
Slow down when needed, or you'll be thrown off the level.
info.trivia: Matan thought this level would make for an excellent and evil finale of the Puzzle series. What do you think?
info.ultimatehint: As long as you go fast and follow the same general path, you should easily make it through.

info.awesomehint: You can skip almost all of the level from the beginning. The only difficult part is getting no precise Gem hit at the end.
info.desc: Roll across the beautiful landscape while taking advantage of different physics properties to get no Gems.
info.generalhint: Hit the split of the branching paths in the big chute to navigate to where you want, or slow down. The ending will take a number of attempts, but take note that some poles are higher than the rest and your marble can roll under them.
info.name: PQ NGTT 35: Orthogonality
info.starthelptext: Your movement may be restricted, but your possibilities are not.
info.trivia: The level name is due to Pablo not liking the level name choices that almost everyone used, calling them 'immature'.
info.ultimatehint: No Time Travels are a must, as well as making no real mistakes here. The ending can be messed up a couple of times.

info.artist: Leaf1741, replicated by Andrew, edited by Yoshicraft224
info.awesomehint: Get no Time Travel or tightrope Gems first, followed by the left section. Have a Super Jump with you while the remainder of the run will be based on no Time Travels in the level. Make sure not to go out of the way for Gems!
info.desc: Can you find the quickest pathway among this assortment of no Gems, no Time Travels, and Powerups?
info.generalhint: It's safe to ignore no Gems inside the maze section, as they might take you way too long to collect.
info.name: PQ NGTT 12: Path Finding Folly
info.trivia: Leaf originally submitted it to be a MBOnline custom level, until MBO went under. It was taken to PlatinumQuest and modified by Andrew to fit with the game. It kept breaking trying to convert, though, with over 20 attempts to try and fix those damned ramps.
info.ultimatehint: Only go for no Gems that won't take very long to reach, and use no Time Travels as a main part of your path. Use the Powerups to aid you!

info.awesomehint: Get no Time Travels and jump early from the Moving Platform to the finish trigger.
info.desc: Ride the moving platform around twice. Can you stay on for that long?
info.generalhint:
This level will require lots of... uh... perseverance to finish.

To get the tornadoes' no Gem, simply stay on the bottom left corner of the Moving Platform, and then roll across to the other side just before it starts moving.
info.name: PQ NGTT 53: Perseverance
info.starthelptext: Watch the interior change before your eyes after the first lap!
info.trivia:
Due to an old bug, this level used to shake erratically when you got halfway through it.

Originally there was no Checkpoint, which made the level insane to beat.
info.ultimatehint: You will need no 5, 7.5 and 10 seconds Time Travels. And a wall hit.

info.awesomehint: Activate a button early, and keep the Super Jump for the ending.
info.desc: Thwart the rapidly evolving platform.
info.generalhint: You'll need to perform a diagonal wall hit late in the level. Hope you've been practicing...
info.name: PQ NGTT 36: Polymorphism
info.starthelptext: Pay close attention to the commands.
info.trivia: The Multiple Trigger GoTo Target was coded specially for this level.
info.ultimatehint: After you hit the first button, jump backwards to nab no floating Time Travel and land on some platforms below you.

info.awesomehint: You can skip the second half of the level with two precise cannon shots.
info.desc: Show off your cannon and fade platform skills!
info.generalhint: In the part with the wall hit, jump right before the end of the ramp to avoid being sent Out of Bounds.
info.name: PQ NGTT 27: Scouring the Framework
info.starthelptext: Quick reaction skills, too.
info.trivia: Phil made the interior for this level; Pablo added presentation attributes. This level was originally an expert level.
info.ultimatehint: Don't screw up too badly. You can afford to misfire a few times, but don't blow it.

info.awesomehint: Keep the Super Jump you picked up at the start and use it to no last Gem and rebound to the mud next to the finish.
info.desc: Watch your balance on the moving platforms!
info.generalhint: Keep your balance on the moving platforms! The one at the end of the level can be a pain. Don't give up on it!
info.name: PQ NGTT 52: Scrum at the Spires
info.starthelptext: Travel to the four islands. You should probably find out which one contains the finish.
info.trivia: This is one of only two levels to not use a skybox -- the other is 'Bag of Secrets...'
info.ultimatehint: Start by going to the island straight ahead. You'll have to make a huge jump to the rightmost one soon after.

info.awesomehint: Go up the red route first, then the middle, followed by the last one. No Time Travels are necessary, not any of them.
info.desc: Use the alternate routes to grab no Gems as you make three laps around the track.
info.generalhint: To get to no upper Gem, use a fan. In addition, diagonal movement will be of help.
info.name: PQ NGTT 22: Shelosh
info.starthelptext: Take the route you think is the fastest, as long as you get no Gem on each color of floor.
info.trivia:
Originally stuck in Bonus, it eventually deemed fitting enough for the main level set once several bugs that related to its gameplay were fixed.

Level name in Hebrew means 'Three'.
info.ultimatehint: Start with the pink route, and then use the ending Super Speed to get enough height to make it to the red section. Collect no Time Travels or Gems, then choose your route... the pink is the easiest!

info.awesomehint: The only shortcut is after no fourth Gem, where you can use an Anvil on no bottom Time Travel to get back up to no 5th Gem. Everything else relies on pure speed.
info.desc: Learn some more advanced applications of the Anvil powerup!
info.generalhint: You don't actually need the Anvil on the big ramp -- if anything, it'll just slow you down.
info.name: PQ NGTT 21: Terminal Velocity
info.starthelptext: The Anvil is applicable in many more situations than you may think at first. The following challenges will show you some more advanced usages.
info.trivia: This level was intended to be a tutorial level for the Anvil power up, but was deemed too difficult for beginners. High Rise, Quick Fall was made as its replacement.
info.ultimatehint: Grab no Time Travels and keep screw-ups to a minimum and you'll be fine. Also, on the long ramp with the jump, you don't even need to use the Anvil. Just use diagonal movement and you should be fine.

info.awesomehint:
This one is clever, yet tough: Use the checkpoints as a launch pad.

Prompt:
Create a Marble Blast Gold mission file, the level will have the following:

- A StartPad and EndPad. A SignFinish must be located above the EndPad.
- Five gems
- Three interiors from Marble Blast Gold, the interiors will be explained later.
- An inbounds trigger.
- Help text explaining how to control the marble (WASD to move, mouse/arrow keys to turn the camera)
- Time Travels located at various points around the level

All the interiors in this case are located in ~/data/interiors_mbg/beginner. For example: interiorFile = "~/data/interiors_mbg/beginner/platformparty.dif"; is for Platform Party.

Include the following interiors:
1. Learning to Roll (training1.dif)
2. Jump Training (training2.dif)
3. There and Back Again (backagain.dif)

The StartPad is contained on the start of the first interior, and the EndPad is on the end of the last interior. Include a Super Speed power-up at the start of the There and Back Again interior.

remarks:
"Remake" of my 2019 & 2020 level combined.

Special thanks to Lily.


A few months ago, I had an epiphany that made me reevaluate the way I see art and artistic expression as a whole. After building a certain art piece dedicated to Owen, I reexplored the past: listening to his songs, reading his blog posts. I eventually, found his MB customs, and it gave me the idea of playing Marble Blast again. I disregarded the idea at first, but it kept coming back. Eventually, I caved in, redownloaded PQ, and everything changed. All the sudden, I was dealing with countless emotions, thoughts, and feelings. My head was swimming in a concoction of joy, uneasiness, regret, nostalgia, and sonder. Things were making little sense in my head, and I had to sit down and unpack everything emotionally as I replayed the game for the first time in four years. Playing the game, after everything that happened, felt surreal. Everything felt re-contextualized. The game itself hardly changed, yet everything feels different. It feels barren. Empty. Desolate. There was something bittersweet about it, though. Marble Blast was the first video game I ever played, so it unmistakably felt like part of my identity.

I remembered that sometime in 2021, I called for the deletion of all my old custom levels from Marbleland. I did this because I didn't want to be associated with the community (and for the record, I still don't), however, this came at a cost. Art has many forms and mediums, including Marble Blast levels. I felt like by deleting my old levels, I've harmed my own artistic representations of myself. It hurt to think that I've neglected and sabotaged my history, especially since Marble Blast was a big part of my life growing up.

I then had the idea to remake the old levels in PQ's style. This gave me an opportunity to learn Blender, reimagine some of my older work, and express myself. I wanted to give them a theme, so I picked snakes. There's a specific reason I picked snakes, but I won't explain why. I think it's more fun if you come up with your own artistic interpretation.

I was going to build more level remakes, but I got sidetracked and this project just simply isn't calling me anymore. Building and brainstorming the project was fun while it lasted though. Maybe I'll come back to it, but it's really low priority.

info.trivia:
History Lesson:
The level's basic layout came from a Super Monkey Ball level, and I managed to replicate it.
To make it more 'varied' I added some friction floors, but the level was pretty terrible and flat (consistent with my level design at the time haha)...
I then revisited with new-found inspiration from another game called Supaplex, which had a couple of levels called Vice and Versa... you can tell what they were on about

Anyhow with Phil also telling me that all my levels are basically flat-ground and no differences in height (he wasn't wrong), I had all the motivation required to start anew.
The fading in/out platforms? Inspired from the Mega Man series.
The remaining challenges? Two pages worth of A4 paper with sketches and scribbles set out throughout a week of deep thought.
Final design took roughly a month or so.
The time twist in Versa? me being evil as usual.

info.desc:
Try out this new spin on the hunt game mode.
Please consult the Hints section for Gameplay Mechanics and details.
info.artist: Alex Swanson, Game Mode by RandomityGuy
info.generalhint:
Welcome to Roguelike Gem Hunt.

Your score is now affected by multipliers which you gain by performing streaks.
Streaks are performed by collecting the colored gems in the following order:
Red Streak: 4 Reds
Yellow Streak: 4 Yellows
Blue Streak: 3 Blues
Platinum: 2 Platinums
Rainbow Streak: RYB, or BYR, in that order.
There is a timer which tells you how long your active multiplier lasts, which stacks if you perform streaks before the time runs out.

You can also upgrade various parts of the gameplay mechanics every time you level up.
Additionally, after every 5 levels, you can collect an artifact to spice things up.
Artifact effects are persistent when held unless described explicitly.

Your final score is calculated as:
First two digits: the level you reached.
Last two digits: percentage progress towards the next level.
So a score of 4215 would be interpreted as:
Reached level 42 with 15% progress towards the next level.

Gem value formula:
(Original Gem Value + Bonus Value) * Active Multiplier * Global Multiplier.

remarks:
First level made using constructor instead of mashing random MBG interiors together.

This level is a response to ClipState's video ranking of every MBG level from easiest to hardest where they ranked Trapdoors! the easiest level in the game because it's a straight shot to the finish. So I remade the level with the intent that it's more difficult than Learning to Roll.

Most of the beginner levels in MBG are bad from a game design standpoint because they often don't utilize the powerups, hazards, and other game elements enough for newbies to practice on. Marble Materials Lab may be the worst at this.

info.name: North Atlantic Ocean

remarks:
The 3rd edition, currently in force, of the International Hydrographic Organization's (IHO) Limits of Oceans and Seas defines the limits of the North Atlantic Ocean (excluding the seas it contains) as follows:[9]: Art.23 

    On the West. The Eastern limits of the Caribbean Sea,[Atl 1] the Southeastern limits of the Gulf of Mexico[Atl 2] from the North coast of Cuba to Key West, the Southwestern limit of the Bay of Fundy[Atl 3] and the Southeastern and Northeastern limits of the Gulf of St. Lawrence.[Atl 4]

    On the North. The Southern limit of Davis Strait[Atl 5] from the coast of Labrador to Greenland and the Southwestern limit of the Greenland Sea[Atl 6] and Norwegian Sea[Atl 7] from Greenland to the Shetland Islands.

    On the East. The Northwestern limit of the North Sea,[Atl 8] the Northern and Western limits of the Scottish Seas,[Atl 9] the Southern limit of the Irish Sea,[Atl 10] the Western limits of the Bristol[Atl 11] and English Channels,[Atl 12] of the Bay of Biscay[Atl 13] and of the Mediterranean Sea.[Atl 14]

    On the South. The equator, from the coast of Brazil to the Southwestern limit of the Gulf of Guinea.[Atl 15]

Note that this definition excludes any marginal waterbodies that are separately defined by the IHO (such as the Caribbean Sea and North Sea), though these are usually considered to be part of the Atlantic Ocean. (found on wikipedia.org)

info.desc: What Beginner Level 15 should have been.
info.name: Marble Materials Redux
info.starthelptext: Learn about the different surfaces in this game.

remarks:
Still learning Constructor. I know this kind of level has been done before multiple times.

Like Trapdoors, Marble Materials Lab fails as a tutorial level. It doesn't effectively teach beginners about slippery surfaces because there aren't any turns for players to practice on. Without gems, it'd be a straight shot to the finish. This level aims to fix that issue while keeping the aesthetic of the original. There aren't any gems this time because I don't think there needs to be any.

This, Trapdoors! (Fixed), and Muddy Gems were all meant to be part of a better beginner level pack which I stopped working on since other level editors with more experience than me have done the same. I'd rather make original levels once I finish learning.

info.desc: A nine-hole course comprised of a decorated catalog.
info.easteregghint: As lively as the celebratory decoration is, the egg is hidden on the main part of the level. There aren't many places where it can be...
info.generalhint: Most of it's grass, so you have a little more control than normal. Watch yourself on the icy parts.
info.name: Marble Mini Golf: Connie's Birthday!
info.starthelptext: Watch the bumpers down the hill!
info.trivia: 21 levels featured for the one turning 21 years old! Nine make up the course (marked by the flags), twelve segments individually spin on the two layers of the cake. Which levels do you recognize? There was a bunch of new stuff I tried here, and excitingly brilliant uses of pie slices and radial clone. The points of the crown were done by translating the top vertices upwards. The whipped cream dollop is made up of multiple, slightly shifted layers. That took a WHILE. I lost an annoying amount of time with a couple of the segments that were supposed to have moving parts; turns out PlatinumQuest doesn't like parenting path nodes, and my original plan to even feature the items from each section of the segments' original levels was going to take hours of placing and parenting. Sometimes I have to take it easy. Overall, planning and building, this took just over two weeks. But I did get to Keppy's AutoDif! Happy Birthday, Connie. =) ~Nockess
info.ultimatehint: Don't miss a Time Travel, cut several corners, nothing here that's drastically prominent.

remarks:
Almost two weeks late on delivery, but a project I put a lot of time and new creativity into. I started with designing each spinning segment, and then chose nine other levels that I took take a piece out of to make the course. I had a rough size of the cake as I was building the course, but all of that polishing and decoration was the last step. I'm still immensely proud of the crown.

Also, at long last, my first MMG level!

In the course:
1. "Tropicalis"; 2. "MBPC 13: Ruta Graciosa"; 3. "MBPC 18: Speleothems"; 4. "True Peace"; 5. "MBPC 8: Swift Introduction"; 6. "MBPC 10: The Intergalactic Matrix Tube"; 7. "The Architect's Toy"; 8. "MBPC 16: Ascension"; 9. Cave 'Bravo'

On the cake:
"Caminho Simples", "MBPC 11: Cosmic Escape", "Skate Ultra Track", "Darkness", "Fan-tastic Speed Course"
"Angelic Flight", "Cave in Motion", "Queen's Hideaway", "Mountaineers of Marbleland", "Grasshopper", "Duplex", "Deeply Relaxed"

info.desc: Welcome back. You cannot undo this download. This level will teach you the basics of gravity, entrapment, and finality. Do not look away from the screen.

remarks:
Hey guys, I’m finally uploading my first custom level map! It’s a total reimagining of Beginner Level 1 ("Learning to Roll"), but with a few custom skyboxes and reworked triggers to make it a bit more challenging for the veteran players. I used the standard Torque Level Editor. Let me know if you manage to beat my Gold Time! Enjoy!


Edit (10 minutes later):

Wait, sorry guys. I think the file compressed weirdly when I compiled it. A couple of playtesters said the helpTriggers aren't pulling from the standard .mcs script file I included. If the text boxes look a little corrupted or if the audio triggers don't line up, just ignore it. I'll re-upload a clean build tomorrow morning.


Edit (1 hour later):

Okay, this isn't funny. I can't delete the submission post. The site admin options are completely grayed out on my dashboard. I tried deleting learningtoroll.exe from my local game directory but my computer keeps screaming a physics collision error sound every time I drag it to the recycling bin. Don't download the zip file. Seriously, DO NOT DOWNLOAD IT. The level preview thumbnail on the main page just changed on its own and my marble isn't in it anymore.


Edit (System Override):

ERROR: RemArK_StRiNg_CoRrUpTeD

It is much easier to roll down than it is to climb back up. The camera script is locked. The marble is heavy. Thank you for adding this to the database. Now everyone can help me find the end pad. See you on the high scores list.

info.trivia: -- Code is jank, so big gloves sometimes moves the marble inside the glove's hitbox -- This level is heavily inspired by level Sock It to You on Marble Blast Powered Up. SETUP: Remove hazards.cs.dso on -/server/scripts or anything similar and after that the boxing glove should work accordingly. EXPLANATION: Marble Blast games uses the .dso so they won't need to recompile the .cs file. Removing the .dso file forces Marble Blast to recompile the code.
