remarks:
Original upload date: June 5 2021 (on the Steam Workshop)

This is not a 1:1 remake. There are some slight differences including platform alignment. I might be slightly off on some platforms but I tried the best I could. Individual levels will be coming soon hopefully

info.awesomehint:
In addition to the wall-hits and edge-hits used in almost all Awesome Time runs, you can use the Shock Absorber-like properties of Cloud Blocks in various ways to pull off some crazy moves. Speaking of crazy moves there are some more shortcuts that are worth noting: In the section with rainbow bridges forming a + shape, if you roll towards the doors as fast as possible without jumping, you can actually get enough height to just leap over the gates without opening them. Some particularly placed decorative pillars may come in handy in saving time too.

These hints are really crucial for this Awesome Time, as <spush><color:F4900C>Stormson<spop> playtested the level a lot of times to determine the Awesome Time for the level.
info.desc: Many things were terrifying at night and became a laughing matter when daylight came.
info.egghint:
See the hatch near the first cannon? One of the balconies has something blue. Touch it, and I hope you can figure out the rest.

Oh, and just one more hint... the Super Jump PowerUp can potentially be used to reach otherwise inaccessible balconies. There may be something hidden on one of those balconies...
info.generalhint: Cloud Blocks split into 8 smaller pieces when touched, and those pieces can be vaporized by touching them again. Each Cloud Block takes 10 seconds to respawn regardless of how many pieces are remaining.
info.name: Stormson's Sky Stronghold
info.starthelptext: Touch Cloud Blocks to split them!
info.trivia:
This level was heavily inspired by the Tower of Babel section in a past Steam game called "Only Up!", which was infamous for the trap that could send the player all the way back to the very beginning of the game. The cloud blocks were inspired by the ghost blocks found in "Haunted Hogs" episode of Angry Birds Seasons. Shout-out to freesound_community and DavidDumaisAudio for the switch sound effect, I took a long time deciding the sounds for the switches in the level.

Last but not least, as the level's title says, this sky stronghold is proudly dedicated to <spush><color:F4900C>Stormson<spop>, who playtested the level and even shared the play screen with me a lot of times!!<color:F4900C> Mrrp mrrow :3
info.ultimatehint: Once you enter the castle, the biggest shortcut in this level awaits: Hitting a slope precisely, you can propel yourself to the central room, entirely skipping the challenges of the castle first floor! Such a <spush><color:F4900C>Cleossally Stormtacular<spop> way to eat a large amount of time off of the clock. As always, don't forget about the <spush><color:F4900C>Mocha<spop>-Sundials for calming the timer down, like how <spush><color:F4900C>Stormson<spop> calms down <spush><color:F4900C>Tabby<spop>.

remarks: My 24th level. Fixed the normal/spec map dependencies.

dependencies: sound/music/Jump High, Jump Far, Jump All the Way!.ogg

info.awesomehint: The so-called "Angry Swipers", despite looking angry, can be even more useful than the wheels in Verticality. They may be more "kind" than just "angry" - they can allow you to save literally DOZENS of seconds!
info.desc: ...in this absolutely-frozen galaxy of various trials and tribulations! Can you overcome them all and get to the Completion Star?
info.egghint: The red dots surely look suspicious...
info.generalhint:
In this level, the colored arrow signs (except for the bright solid red ones) will guide you to the button of the same color. When in doubt, look for such arrow signs, as they are really helpful clues for you to examine!

Additionally, the snow in this level is four times as frictional as regular floors, and can also absorb a lot of bounce. Keep that in mind whenever you climb up or slide down a steep slope.
info.music: Jump High, Jump Far, Jump All the Way!.ogg
info.name: Throttling the Thrust...
info.starthelptext: The bright cyan liquid is exceptionally freezing. Seriously don't touch it, or you'll get frostburned!
info.trivia:
Notice the shapes of the interiors forming the terrain of the level? Yes, they are interiors created using Blender. This level is in fact my first level with Blender interiors. Shoutout to RandomityGuy for the IO DIF plugin - Without it, I would've suffered from writing all of those zeroes and ones myself!

Also, this is my first level that I have uploaded via my new computer bought in 2025. My older computer is nowadays too old to use.
info.ultimatehint: The ropes with colorful lights? Even they may be "tight", they indeed do have more reasons to exist than just decorative purposes. The gift boxes with rockets? Despite that they use naughty coal lumps for fuel, their powerful thrusters may let you skip quite a lot of areas... if you're good at loop exits. There can be even more shortcuts to find, and such shortcuts are vital for Ultimate Times like this one!

remarks: My 25th level. Fixed the arrow signs and normal/spec dependencies

info.awesomehint: It turned out that SummerArmy has seen varieties of shortcuts and skips while watching Stormson playtesting this level! Way too many to list them all, but want to know just one more trick for reaching the beloved finish pad sooner? In the section where you have to survive on the two flipping platforms while waiting for the touchstone to arrive, you can actually get a running start and do some precise parkour to reach the other side, skipping the survival challenge! It's such a tough trick to pull off, isn't it? Writing this hint and the Ultimate Hint was also a tough job for SummerArmy.
info.desc: Geurae. Nado yeogie onji beolsseo samnyeoni neomeosseo. Geureochiman i ginagin yeojeongdo ajik seomagil ppuniya. Apeurodo uriwa hamkke naaganeun geoya! Keomyuniti Hoewondeul Saranghae!
info.egghint: The symbols on a few of the floor tiles seem suspicious... maybe they are related to the cake?
info.generalhint: Most touchstones simply move along basic straight paths, but some others may have non-linear, irregular paths. Pay attention to the floor tiles with star icons as they mark the paths the touchstones travel!
info.name: Eonjerado Gomawo!
info.starthelptext: Jump on the touchstone to make it move!
info.trivia:
This level is for celebrating the third anniversary of SummerArmy joining the Marble Blast Community, hinted by the birthday party-like scenery, the cake in front of the giant SummerArmy statue, and the references to his older levels.

The overall design of this level was inspired by the Ultimate IV stage from Hamsterball PS3, and the touchstones were inspired by the touchstones from the level Puffprod Peaks from Super Mario 3D World.

Fun fact: There are 208 dependency inclusion lines in the .mis file for the level, significantly more than any of my other levels (39 in "Stormson's Sky Stronghold" and 61 in "Throttling the Thrust..."). Hope my future levels don't have more.
info.ultimatehint: The rainbow slide can give your marble more velocity than you think. Just slide diagonally to the left with sufficient momentum, precisely hop off of a touchstone, then hit an ice shard so that you stick the landing, and voila! This really shaves off a good amount of time. Don't forget about the Time Travels scattered around the level too.

remarks: My 26th level. Fixed the normal/spec dependencies and added the missing sound effect to the jump pads

info.awesomehint: Speaking of the "loop" made of neon platforms, you can actually use it in conjunction with two Super Speeds to propel your marble all the way up to the finish trigger above the level! Such an astronomical shortcut requires extremely precise timing, but it exists. In fact, SummerArmy actually didn't know that this shortcut really existed when he was watching Stormson's playtesting screenshare.
info.desc: RandomityGuy was going to release the BSP fix for his Blender io_dif plugin. He was tired, so he decided to sleep beforehand. but as soon as he fell asleep, his nightmares decided to trap him, preventing him from getting up again, unless he somehow escapes from his nightmarish dimension. At least this one is somewhat radiant and pleasant, with all of those tall buildings and skyscrapers, equipped with bright neon lights illuminating the skyline. Your job is to find him sleeping in one of many beds and then wake him up... in this glowing city!
info.egghint: Try to find where RandomityGuy is sleeping... and the satellite dishes can also be a good clue for you...
info.generalhint: Some neon platforms not only must be used to advance further in the level, but also can get in your way when it's visible, making them effectively double-edged swords... or maybe double-faced platforms? Anyways, anticipating the way the platforms fade in and out helps a lot in such sections.
info.name: RandomityGuy's REM Radiance
info.starthelptext: Does this landscape remind you of the Soggy Town?
info.trivia:
This level's general aesthetics was mainly inspired by the first part of "High Life", a Geometry Dash level, and "Night Puzzle III", a Hustle level in Hamsterball PS3. The ending of this level is also a shoutout to the ending in SummerArmy's seventh level, "Navigating the tSohggVGo6Y Town", with the same way the Finish Trigger works here and there.

Fun fact: The Bounds trigger was the LAST object ever added to this level's .mis file! Good thing SummerArmy didn't forget to put it before uploading his hard work online.
info.ultimatehint: There are only five Time Travels in the entire level, so it's much better to rely on shortcuts and analyzing the neon platforms' cycles. The Super Speed just before the "loop" made of neon platforms can also be saved up and therefore be used in various ways, so try to be more creative!

remarks: My 27th level. Fixed the normal/spec maps

info.awesomehint: Have you considered skipping the pink flower switch too?
info.desc: After discovering that RandomityGuy had been whisked into a different realm of his nightmare, you were forced to flee the high-life metropolis via a levitation beacon. You soon found yourself in a purple, romantic-looking forest dimension, teeming with strange trees and floral life. Until the mechanics of the spatial rifts are understood, it remains a mystery how you arrived in the heart of this cosmic forest--and whether RandomityGuy is truly trapped within its depths.
info.egghint: Like in Pathfinding Ingenuity, this Nest Egg (don't confuse it with the striped eggs) is easy to spot, yet hard to actually reach. So... have you explored more of the trees around you?
info.generalhint:
Stay nimble! You'll need quick reflexes to navigate these moving platforms. And a word of warning: a few of those cosmic flowers might remind you of the bumpers and duct fans from Marble Blast. Don't let them catch you off guard--or better yet, use them to your advantage whenever the situation allows.

Tip: After hitting the moving target halfway through the level, you might as well find a cool shortcut with ease. It will be important for beating challenge times such as the Platinum Time, so keep it in mind!
info.name: Jadonghwa Jungle
info.starthelptext: Does this gauntlet feel familiar to you?
info.trivia:
Originally, this level had a realistic, orange, autumn-like atmosphere. However, to better complement its purple flowers, it was changed to a purple, cosmic fantasy theme. Back then, those flowers even had green stems instead of the current purple ones.

This is also my first level to use some of the free PBR textures from ambientCG. Specifically, Ground095A, Ground079L, Grass001, Grass008, WoodFloor051, Wood058, and Bark014 have been used.
info.ultimatehint: Time Travels in this level have different colors depending on the time bonuses they give. The darker the shade of purple, the longer the time bonus. Nonetheless, finding the right cycles of the moving platforms is crucial for planning the route. Seriously, don't forget that aforementioned shortcut!
